l4_steps.output: Systemic issue flags (e.g. route-level catering failure, recurring IFE outage) with owning department assignment
l4_steps.kpi: Systemic issues identified within 48 hours of NPS batch; ≥ 80% of flags routed to correct owning department
l4_steps.pain_point: Cross-functional escalation path for systemic NPS drivers (e.g. catering contracted to LSG Sky Chefs, IFE operated by Panasonic Avionics) lacks SLA enforcement; owning department may dispute root cause assignment without corroborating ops data

l4_steps.name: Generate NPS insight report for leadership
l4_steps.input: Aggregated NPS scores, segment data, systemic flags, and verbatim themes
l4_steps.output: Weekly NPS insight report: route heatmap, driver waterfall, trend vs. prior period
l4_steps.kpi: Report published by Monday 08:00 local time for prior week's flights; ≥ 95% data completeness
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual Tableau report assembly from multiple AWS Redshift views causes inconsistent metric definitions across business units; finance uses different on-time threshold (D15) vs. CX team (D0), creating conflicting NPS driver narratives

l4_steps.name: Prioritise detractor outreach by severity tier
l4_steps.input: Detractor case queue from Salesforce Service Cloud prioritised by NPS score and LTV flag
l4_steps.output: Prioritised outreach list: Tier 1 (NPS 0–3, high-value loyalty member), Tier 2 (NPS 4–6)
l4_steps.kpi: Tier 1 first contact attempt within 24 hours; Tier 2 within 72 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Salesforce Service Cloud LTV flag relies on Amadeus Altéa loyalty tier sync; sync runs nightly so recently tier-upgraded passengers are misclassified as standard for up to 24 hours, delaying priority recovery for high-value detractors

l4_steps.name: Execute personalised recovery — miles or voucher
l4_steps.input: Detractor case with verified passenger loyalty profile and verbatim complaint theme
l4_steps.output: Recovery action logged: goodwill miles credited via Altéa loyalty API or travel voucher issued
l4_steps.kpi: Recovery offer acceptance rate ≥ 65%; average goodwill cost per case ≤ $35 equivalent
l4_steps.pain_point: Goodwill miles crediting via Altéa loyalty API requires PNR match; passengers who booked via OTA without loyalty number attached cannot receive miles recovery without manual agent intervention, increasing handle time by 12–15 minutes per case

l4_steps.name: Confirm recovery satisfaction and close case
l4_steps.input: Recovery action confirmation and passenger acknowledgement
l4_steps.output: Case closed with recovery outcome tag; re-survey flag set if unresolved
l4_steps.kpi: Case resolution rate ≥ 80% within 7 days; re-escalation rate ≤ 5%
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated post-recovery satisfaction check; agents manually follow up by phone or email with no structured close-loop survey, making it impossible to measure whether recovery actions actually reversed detractor sentiment

l4_steps.name: Publish NPS dashboard to operational stakeholders
l4_steps.input: Aggregated NPS scores, driver analysis, recovery metrics from AWS Redshift
l4_steps.output: Live Tableau dashboard: route NPS heatmap, weekly trend, detractor volume, recovery SLA status
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard refresh latency ≤ 4 hours; ≥ 200 active monthly dashboard users across CX, Ops, and Commercial
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau Server licence costs scale with named users; CX team frequently requests ad-hoc access for seasonal staff or agency partners which requires IT procurement cycle of 5–10 business days, delaying insight access during high-disruption periods

l4_steps.name: Update CX improvement backlog with NPS-driven initiatives
l4_steps.input: Systemic failure flags, driver waterfall, and benchmarked NPS gap vs. target
l4_steps.output: Prioritised improvement backlog items linked to specific NPS driver themes and owning teams
l4_steps.kpi: ≥ 3 backlog items added per monthly NPS review cycle; ≥ 60% of prior-cycle items in active delivery
l4_steps.pain_point: NPS-driven improvement initiatives require cross-functional commitment from Ops, IT, and Commercial; without formal governance linking NPS driver escalation to change request prioritisation, improvement backlog items stall at department boundaries

l4_steps.name: Capture SSR from booking or service channel
l4_steps.input: Customer request via call centre, web booking, airport counter, or travel agent GDS
l4_steps.output: Raw SSR record attached to PNR
l4_steps.kpi: SSR capture rate ≥98% of requests received across all channels
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC channel requests may not automatically propagate IATA SSR codes into Altéa PSS, requiring manual re-entry and creating duplication risk

l4_steps.name: Classify SSR using IATA ADRM standard codes
l4_steps.input: Raw SSR record and IATA ADRM SSR code library
l4_steps.output: Standardised IATA SSR code assigned (e.g. WCHR, WCHS, WCHC, UMNR, MEDA, STCR, BLND, DEAF, BSCT, VGML, EXST)
l4_steps.kpi: SSR miscoding rate <0.5% of all SSRs entered
l4_steps.pain_point: Agents conflate WCHR (ramp wheelchair) with WCHC (cabin wheelchair), causing resource over/under-provision at the gate

l4_steps.name: Validate SSR code against passenger record
l4_steps.input: SSR code, PNR, flight itinerary, passenger age and loyalty tier
l4_steps.output: Validated SSR record or validation-fail alert
l4_steps.kpi: Validation completion within 4 hours of SSR capture for standard requests; <1 hour for MEDA cases
l4_steps.pain_point: UMNR age validation relies on data-entry accuracy — no automated DOB check against passport data until check-in APIS processing

l4_steps.name: Check aircraft equipment compatibility for SSR
l4_steps.input: Validated SSR code, assigned aircraft type, cabin configuration
l4_steps.output: Equipment compatibility decision (e.g. STCR requires aft bulkhead row; BSCT requires bassinet-mount rows)
l4_steps.kpi: Equipment conflict detection rate 100% prior to SSR confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: Last-minute aircraft swaps (e.g. gauge change from 737-800 to 737-700) invalidate pre-assigned STCR/BSCT seats with no automated re-trigger of SSR review

l4_steps.name: Assess ground handling resource requirements
l4_steps.input: SSR code, flight schedule, station staffing roster
l4_steps.output: Resource allocation plan (wheelchair, ambulift, escort staff, medical oxygen)
l4_steps.kpi: Resource pre-positioning completed ≥2 hours before scheduled departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Third-party ground handler contracts at outstations often exclude specialised WCHC lift-on/lift-off equipment, requiring airline-owned asset repositioning at cost

l4_steps.name: Verify regulatory and safety compliance for SSR
l4_steps.input: SSR type, MEDA form, DOT 14 CFR Part 382 requirements, IATA Medical Manual
l4_steps.output: Compliance clearance or MEDA medical clearance request issued to CMO
l4_steps.kpi: MEDA clearance turnaround <6 hours for standard medical cases; 100% DOT Part 382 compliance audit pass rate
l4_steps.pain_point: MEDA cases require Chief Medical Officer sign-off but CMO availability outside business hours causes SSR holds and flight-day escalations

l4_steps.name: Confirm SSR and update PNR in Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Feasibility approval, compliance clearance, resource plan
l4_steps.output: Confirmed SSR element in PNR with free-text OSI remarks for crew
l4_steps.kpi: PNR update latency <30 minutes from approval; SSR visible in all downstream systems within 1 hour
l4_steps.pain_point: OSI remark field character limit (64 chars) forces abbreviation of complex medical notes, leading to misinterpretation by cabin crew at boarding

l4_steps.name: Broadcast SSR notification to all handling stations
l4_steps.input: Confirmed SSR elements from PNR, flight leg routing
l4_steps.output: Station-specific SSR notification delivered to each departure and transit station
l4_steps.kpi: Notification delivery confirmation rate ≥99.5%; transit station SSR awareness rate ≥97%
l4_steps.pain_point: Interline/codeshare segments handled by operating carrier may not receive SSR notifications via SITA AMS if operating carrier uses a non-Altéa PSS — manual telex fallback required

l4_steps.name: Send SSR confirmation to passenger
l4_steps.input: Confirmed SSR details, contact preferences from loyalty profile
l4_steps.output: Confirmation email or SMS to passenger with SSR summary and pre-travel instructions
l4_steps.kpi: Passenger confirmation sent ≥24 hours before departure for pre-booked SSRs; <2 hours for same-day airport requests
l4_steps.pain_point: Salesforce CRM and Altéa PSS use separate customer identifiers — real-time SSR status sync requires middleware (API layer) that has a known 15-minute polling lag

l4_steps.name: Generate SSR pre-departure briefing sheet for crew
l4_steps.input: Confirmed SSR list for flight, crew assignment roster
l4_steps.output: Passenger Special Needs Brief (PSNB) attached to flight pack
l4_steps.kpi: PSNB delivery to crew ≥60 minutes before departure; crew acknowledgement rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Late SSR additions (<2 hours before departure) do not always trigger PSNB update in Jeppesen — crew may operate on stale briefing data

l4_steps.name: Pre-position special equipment at departure gate
l4_steps.input: Resource allocation plan, SSR type, gate assignment
l4_steps.output: Equipment confirmed at gate (ambulift, wheelchair, STCR board, medical oxygen kit)
l4_steps.kpi: Equipment pre-positioned ≥45 minutes before boarding; zero gate-delay incidents attributable to missing SSR equipment
l4_steps.pain_point: Ambulift availability is shared across multiple gates at hub airports — competing WCHC requests on peak departure banks cause queuing and boarding delays

l4_steps.name: Review and protect SSR passenger seat assignment
l4_steps.input: SSR code, current seat map, aircraft equipment type
l4_steps.output: Protected seat assignment with SESL (Seat Especial Service Lock) flag; adjacent seats blocked where required
l4_steps.kpi: SSR seat protection applied ≥12 hours before departure; zero involuntary seat moves for SSR passengers
l4_steps.pain_point: Upgrade clearance processes (Tier status upgrades) can inadvertently re-assign SSR-protected rows if the upgrade algorithm does not read SESL flags correctly

l4_steps.name: Verify SSR at check-in and issue special boarding pass
l4_steps.input: Passenger identity document, PNR with SSR elements, APIS data
l4_steps.output: Verified SSR, special boarding pass (e.g. pre-board marker), updated APIS manifest
l4_steps.kpi: SSR verification completion rate 100% at check-in; check-in processing time for WCHC/MEDA ≤8 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: APIS/ICTS name matching failures for passengers with SSR who also have name correction remarks cause check-in holds and require supervisor override

l4_steps.name: Coordinate pre-board assistance and boarding sequence
l4_steps.input: SSR passenger list, boarding gate assignments, special boarding pass flags
l4_steps.output: Pre-board completion confirmation; SSR passengers boarded and seated before general boarding
l4_steps.kpi: Pre-board completion ≥10 minutes before general boarding start; zero SSR passenger miss-boards
l4_steps.pain_point: Congested gate areas at hub turnaround stations make wheelchair manoeuvring hazardous; lack of dedicated SSR queuing lanes creates safety and delay incidents

l4_steps.name: Execute cabin crew SSR handoff at aircraft door
l4_steps.input: PSNB, boarding confirmation, SSR passenger seat locations
l4_steps.output: Cabin crew SSR acknowledgement; in-flight service adaptations confirmed (e.g. meal, oxygen, PA announcements for BLND/DEAF)
l4_steps.kpi: SSR handoff completed before aircraft door closure; cabin crew SSR briefing acknowledgement 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: High crew-to-SSR passenger ratios on wide-body or full narrow-body flights limit the attention available for complex MEDA or STCR cases during turbulence events

l4_steps.name: Record SSR fulfillment outcome post-arrival
l4_steps.role: Airport Customer Service Agent / Gate Agent
l4_steps.input: SSR completion status, any in-flight deviation notes from cabin crew
l4_steps.output: SSR fulfillment record with outcome code (Fulfilled / Partial / Failed) logged against PNR and customer profile
l4_steps.kpi: Post-flight SSR outcome recorded within 4 hours of block-in; SSR data completeness ≥95%
l4_steps.pain_point: No structured digital handoff mechanism between cabin crew and ground at arrival — fulfillment gaps are captured verbally or not at all, degrading SSR performance data quality

l4_steps.name: Trigger complaint or recovery action for failed SSR
l4_steps.input: SSR failure outcome record, passenger contact details, DOT Part 382 breach indicator
l4_steps.output: Proactive customer apology communication, compensation offer, and DOT incident report if applicable
l4_steps.kpi: Proactive recovery contact within 24 hours of SSR failure; DOT Part 382 incidents reported within 10 days per regulatory requirement
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual identification of DOT-reportable SSR failures relies on agent judgement — no automated flag in Salesforce CRM triggers the mandatory DOT disability complaint reporting workflow

l4_steps.name: Analyse SSR performance and update service standards
l4_steps.input: SSR fulfillment records, DOT complaint data, NPS verbatims tagged to SSR journeys
l4_steps.output: Monthly SSR performance dashboard; process improvement recommendations; updated SSR handling SOPs
l4_steps.kpi: SSR on-time fulfillment rate ≥96%; SSR-related NPS ≥+45; DOT disability complaints per 10,000 enplanements <0.2
l4_steps.pain_point: SSR data is fragmented across Altéa PSS, Salesforce CRM, and SITA AMS with no unified SSR BI view — monthly reconciliation is manual and takes 3–4 days

l4_steps.name: Ingest booking & transaction data from PSS
l4_steps.input: Nightly batch feed of PNR, ticketing, and ancillary purchase records
l4_steps.output: Raw booking event stream loaded to data lake
l4_steps.kpi: Data pipeline SLA: 100% of prior-day records ingested by 04:00 local
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PNR schema changes on major releases can silently break field mappings, causing downstream profile gaps until the next data audit cycle

l4_steps.name: Collect loyalty programme interaction events
l4_steps.input: Email opens, loyalty portal logins, miles accrual and redemption events
l4_steps.output: Loyalty event stream appended to data lake
l4_steps.kpi: Event capture rate ≥99% of Salesforce Marketing Cloud triggers per day
l4_steps.pain_point: Loyalty tier change events arrive asynchronously from PSS; without an event-ordering layer, a customer can receive a downgrade communication before the upgrade is confirmed

l4_steps.name: Capture web & mobile behavioural data
l4_steps.input: Clickstream, search, seat-map interaction, and app session events
l4_steps.output: Behavioural event stream with session IDs written to AWS S3
l4_steps.kpi: Tag coverage ≥98% of key conversion pages; session data latency ≤2 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: iOS ATT (App Tracking Transparency) and Safari ITP limit cross-device identity stitching, reducing identifiable behavioural profiles by ~20–30% on Apple devices

l4_steps.name: Validate data completeness across all sources
l4_steps.input: Ingested event counts vs expected record volumes per source
l4_steps.output: Completeness scorecard; pipeline held or released
l4_steps.kpi: Overall data completeness ≥95% before downstream processing proceeds
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS-originated bookings (Sabre, Travelport, Amadeus GDS) often arrive with partial passenger profile fields; missing DOB or contact email breaks identity resolution

l4_steps.name: Cleanse and deduplicate customer records
l4_steps.input: Raw multi-source event streams from data lake
l4_steps.output: Standardised, deduplicated customer record set
l4_steps.kpi: Duplicate record rate ≤0.5% post-cleanse; address standardisation accuracy ≥97%
l4_steps.pain_point: Passengers booking via third-party OTAs (Expedia, booking.com) often have name/email variations that resist standard matching rules, inflating duplicate counts

l4_steps.name: Verify PII consent and GDPR / CCPA compliance
l4_steps.input: Customer consent records, marketing opt-in flags, data retention schedules
l4_steps.output: Consent-cleared record set; non-consented records quarantined
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of records processed against current consent status before any marketing activation; consent sync latency ≤24 hours from collection event
l4_steps.pain_point: Consent revocation must propagate to Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Adobe Experience Platform, and Braze within the 72-hour GDPR window — cross-system latency routinely misses this SLA without automated orchestration

l4_steps.name: Enforce data retention and right-to-erasure rules
l4_steps.input: Erasure requests from customer portal, regulatory notices
l4_steps.output: Deletion confirmation across all downstream systems within SLA
l4_steps.kpi: Right-to-erasure requests fulfilled within 30 days per GDPR Article 17; 100% completion rate
l4_steps.pain_point: Cascading deletes across Altéa PSS, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Adobe Experience Platform, and AWS Redshift require coordinated API calls; partial deletions create residual PII exposure

l4_steps.name: Resolve identity and stitch cross-channel profiles
l4_steps.input: Consent-cleared, cleansed records with email, loyalty ID, device ID, PNR
l4_steps.output: Unified customer profiles with deterministic and probabilistic identity links
l4_steps.kpi: Identity match rate ≥80% of known travellers; profile stitching latency ≤6 hours from data ingestion
l4_steps.pain_point: Passengers using travel agent bookings have no direct loyalty ID in the PNR, requiring probabilistic name+route matching which has a ~12% false-positive rate without additional signal

l4_steps.name: Compute customer lifetime value and tier segments
l4_steps.input: Unified profiles enriched with 24-month transaction history
l4_steps.output: CLV score, predicted annual revenue, and tier classification per customer
l4_steps.kpi: CLV model R² ≥0.72; tier classification refreshed weekly; top-decile CLV customers identified for proactive retention
l4_steps.pain_point: Frequent-flyer programme changes (e.g., move from segment- to revenue-based earning) invalidate historical CLV models requiring full retraining — a 3–4 week disruption to personalisation pipelines

l4_steps.name: Run customer segmentation models
l4_steps.input: Unified profiles with CLV, travel frequency, route preferences, ancillary purchase history
l4_steps.output: Customer segment labels (e.g., Leisure Infrequent, Corporate Road Warrior, Premium Aspirant)
l4_steps.kpi: Silhouette score ≥0.55 for k-means clusters; segment refresh cycle ≤7 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Seasonal demand patterns (holidays, school breaks) cause segment drift that is difficult to distinguish from genuine behavioural change — misclassification drives irrelevant offers during peak booking windows

l4_steps.name: Build propensity scores for ancillary and upgrade offers
l4_steps.input: Segment labels, historical ancillary purchase events, seat-map interaction data
l4_steps.output: Per-customer propensity scores: upgrade likelihood, seat upsell, lounge day-pass, travel insurance
l4_steps.kpi: AUC ≥0.75 per propensity model; score refresh ≤48 hours before scheduled departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Short-haul domestic passengers have sparse ancillary purchase histories, causing propensity models to default to population averages and suppressing personalisation lift on high-frequency leisure routes

l4_steps.name: Score churn risk for loyalty programme members
l4_steps.input: Loyalty transaction recency, frequency, redemption gap, competitive route exposure
l4_steps.output: Churn risk tier (High / Medium / Low) and recommended retention intervention
l4_steps.kpi: Churn model recall ≥70% on held-out validation set; High-risk members flagged ≥60 days before predicted lapse
l4_steps.pain_point: Alliance-free carriers have no partner accrual data to detect cross-airline defection; churn signals are visible only after the customer has already reduced flying frequency, limiting intervention window

l4_steps.name: Generate personalised pre-trip offer packages
l4_steps.input: Propensity scores, segment labels, PNR departure date, fare class booked
l4_steps.output: Personalised offer payload (upgrade, seat, lounge, hotel partner) per customer
l4_steps.kpi: Offer relevance score ≥70% (measured by click-through proxy); ancillary attach rate uplift ≥8% vs control
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO-filed fare class restrictions may invalidate upgrade offers at activation time — without real-time inventory checks against Amadeus NRM, irrelevant offers are served, eroding customer trust

l4_steps.name: Activate offers across email, app push, and web
l4_steps.input: Personalised offer payloads, customer channel preference flags, optimal send-time scores
l4_steps.output: Delivered personalised messages across email, push notification, and website homepage
l4_steps.kpi: Email open rate ≥28%; push notification opt-in rate ≥45%; web personalisation CTR ≥4%
l4_steps.pain_point: Channel fatigue from overlapping CRM, loyalty, and operational email streams — without cross-channel frequency capping in Braze, customers in high-propensity segments receive 5–8 emails per week, driving unsubscribe rates above 0.6%

l4_steps.name: Serve real-time personalisation at airport touchpoints
l4_steps.input: Customer profile, check-in event trigger, real-time upgrade inventory from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Targeted upgrade or ancillary prompt displayed at kiosk or agent terminal
l4_steps.kpi: Kiosk upgrade conversion rate ≥5% for High-propensity customers; offer display latency ≤500ms from check-in event
l4_steps.pain_point: Real-time inventory sync between Amadeus Altéa PSS and SITA AMS kiosks can lag by 2–4 minutes during peak check-in, causing declined upgrade offers that had already been verbally accepted at the counter

l4_steps.name: Track offer redemption and revenue attribution
l4_steps.input: Offer delivery logs from Braze and SITA AMS, ancillary revenue from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Offer conversion rate, incremental revenue per segment, cost-per-acquisition
l4_steps.kpi: Incremental ancillary revenue per personalised journey ≥€12 vs control; attribution model updated weekly
l4_steps.pain_point: Last-click attribution in Salesforce Marketing Cloud over-credits email and under-credits app push and airport kiosk touchpoints — multi-touch attribution requires custom AWS Redshift modelling not available out-of-the-box

l4_steps.name: Analyse A/B test results and model performance
l4_steps.input: Conversion data, control vs treatment group outcomes, propensity model predictions vs actuals
l4_steps.output: Performance report; decision to retrain models or adjust segmentation thresholds
l4_steps.kpi: A/B test statistical significance ≥95% before rolling out winning variant; model performance reviewed bi-weekly
l4_steps.pain_point: Small holdout sizes on low-frequency routes (e.g., thin regional services) prevent statistical significance from being reached within a single IATA season, forcing carry-over decisions based on directional data only

l4_steps.name: Monitor operational alerts for IRROP triggers
l4_steps.input: Flight delay or cancellation signals from ops control, ATC, or OCC
l4_steps.output: IRROP alert ticket created with flight number, delay code, and estimated passenger impact count
l4_steps.kpi: IRROP detection-to-alert time ≤15 min from event confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS integration with Altéa PSS can lag 5–10 min during high-volume events, widening the window before rebooking can begin and increasing downstream queue pressure

l4_steps.name: Classify disruption type, cause, and regulatory scope
l4_steps.input: IRROP alert from SITA AMS, IATA delay codes, flight status data
l4_steps.output: Disruption classification record (delay / cancel / divert), IATA cause code, DOT 14 CFR Part 250 and EC 261/2004 applicability flag
l4_steps.kpi: Cause code classification accuracy ≥95%; regulatory flag set within 5 min of classification
l4_steps.pain_point: Weather vs. technical cause code misclassification directly affects DOT compensation liability exposure; Altéa delay code mapping requires manual override when ops and commercial teams disagree

l4_steps.name: Activate IRROP protocol and notify stakeholders
l4_steps.input: Completed disruption classification record
l4_steps.output: IRROP case opened in Salesforce with severity tier; airport ops, crew coordination, and customer comms teams alerted
l4_steps.kpi: All operational stakeholders notified within 10 min of IRROP classification; case opened with correct priority tier in 100% of activations
l4_steps.pain_point: Parallel activation across Altéa, Salesforce, and the crew management system has no single handshake confirmation; coordination gaps emerge during simultaneous multi-flight IRROPs

l4_steps.name: Extract affected passenger manifest and PNR records
l4_steps.input: Disrupted flight number and departure date from IRROP case
l4_steps.output: Full passenger manifest with PNR, contact details (email, mobile), fare class, loyalty tier, and connection itinerary flag
l4_steps.kpi: Manifest extraction completed within 5 min of IRROP activation; contact data completeness ≥92% of affected PAX
l4_steps.pain_point: Passengers booked through OTAs and GDS channels frequently have incomplete or agency-held contact fields in the Altéa PNR; direct SMS or email outreach fails for approximately 8% of affected passengers

l4_steps.name: Segment passengers by recovery priority tier
l4_steps.input: Passenger manifest with loyalty tier, fare basis, connection risk flag, and booking channel
l4_steps.output: Prioritised recovery queue: P1 (elite status and passengers with tight connections), P2 (connecting itineraries), P3 (point-to-point local)
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of premium-tier and connection-at-risk passengers classified as P1 before notification dispatch
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa segmentation logic does not automatically identify passengers with connection windows under 60 min on the same PNR; analysts must manually review itineraries, adding 10–15 min per large event

l4_steps.name: Send proactive disruption notification with self-serve link
l4_steps.input: Prioritised passenger manifest, disruption details, self-service rebooking portal URL
l4_steps.output: SMS, email, and app push notification sent per passenger; self-service rebooking link and 60-minute response window communicated
l4_steps.kpi: ≥90% of affected PAX notified within 30 min of IRROP activation; self-serve rebooking adoption ≥35% of notified passengers
l4_steps.pain_point: Push notification delivery drops to approximately 72% for passengers without the airline app installed; passengers booked via travel agencies require manual outreach via GDS telex, which averages 20 min per agency

l4_steps.name: Run automated rebooking engine against open inventory
l4_steps.input: Prioritised unresolved passenger queue, disrupted flight data, real-time seat inventory
l4_steps.output: Candidate alternative itineraries generated per passenger prioritised by departure proximity and cabin match
l4_steps.kpi: Auto-rebook match rate ≥70% of affected passengers on same-day service; engine execution time ≤3 min per 200-PAX event
l4_steps.pain_point: Inventory constraints on popular routes during a large IRROP cause cascading rebooking failures; Altéa auto-rebook does not dynamically reprice across fare classes without a manual IT change request, locking lower-fare passengers out of available premium inventory

l4_steps.name: Validate alternative itinerary against re-protection policy
l4_steps.input: Candidate itineraries, re-protection policy thresholds (same-day ±4 hrs; next-day ±24 hrs)
l4_steps.output: Policy-compliant itinerary approved for issuance, or case flagged for agent-assisted recovery
l4_steps.kpi: Re-protection policy compliance ≥98% of issued auto-rebooks; policy exception review completed within 5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Re-protection thresholds are hardcoded configuration parameters in Altéa requiring an IT change request to update; during major weather events affecting 50+ flights simultaneously the static thresholds cannot flex to match available capacity

l4_steps.name: Issue confirmed rebooking and send updated itinerary
l4_steps.input: Validated replacement itinerary, passenger PNR
l4_steps.output: Updated PNR with new flight segment, boarding pass where applicable, confirmation notification delivered via AWS SNS
l4_steps.kpi: Itinerary confirmation delivered within 5 min of rebooking commit; boarding pass pre-issuance success rate ≥95%
l4_steps.pain_point: DCS boarding pass pre-issuance fails for departures more than 24 hrs out or where gate assignment is pending at origin; passengers receive confirmation but must re-check in at the airport, creating service desk queue spikes

l4_steps.name: Assess passenger welfare entitlement under applicable regulations
l4_steps.input: Disruption cause code, flight distance, delay duration, passenger origin and nationality
l4_steps.output: Entitlement determination per DOT 14 CFR Part 250 and EC 261/2004; overnight flag, meal flag, and transport flag set on IRROP case
l4_steps.kpi: Entitlement determination completed within 15 min of IRROP activation; regulatory accuracy ≥99% validated by Customer Relations
l4_steps.pain_point: Dual-regulation scenarios on transatlantic routes require manual legal review; Salesforce workflow rules do not auto-resolve cross-jurisdictional entitlement conflicts, exposing the airline to under-compensation claims and EU regulatory fines

l4_steps.name: Issue hotel accommodation vouchers for stranded passengers
l4_steps.input: Overnight entitlement flag, passenger count by airport, contracted hotel partner API availability
l4_steps.output: Hotel voucher codes issued digitally via app, email, or airport kiosk; rooms blocked with hotel partner
l4_steps.kpi: Hotel voucher issuance within 45 min of overnight determination; room availability confirmed for ≥90% of entitled passengers
l4_steps.pain_point: Hotel partner API connectivity is inconsistent at smaller outstations; manual phone booking is required at approximately 30% of network stations, extending wait times to 2+ hrs and exhausting customer service staff capacity during simultaneous multi-station IRROPs

l4_steps.name: Distribute meal and ground transportation vouchers
l4_steps.input: Delay duration, regulatory entitlement thresholds, terminal and gate location
l4_steps.output: Meal vouchers and transport vouchers issued digitally or at service desk; voucher redemption records logged in SITA
l4_steps.kpi: ≥85% of vouchers issued digitally (app or email); airport service desk queue time ≤20 min during events under 300 PAX
l4_steps.pain_point: Digital voucher adoption varies significantly by passenger demographic; elderly and tech-averse passengers queue at service desks, creating bottlenecks during large IRROPs that overwhelm deployed airport staff ratios

l4_steps.name: Route unresolved cases to contact centre agent queue
l4_steps.input: IRROP cases with no auto-rebook match or passenger rejection of auto-offer
l4_steps.output: Cases assigned to agent queue with priority tier flag; estimated wait time communicated to passenger via SMS
l4_steps.kpi: P1 passengers reached by agent within 5 min; P2 within 15 min; P3 within 30 min of queue entry
l4_steps.pain_point: Contact centre surge during large IRROP events pushes wait times to 60–90 min for P3 passengers; AWS Connect IVR overflow routing is not dynamically linked to real-time IRROP case volume for on-demand agent staffing scale-up

l4_steps.name: Present interline and OAL rebooking options to passenger
l4_steps.input: Unresolved IRROP case, active interline e-ticketing agreements, OAL real-time availability
l4_steps.output: Expanded rebooking options including partner carrier itineraries presented and explained to passenger
l4_steps.kpi: Interline option presented within 10 min of agent engagement; OAL rebook success rate ≥60% when invoked
l4_steps.pain_point: Interline agreements and bilateral e-ticketing eligibility must be manually verified in Sabre before issuance; Altéa has no automated interline rebook capability for many partner carriers, requiring agents to switch between Sabre and Altéa and manually reissue tickets

l4_steps.name: Confirm passenger decision on rebooking or refund
l4_steps.input: Alternative itinerary options presented, passenger verbal or digital preference
l4_steps.output: Accepted rebooking confirmed in Altéa PNR, or refund request logged in Salesforce Service Cloud with case ID
l4_steps.kpi: Agent average handling time ≤12 min per case; passenger acceptance rate of presented alternatives ≥75%
l4_steps.pain_point: Refund processing for NDC-booked tickets falls outside the standard Altéa refund workflow; agents must manually process credits across 2–3 systems, extending handling time by 8–12 min per NDC case and increasing error rates

l4_steps.name: Calculate entitlement and initiate compensation payment
l4_steps.input: Confirmed refund or compensation decision, entitlement determination record, original fare paid
l4_steps.output: Refund or compensation payment initiated in SAP; payment timeline and reference communicated to passenger via Salesforce case
l4_steps.kpi: Refund processing completed within 7 business days per DOT requirement; compensation acknowledgement letter issued within 24 hrs of claim receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: Refunds for GDS and OTA-booked tickets must route through the original selling channel; the airline has no direct refund path to the customer, requiring agency debit memos or manual credit card processing that can extend settlement to 15–30 business days

l4_steps.name: Log IRROP event data and capture NPS impact
l4_steps.input: Closed IRROP cases from Salesforce, post-event NPS survey responses, cost summary from SAP
l4_steps.output: IRROP event record with root cause, passenger count, recovery rate, NPS delta, and total recovery cost; stored in data lake for reporting
l4_steps.kpi: Post-IRROP NPS survey response rate ≥25%; recovery satisfaction score ≥3.5 out of 5.0; event record published within 48 hrs of case closure
l4_steps.pain_point: NPS survey responses from post-IRROP emails are not automatically linked to specific IRROP event records in Salesforce; manual tagging is required, delaying analytics availability by 48–72 hrs and reducing the accuracy of root cause attribution

l4_steps.name: Retrieve passenger PNR and loyalty tier status
l4_steps.input: Passenger boarding pass or loyalty card scan at lounge entry
l4_steps.output: Confirmed PNR, fare class, and loyalty tier record
l4_steps.kpi: Access verification time < 30 seconds per passenger
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa tier-lookup latency spikes during irregular operations (IRROP) can queue 20+ passengers at peak departure banks, degrading premium brand perception

l4_steps.name: Validate lounge entitlement against fare and tier
l4_steps.input: PNR, fare class code, loyalty tier from step 1.1
l4_steps.output: Entitlement decision (Eligible / Not Eligible) and access tier (Standard / Premium / First)
l4_steps.kpi: Entitlement accuracy rate ≥ 99.5% (no wrongful denial or admission)
l4_steps.pain_point: Misalignment between ATPCO fare class entitlement rules and Comarch loyalty tier tables causes wrongful denials for premium codeshare passengers not in airline's own PSS

l4_steps.name: Check real-time lounge occupancy vs. capacity cap
l4_steps.input: Live occupancy count from SITA AMS badge-in sensors; configured capacity limit per lounge
l4_steps.output: Current occupancy percentage; green / amber / red capacity status
l4_steps.kpi: Lounge occupancy maintained at ≤ 90% of rated capacity during peak banks
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS occupancy sensors in third-party contract lounges (e.g. airport operator lounges) are not integrated, requiring manual headcounts and creating data lag of 5–10 minutes

l4_steps.name: Issue digital lounge access pass or redirect passenger
l4_steps.input: Entitlement decision from 1.2; occupancy status from 1.3
l4_steps.output: Digital lounge pass (QR code) issued to eligible passenger, or voucher / priority queue token issued when capacity exceeded
l4_steps.kpi: Guest satisfaction with access process ≥ 4.2 / 5.0 (post-visit survey)
l4_steps.pain_point: No dynamic overbooking buffer in Altéa lounge module — capacity denial is binary, leading to complaints when eligible passengers are turned away 1–2 seats below hard cap

l4_steps.name: Forecast lounge demand from departure schedule
l4_steps.input: Published schedule SSIM file; historical lounge utilisation by departure bank; loyalty tier passenger mix from Comarch
l4_steps.output: Hourly demand forecast per lounge (expected arrivals by tier) for next 72 hours
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast accuracy within ± 10% of actual peak occupancy
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS schedule feed does not include real-time irregular-operations (IRROP) rebooking data; demand spikes from cancelled flight consolidations are not reflected until T-4 hours

l4_steps.name: Generate staffing and F&B resource plan
l4_steps.input: 72-hour demand forecast from 2.1; staffing contracts and F&B par levels
l4_steps.output: Shift roster, F&B order quantities, amenity replenishment schedule
l4_steps.kpi: Staff-to-guest ratio ≥ 1:15 during peak departure banks; F&B stockout rate < 1%
l4_steps.pain_point: Resource planning is manual in spreadsheets at most stations — no integrated workforce management system feeding lounge-specific demand signals, leading to over/understaffing 30% of departure banks

l4_steps.name: Submit F&B and consumables requisition to catering
l4_steps.input: F&B order quantities from 2.2; approved supplier catalogue
l4_steps.output: Purchase orders raised in SAP Ariba; delivery confirmed for T-3 hours pre-departure bank
l4_steps.kpi: Catering order fulfilment rate ≥ 98% within agreed lead time
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP Ariba supplier catalogue is managed by central procurement and updated quarterly — lounge-specific seasonal menu changes or regional items cannot be added ad hoc, limiting localisation of premium experience

l4_steps.name: Activate surge staffing protocol for high-load windows
l4_steps.input: Forecast showing > 80% occupancy in any 30-minute window; SITA AMS flight load alerts
l4_steps.output: Surge staffing confirmation; overflow lounge section opened (if available); partner lounge access tokens issued
l4_steps.kpi: Surge activation lead time ≤ 2 hours before predicted peak; guest wait time at entry ≤ 5 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: Overflow agreements with airport operator lounges are station-specific and not codified in SITA AMS — activation requires manual phone calls, causing delays of 20–30 minutes in agreeing capacity at short notice

l4_steps.name: Retrieve passenger profile and service preferences
l4_steps.input: Confirmed PNR and loyalty ID from step 1.1
l4_steps.output: Passenger profile: dietary preferences, language, past complaints, upgrade history, service notes
l4_steps.kpi: Profile retrieval at lounge entry < 15 seconds; preference recognition rate ≥ 85% of repeat premium guests
l4_steps.pain_point: Salesforce CRM preference data is updated via post-flight survey only — real-time in-flight service notes from cabin crew (e.g., passenger declined meal) are not written back to CRM, causing repeat service failures on next journey

l4_steps.name: Flag VIP, VVIP, and special service requests on manifest
l4_steps.input: Day-of-operations manifest; CRM profile flags from 3.1; SSR codes (VVIP, WCHR, MEDA, SPML)
l4_steps.output: Annotated manifest with VIP tier flags, SSR types, and assigned concierge owner per passenger
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of SSR-flagged premium passengers identified ≥ 90 minutes prior to departure
l4_steps.pain_point: VVIP flags set by sales or government affairs teams are stored in a separate SharePoint list not integrated with Altéa PSS — lounge staff miss VVIPs when SharePoint is not checked manually before each departure bank

l4_steps.name: Coordinate personalised amenity kits and premium meal setup
l4_steps.input: Annotated manifest from 3.2; dietary and preference data from Salesforce CRM; catering delivery confirmation from 2.3
l4_steps.output: Personalised amenity kit assignment per seat; meal pre-selection recorded in catering order
l4_steps.kpi: Meal pre-selection accuracy ≥ 97%; amenity kit shortfall rate < 0.5% of premium seats
l4_steps.pain_point: Pre-selection data from Salesforce CRM must be manually transcribed into the catering system — no API integration between CRM preference data and catering management platform increases transcription error rate to ~3%

l4_steps.name: Activate meet-and-greet and dedicated butler for VIPs
l4_steps.input: VIP / VVIP flag from step 3.2; expected arrival time from SITA AMS inbound flight status
l4_steps.output: Named concierge assigned to VIP; curbside or airside meet-and-greet schedule confirmed; butler service briefing completed
l4_steps.kpi: VIP meet-and-greet execution rate 100% of flagged passengers; greeting delay < 5 minutes from arrival
l4_steps.pain_point: Inbound flight delays not surfaced in Salesforce CRM require concierge to monitor SITA AMS separately — no unified notification when VIP inbound flight is delayed > 30 minutes, leading to missed or premature meet-and-greets

l4_steps.name: Execute lounge F&B, spa, and digital amenity service
l4_steps.input: Active guest list from SITA AMS lounge occupancy module; F&B stock confirmed in 2.3
l4_steps.output: Service log per guest (items consumed, special requests fulfilled, service timestamps)
l4_steps.kpi: F&B replenishment cycle ≤ 20 minutes; spa booking wait time ≤ 10 minutes; Wi-Fi uptime ≥ 99.9%
l4_steps.pain_point: Service logging is paper-based in most third-party contract lounges — consumption data is not captured digitally, preventing demand pattern analysis and cost reconciliation accuracy, leading to billing disputes with caterers

l4_steps.name: Broadcast boarding gate notifications to lounge guests
l4_steps.input: Gate departure T-30 and T-15 alerts from SITA AMS flight information display system (FIDS)
l4_steps.output: Visual and audio boarding alerts in lounge; individual SMS / app push notifications to guests
l4_steps.kpi: Boarding notification issued ≥ 30 minutes before STD; missed notification rate < 0.1%
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS FIDS integration is reliable at hub stations but frequently lags at outstations (> 5 minutes) — lounge staff rely on personal phone calls to gate agents for departure time confirmation at 30% of stations

l4_steps.name: Escalate and resolve in-lounge SSR requests
l4_steps.input: Guest SSR codes from step 3.2; real-time service requests raised at lounge reception
l4_steps.output: SSR resolved or escalated to operations; record updated in Altéa PSS with resolution notes
l4_steps.kpi: SSR resolution within lounge: ≥ 90% within 15 minutes; escalation to operations < 5% of SSRs
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS SSR update requires back-office terminal access — lounge concierges using mobile devices cannot update SSR records in real time, causing duplication of effort when the same request is re-raised at the gate

l4_steps.name: Execute no-show baggage offload for gate-close no-shows
l4_steps.input: Final boarding close signal from SITA AMS; passenger no-show confirmation from gate agent
l4_steps.output: Offload order issued in Altéa PSS; baggage reconciliation request sent to ramp; lounge access record closed
l4_steps.kpi: Baggage offload completion within 15 minutes of gate close; no-show offload accuracy 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Lounge no-show visibility depends on gate agent manually communicating non-boarding to the lounge — no automated Altéa trigger when a premium passenger clears lounge entry but does not scan boarding pass at gate, causing offload delays that breach 15-minute target

l4_steps.name: Capture post-lounge NPS and satisfaction scores
l4_steps.input: Lounge visit closed (guest departed for gate); guest contact details from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: NPS score per visit; free-text feedback categorised by theme (F&B, Staff, Comfort, Connectivity)
l4_steps.kpi: Survey response rate ≥ 35% of lounge visitors; Lounge NPS target ≥ 75
l4_steps.pain_point: Medallia survey invitation is triggered by flight departure, not lounge exit — passengers in transit or connecting through a second lounge receive duplicate invitations, inflating response counts and skewing NPS by station

l4_steps.name: Review KPI dashboard and trigger service recovery if below threshold
l4_steps.input: Aggregated NPS scores, occupancy data, F&B stockout events, SSR resolution rates from Medallia and SITA AMS
l4_steps.output: Weekly KPI report; service recovery action plan if NPS < 75 or complaint rate > 2%; trend analysis by station
l4_steps.kpi: KPI dashboard refresh latency ≤ 24 hours; corrective action plans issued within 48 hours of threshold breach
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau dashboards pull from multiple source systems (Medallia, SITA AMS, Altéa, SAP Ariba) with inconsistent refresh cadences — data as-of timestamps differ by up to 48 hours, making same-week service recovery decisions unreliable for fast-moving operational issues

l4_steps.name: Evaluate co-brand bank partner candidates
l4_steps.input: Bank RFP responses, cardholder portfolio data, credit union benchmarks
l4_steps.output: Partner shortlist with scored evaluation matrix
l4_steps.kpi: Partner evaluation cycle ≤60 days; minimum 3 candidates scored
l4_steps.pain_point: Airline loyalty platforms (e.g., Comarch Loyalty) lack native RFP workflow tooling — scoring is manual in spreadsheets, creating audit gaps for legal review

l4_steps.name: Negotiate revenue-share and miles pricing terms
l4_steps.input: Partner shortlist, actuarial breakage model, competitive miles CPM benchmarks
l4_steps.output: Agreed term sheet: miles CPM, sign-up bonus pool, revenue-share %
l4_steps.kpi: Miles CPM negotiated ≥$0.011 per mile; sign-up bonus cost per card ≤$120
l4_steps.pain_point: Breakage assumptions differ between airline actuary and bank models — misalignment inflates miles liability on SAP S/4HANA FI balance sheet by up to 15%

l4_steps.name: Execute partnership agreement and integration SLA
l4_steps.input: Signed term sheet, legal review, PCI-DSS compliance checklist
l4_steps.output: Executed co-brand agreement, data-sharing addendum, SLA schedules
l4_steps.kpi: Contract execution ≤90 days from term sheet; SLA uptime commitment ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: PCI-DSS and GDPR/CCPA data-sharing clauses require iterative legal review — delays frequently push launch dates 4–8 weeks beyond plan

l4_steps.name: Define card tier earn rates and bonus categories
l4_steps.input: Executed partnership agreement, competitive card benchmarking (OAG / Phocuswire reports)
l4_steps.output: Earn rate table: base miles/$ per spend category, bonus multipliers per tier
l4_steps.kpi: Earn rate design approved by actuary within 10 business days; ≥3 spend bonus categories defined
l4_steps.pain_point: Earn rule complexity (dining, travel, grocery multipliers) creates combinatorial edge cases in Comarch rule engine — insufficient QA leads to overpayment incidents

l4_steps.name: Configure earn rules in loyalty management platform
l4_steps.input: Earn rate table, card BIN ranges from bank processor (Visa/Mastercard)
l4_steps.output: Live earn rule configuration in loyalty platform, BIN-mapped to card product
l4_steps.kpi: Rule configuration UAT pass rate ≥98%; zero overpayment defects in regression suite
l4_steps.pain_point: BIN range changes during card reissue cycles (e.g., chip migration) are not proactively communicated by Visa/Mastercard — stale BIN mapping causes missed miles posts

l4_steps.name: Validate earn rules against PSS booking data
l4_steps.input: Comarch earn rule config, synthetic test transaction set, Altéa member profiles
l4_steps.output: Validation report: earn accuracy %, exception count, sign-off for go-live
l4_steps.kpi: Miles earn accuracy ≥99.9% in UAT; <5 exception cases per 1,000 test transactions
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa loyalty module integration requires custom API adapter for co-brand transactions — adapter versioning lags Altéa PSS upgrades, causing earn rule regressions post-patch

l4_steps.name: Certify integration with bank card processor
l4_steps.input: Bank-issued API credentials, PCI-DSS network diagram, certification test plan
l4_steps.output: Certified integration: bank transaction feed → loyalty platform; go/no-go decision
l4_steps.kpi: Certification completed ≤30 days; API response latency ≤200ms p99
l4_steps.pain_point: Bank processor certification environments are infrequently refreshed — test data does not reflect production edge cases, leading to post-launch transaction failures

l4_steps.name: Receive daily transaction file from bank partner
l4_steps.input: Bank-generated SFTP daily transaction file (ISO 8583 or proprietary format)
l4_steps.output: Ingested transaction file in AWS S3 data lake; ingestion audit log
l4_steps.kpi: File receipt by 06:00 local time daily; file completeness ≥99.95% of expected records
l4_steps.pain_point: Bank SFTP file delivery SLAs are frequently breached (5–10 min late) — cascading delay into daily miles posting batch impacts member experience for same-day redemptions

l4_steps.name: Match cardholder to loyalty programme member
l4_steps.input: Daily transaction file, loyalty member master (Comarch), name/DOB/email match keys
l4_steps.output: Matched transaction set; unmatched exception queue for manual review
l4_steps.kpi: Member match rate ≥99.2%; unmatched queue resolved within 48 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Name discrepancies between bank card embossing (legal name) and loyalty profile (preferred name) cause false negatives — no automated fuzzy-match in current Comarch-Redshift pipeline

l4_steps.name: Calculate miles earned per matched transaction
l4_steps.input: Matched transactions, earn rule table, merchant category codes (MCC)
l4_steps.output: Miles calculation ledger: member ID, transaction ID, miles awarded
l4_steps.kpi: Miles calculation accuracy ≥99.99%; batch processing completed within 2 hours of file receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: MCC mapping inconsistencies from Visa/Mastercard network (e.g., new fintech merchants with catch-all MCCs) result in incorrect bonus tier application — no real-time MCC correction feed

l4_steps.name: Post miles to member loyalty account
l4_steps.input: Miles calculation ledger, member account status (active/suspended/expired)
l4_steps.output: Posted miles on member account; transaction confirmation email triggered
l4_steps.kpi: Miles posting within 24 hours of transaction date; member notification sent ≤1 hour post-post
l4_steps.pain_point: Suspended accounts (fraud hold by bank) do not trigger Comarch status sync — miles post to suspended accounts creating redemption liability that cannot be fulfilled

l4_steps.name: Execute co-brand card acquisition campaign
l4_steps.input: Approved campaign brief, member segmentation (Redshift cohorts), bank co-op budget
l4_steps.output: Live campaign: email, in-app, boarding pass inserts; click/apply tracking UTMs
l4_steps.kpi: Campaign conversion rate ≥2.5% of targeted members; cost per new card account ≤$85
l4_steps.pain_point: Boarding pass insert channel requires coordination with PSS vendor (Altéa) for printing logic — lead time is 6 weeks, making last-minute promotional changes impossible

l4_steps.name: Validate welcome bonus eligibility for new cardholders
l4_steps.input: New cardholder activation event from bank, minimum spend threshold rules
l4_steps.output: Eligibility flag: welcome bonus approved or pending spend threshold
l4_steps.kpi: Welcome bonus activation within 5 business days of threshold met; ≤0.1% erroneous bonus grants
l4_steps.pain_point: Bank spend threshold data arrives in arrears (T+3 days) — members who query missing welcome bonus generate high CSAT complaints before data is available

l4_steps.name: Activate welcome bonus miles for eligible cardholders
l4_steps.input: Eligibility approval flag, welcome bonus amount per card product tier
l4_steps.output: Welcome bonus miles credited to member account; confirmation notification sent
l4_steps.kpi: Welcome bonus credited ≤24 hours of eligibility approval; zero duplicate grants in batch
l4_steps.pain_point: Idempotency controls in Comarch bonus posting API are not enforced at the bank feed layer — duplicate activation events from bank cause double-grant incidents requiring costly manual reversal

l4_steps.name: Reconcile miles sold to bank vs miles posted
l4_steps.input: Comarch miles posting ledger, bank-reported miles purchase invoice, AWS Redshift audit log
l4_steps.output: Reconciliation report: matched/unmatched miles, variance %, discrepancy log
l4_steps.kpi: Monthly reconciliation variance ≤0.05% of total miles posted; reconciliation completed by day 5 of following month
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP FI miles liability account uses standard cost per mile — market-rate fluctuations in miles CPM are not reflected until year-end revaluation, distorting monthly P&L by up to $2M

l4_steps.name: Invoice bank partner for miles purchased
l4_steps.input: Reconciled miles volume, agreed CPM rate from contract, applicable taxes/fees
l4_steps.output: AR invoice issued to bank partner in SAP; payment terms triggered (Net 30)
l4_steps.kpi: Invoice issued within 3 business days of reconciliation sign-off; DSO ≤35 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Bank disputes over MCC-categorised bonus miles (billed at higher CPM) are frequent — lack of automated MCC audit trail in SAP AR module prolongs dispute resolution to 60+ days

l4_steps.name: Generate quarterly partnership performance report
l4_steps.input: AWS Redshift (card spend, miles earned, member acquisition, redemption rates), SAP FI revenue data
l4_steps.output: QBR deck: card acquisition, active cardholder rate, miles revenue, breakage %, churn
l4_steps.kpi: Active cardholder rate ≥65% (spent in last 90 days); miles revenue per active card ≥$180/yr
l4_steps.pain_point: No single source of truth for 'active cardholder' definition — Comarch, Altéa, and bank definitions diverge, causing QBR figures to be challenged by bank partner and delaying review sign-off

l4_steps.name: Conduct annual contract review and renegotiation
l4_steps.input: QBR performance history, breakage actuary update, competitive co-brand benchmarks, CPM market data
l4_steps.output: Renewed or renegotiated contract terms; updated SLA schedules in Salesforce
l4_steps.kpi: Contract renewal completed ≥90 days before expiry; CPM improvement ≥3% vs prior term
l4_steps.pain_point: Airline bargaining leverage is limited without alliance membership — bank partners benchmark co-brand terms against carriers with larger frequent flyer bases, compressing CPM improvement potential

l4_steps.name: Screen potential partners against loyalty fit criteria
l4_steps.input: Annual partnership strategy, competitor loyalty benchmarking data
l4_steps.output: Qualified partner longlist with fit-score ranking
l4_steps.kpi: Minimum 20 candidates screened per category (hotel/car/retail) per quarter
l4_steps.pain_point: Retail and hotel categories have inconsistent earn-per-dollar standards across IATA-affiliated programmes; benchmarking requires manual OAG and ATPCO data pulls with no automated feed

l4_steps.name: Score partner on member overlap and revenue potential
l4_steps.input: Qualified partner longlist, member travel and spend segmentation data
l4_steps.output: Partner scoring matrix with estimated incremental miles issued
l4_steps.kpi: Projected incremental miles-earned revenue ≥ $500K annually per partner
l4_steps.pain_point: Member spend data outside airline transactions is incomplete; reliance on third-party data append (e.g. Acxiom) adds latency of 4–6 weeks and increases data privacy compliance overhead under GDPR and CCPA

l4_steps.name: Approve partner for commercial engagement
l4_steps.input: Partner scoring matrix, brand alignment assessment
l4_steps.output: Approved partner shortlist; go/no-go decision logged in CRM
l4_steps.kpi: Decision turnaround ≤ 10 business days from submission
l4_steps.pain_point: Approval workflows require sign-off from Legal, Finance, and Brand teams simultaneously; lack of a unified workflow tool causes email-chain approvals that are difficult to audit

l4_steps.name: Define earn/burn mile rates per partner category
l4_steps.input: Approved partner shortlist, ATPCO fare basis data, competitor earn-rate benchmarks
l4_steps.output: Draft earn/burn rate card per partner (miles per $1 spend)
l4_steps.kpi: Earn rate set within ±10% of top-3 competitor benchmark to maintain programme competitiveness
l4_steps.pain_point: Earn rate proposals must account for currency-of-sale variations across hotel booking platforms; multi-currency mile valuation is not natively handled in SAP FI without custom enhancement

l4_steps.name: Model financial liability and breakage assumptions
l4_steps.input: Draft earn/burn rate card, historical redemption rates by tier, actuary breakage estimates
l4_steps.output: Points liability model with 3-year NPV projection and breakage sensitivity analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Projected breakage rate ≥ 20% to ensure programme profitability; liability exposure within approved board ceiling
l4_steps.pain_point: IFRS 15 requires deferred revenue recognition for miles issued; SAP FI configuration for loyalty liability is complex and frequently requires external audit review, delaying deal closure by 2–4 weeks

l4_steps.name: Negotiate SLA terms, data-sharing clauses, and audit rights
l4_steps.input: Approved financial model, partner draft term sheet, GDPR/CCPA data processing requirements
l4_steps.output: Negotiated term sheet with agreed data-sharing protocols and SLA penalties
l4_steps.kpi: Contract execution within 60 days of first commercial engagement; SLA uptime commitment ≥ 99.5% for transaction API
l4_steps.pain_point: Hotel and car rental partners often resist audit rights on transaction data, creating reconciliation disputes; without real-time feeds, monthly batch reconciliations result in miles posting delays of up to 72 hours, breaching member-facing SLA

l4_steps.name: Execute legally signed partnership agreement
l4_steps.input: Final negotiated term sheet, Legal sign-off, Finance approval
l4_steps.output: Countersigned partnership agreement; CRM opportunity moved to Closed Won
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of executed agreements stored in CRM document vault within 24 hours of signature
l4_steps.pain_point: Wet-signature requirements from some international hotel chains (particularly APAC and MEA regions) extend execution timelines; e-signature platforms (DocuSign) not universally accepted by all partners

l4_steps.name: Configure partner profile in loyalty management system
l4_steps.input: Signed partnership agreement, earn/burn rate card, partner branding assets
l4_steps.output: Partner configuration record active in Comarch Loyalty; earn rules loaded
l4_steps.kpi: Partner configuration completed within 5 business days of contract execution
l4_steps.pain_point: Comarch Loyalty rule engine requires structured XML earn-rule definitions; hotel chains with tiered earn rates (e.g. brand-tier multipliers) require multiple rule variants, increasing configuration time and regression test scope

l4_steps.name: Build and certify partner transaction API connector
l4_steps.input: Partner API specification, Comarch Loyalty webhook endpoints, test credentials
l4_steps.output: Certified REST/SOAP connector deployed in AWS API Gateway; sandbox test suite passing
l4_steps.kpi: API throughput ≥ 500 transactions per second; p99 latency ≤ 2 seconds
l4_steps.pain_point: Car rental partners (e.g. Hertz, Enterprise) still expose legacy SOAP APIs; bridging SOAP-to-REST within AWS API Gateway adds development cycles and creates brittle transformation layers that break on partner schema updates

l4_steps.name: Execute UAT — earn/burn transaction end-to-end test
l4_steps.input: Sandbox API connector, test member profiles in Amadeus Altéa PSS, earn/burn rule set
l4_steps.output: UAT test report; pass/fail matrix by transaction scenario
l4_steps.kpi: Transaction error rate < 0.5%; all earn/burn scenarios in test matrix pass before production release
l4_steps.pain_point: Member account linking between Amadeus Altéa PSS and partner booking engines relies on loyalty number matching; mismatched account formats (numeric vs alphanumeric) cause silent earn failures that are only detected in post-flight reconciliation

l4_steps.name: Enable partner earn/burn in production environment
l4_steps.input: UAT sign-off, change advisory board approval, production deployment runbook
l4_steps.output: Partner live in Comarch Loyalty production; transaction monitoring alerts configured in AWS CloudWatch
l4_steps.kpi: Zero P1 incidents in first 72 hours post-launch; real-time alert threshold set at error rate > 1%
l4_steps.pain_point: Production rollbacks are disruptive if a partner API sends unexpected payloads post-launch; Comarch Loyalty does not support canary releases natively, requiring full cutover with no gradual traffic ramp

l4_steps.name: Publish partner to member-facing loyalty portal and app
l4_steps.input: Partner configuration confirmed live, partner logos and copy approved by Brand
l4_steps.output: Partner listing visible on loyalty website earn-partners page and mobile app
l4_steps.kpi: Partner page live within 3 business days of production enablement; page load time ≤ 2 seconds
l4_steps.pain_point: Loyalty portal content management is tightly coupled to Altéa PSS member-facing APIs; content updates require IT release cycle (bi-weekly) rather than CMS self-service, slowing time-to-market for partner promotions

l4_steps.name: Launch targeted co-marketing campaign to member segments
l4_steps.input: Member segments from AWS Redshift, partner co-marketing budget, email/push templates
l4_steps.output: Email and push notification campaign deployed; UTM-tagged campaign links active
l4_steps.kpi: Email open rate ≥ 22%; click-through rate (CTR) ≥ 2%; campaign ROI ≥ 3:1 on miles-issued cost
l4_steps.pain_point: Member communication frequency caps (set in Salesforce Marketing Cloud) limit partnership launch campaigns to one email per member per week; competing loyalty promotions from the same period suppress campaign visibility

l4_steps.name: Monitor partner transaction volumes and error rates weekly
l4_steps.input: AWS CloudWatch API metrics, Comarch Loyalty transaction logs, partner reconciliation files
l4_steps.output: Weekly partner performance dashboard; anomaly alerts escalated to partner account manager
l4_steps.kpi: Transaction volume within ±15% of forecast; earn posting success rate ≥ 99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Hotel partners send batch transaction files (nightly SFTP) rather than real-time API calls; delayed posting means members do not see miles for 24–72 hours, generating inbound contact centre volume and NPS drag

l4_steps.name: Audit points liability exposure and breakage monthly
l4_steps.input: Comarch Loyalty issued-miles ledger, SAP deferred revenue balance, redemption actuals
l4_steps.output: Monthly liability reconciliation report; variance flagged for CFO review if > 5% vs forecast
l4_steps.kpi: Liability reconciliation completed by business day 5 of each month; breakage rate maintained ≥ 18%
l4_steps.pain_point: IFRS 15 standalone selling price (SSP) for miles must be updated quarterly; SAP CO-PA margin reporting does not natively integrate with Comarch Loyalty ledger, requiring manual extract-transform-load (ETL) via AWS Redshift

l4_steps.name: Trigger partner performance improvement plan if KPIs missed
l4_steps.input: Weekly performance dashboard, partner SLA breach log, financial variance report
l4_steps.output: Formal performance improvement plan (PIP) issued to partner; 90-day remediation timeline logged in CRM
l4_steps.kpi: PIP issued within 10 business days of confirmed SLA breach; partner response received within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: SLA penalty clauses are often commercially difficult to enforce with major hotel chains (Marriott, Hilton) due to contractual carve-outs; legal escalation stalls programme improvements and damages long-term relationship

l4_steps.name: Conduct annual partner business review (ABR)
l4_steps.input: Full-year transaction data, financial P&L by partner, member satisfaction scores (NPS by earn category)
l4_steps.output: ABR presentation deck; renewal recommendation with commercial term changes proposed
l4_steps.kpi: ABR completed ≥ 90 days before contract expiry; partner NPS score ≥ +30 for renewal consideration
l4_steps.pain_point: Attribution of loyalty revenue uplift to specific partners is difficult; multi-partner journeys (hotel + car + flight) where miles are earned across a trip create ambiguous incrementality data that weakens negotiation positions

l4_steps.name: Execute contract renewal, renegotiation, or off-boarding
l4_steps.input: ABR recommendation, partner counter-proposal, updated financial model from SAP
l4_steps.output: Renewed/amended contract executed; or off-boarding runbook triggered with Comarch Loyalty deactivation schedule
l4_steps.kpi: Contract renewal signed ≥ 30 days before expiry; off-boarding completed within 45 days with zero orphaned earn transactions
l4_steps.pain_point: Partner off-boarding requires coordinated deactivation across Comarch Loyalty, AWS API Gateway, Salesforce Marketing Cloud suppression lists, and Altéa PSS member portal; no single orchestration tool manages the full off-boarding workflow, creating risk of earn transactions processed after contract end

l4_steps.name: Receive inbound contact via omnichannel
l4_steps.input: Customer call, webchat, email, or social media contact event
l4_steps.output: Contact session initiated; channel and intent captured
l4_steps.kpi: First contact resolution (FCR) rate ≥75%
l4_steps.pain_point: Channel fragmentation — voice, chat, email, and social handled by separate queues, driving repeat contacts and inflated contact volume

l4_steps.name: Attempt IVR / AI chatbot self-service
l4_steps.input: Contact session, customer-stated intent, IVR menu selection
l4_steps.output: Self-service resolution or escalation flag to live agent queue
l4_steps.kpi: Self-service containment rate ≥40%; bot CSAT ≥3.8/5.0
l4_steps.pain_point: IVR containment collapses during IRROP events; customers bypass bot with repeated keypress-zero, spiking live agent demand by up to 300%

l4_steps.name: Route contact to skilled agent queue
l4_steps.input: Identified customer intent, agent skill tags, real-time queue depth
l4_steps.output: Contact queued to appropriate agent team; estimated wait time published
l4_steps.kpi: Average Speed of Answer (ASA) ≤90 seconds; abandonment rate ≤5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Skill-tag mismatches in WFM routing rules direct contacts to wrong specialisms (e.g. loyalty queries to general-service agents), increasing Average Handle Time by 20–35%

l4_steps.name: Authenticate customer identity
l4_steps.input: Customer-provided name, booking reference, FFP number, or date of birth
l4_steps.output: Identity verification flag set in CRM; authentication level recorded
l4_steps.kpi: Authentication success rate ≥98%; failed authentication escalation rate ≤1%
l4_steps.pain_point: PCI-DSS compliance prohibits agents from handling raw card data; non-FFP member identity verification has no single standard, causing inconsistent agent behaviour and potential fraud exposure

l4_steps.name: Retrieve PNR and loyalty profile from PSS
l4_steps.input: Booking reference or loyalty account number
l4_steps.output: PNR itinerary, fare basis, ticket number, and loyalty tier displayed on agent desktop
l4_steps.kpi: PNR retrieval response time ≤5 seconds; PSS availability ≥99.9%
l4_steps.pain_point: Codeshare or interline itineraries may not surface fully in Altéa; agent must switch to a partner portal or call partner CLC, adding 3–5 minutes per contact

l4_steps.name: Create or update CRM case record
l4_steps.input: Contact reason, PNR details, loyalty profile, channel identifier
l4_steps.output: Case ID created with linked PNR, reason code, channel tag, and priority flag
l4_steps.kpi: Mandatory field completion rate ≥99%; case creation accuracy ≥97%
l4_steps.pain_point: Inconsistent reason-code taxonomy in Salesforce yields corrupted trend reporting; root-cause signals for systemic issues (e.g. baggage carousel failures) go undetected for hours

l4_steps.name: Categorise and diagnose customer issue
l4_steps.input: Customer statement, PNR details, case record, NOC disruption feed
l4_steps.output: Issue category assigned (delay, refund, baggage, loyalty, complaint, IRROP)
l4_steps.kpi: First-call categorisation accuracy ≥90%; misroute rate ≤3%
l4_steps.pain_point: IRROP-related contact spikes arrive before NOC disruption alerts propagate to Salesforce; agents categorise manually without system-side context, slowing diagnosis

l4_steps.name: Apply Tier 1 resolution per service policy
l4_steps.input: Issue category, fare rules from ATPCO, service policy matrix, customer loyalty tier
l4_steps.output: Resolution action determined: rebooking, waiver, information provision, or compensation
l4_steps.kpi: Average Handle Time (AHT) ≤7 minutes; FCR ≥75%
l4_steps.pain_point: Agents must toggle between Altéa and Salesforce with no unified desktop; dual-screen context switching increases AHT by 15–20% and introduces data-entry errors

l4_steps.name: Rebook or modify flight in PSS
l4_steps.input: Customer rebooking preference, available seat inventory, fare rules
l4_steps.output: Revised PNR confirmed; itinerary change notification sent to customer
l4_steps.kpi: Rebooking completion rate ≥95%; change-fee waiver audit compliance 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Involuntary rebooking fare-difference calculations require manual ATPCO fare rule lookup — no automated waiver logic in Altéa — leading to over- or under-collection and regulatory exposure

l4_steps.name: Escalate unresolved case to Tier 2 specialist
l4_steps.input: Unresolved case ID, escalation reason code, full interaction transcript
l4_steps.output: Case warm-transferred with context; Tier 2 specialist assigned and notified
l4_steps.kpi: Escalation rate ≤15%; Tier 2 resolution within 24 hours ≥90%
l4_steps.pain_point: Case context is frequently lost during warm transfers; Tier 2 agents ask customers to repeat information, reducing CSAT by an average of 0.4 points per repeat

l4_steps.name: Assess service recovery compensation eligibility
l4_steps.input: Disruption type and cause, fare class, loyalty tier, EC261/DOT regulation applicability flags
l4_steps.output: Compensation eligibility decision (Y/N); recommended recovery action documented in case
l4_steps.kpi: Compensation decision accuracy ≥98%; EC261 regulatory compliance 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: EC261 applicability for EU-origin flights requires manual legal review — no automated rule engine in Salesforce; agents under volume pressure make incorrect eligibility decisions, creating regulatory liability

l4_steps.name: Issue compensation — miles, voucher, or refund
l4_steps.input: Compensation decision, customer loyalty account, fare paid, voucher policy matrix
l4_steps.output: Miles credited to FFP account, travel voucher issued, or refund initiated in PSS
l4_steps.kpi: Miles crediting accuracy 100%; voucher issuance within 24 hours; DOT-mandated cash refund within 7 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Miles issuance, voucher generation, and PSS refund initiation are in three separate systems with no unified API; dual-entry requirement creates a 2–3% error rate on high-volume disruption days

l4_steps.name: Process policy exception with supervisor approval
l4_steps.input: Agent exception request, case notes, customer loyalty tier and lifetime value
l4_steps.output: Exception approved or denied; case notes updated with justification and supervisor ID
l4_steps.kpi: Exception approval turnaround ≤10 minutes; monthly exception rate tracked as % of total contacts
l4_steps.pain_point: Supervisor approval queue backs up during IRROP events; customers placed on hold >5 minutes, reducing Customer Effort Score (CES) and increasing call abandonment

l4_steps.name: Confirm resolution and close case
l4_steps.input: Resolution actions completed, customer verbal or written confirmation
l4_steps.output: Case status set to Resolved; wrap-up code, resolution notes, and handle time recorded
l4_steps.kpi: Same-day case closure rate ≥85%; after-call work (ACW) time ≤90 seconds
l4_steps.pain_point: Agents under volume pressure skip ACW documentation; incomplete case notes degrade QA coaching effectiveness and root-cause trending by up to 30%

l4_steps.name: Trigger post-contact NPS / CSAT survey
l4_steps.input: Case closed event, customer email or SMS on file, marketing opt-in status
l4_steps.output: CSAT / NPS survey dispatched via email or SMS; response tracked in Medallia dashboard
l4_steps.kpi: Survey response rate ≥20%; NPS ≥45; CSAT ≥4.2/5.0
l4_steps.pain_point: Survey fatigue among frequent flyers who receive multiple survey requests per journey leg; opt-out rate rising 3–5% per quarter, eroding feedback sample size

l4_steps.name: QA review, score, and coach agent
l4_steps.input: Recorded interactions, case notes, CSAT scores, compliance checklist
l4_steps.output: QA scorecard per interaction; coaching flags raised; compliance audit trail maintained
l4_steps.kpi: QA sample rate ≥10% of all contacts; QA score ≥85%; coaching session within 5 business days of flag
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual QA sampling misses systemic issues; AI-assisted speech analytics available in NICE CXone but not fully deployed across all contact types, leaving compliance blind spots

l4_steps.name: Define digital channel scope & use-case catalogue
l4_steps.input: Contact centre volume reports, top-10 call driver analysis from Genesys Cloud CX
l4_steps.output: Approved use-case catalogue listing automatable intents (flight status, rebooking, refund, baggage, check-in)
l4_steps.kpi: Use-case coverage ≥70% of top contact drivers
l4_steps.pain_point: Airlines frequently undercount automatable intents by excluding irregular operations (IRROP) scenarios, leaving high-volume disruption contacts undeflected

l4_steps.name: Configure NLU intents, entities & training utterances
l4_steps.input: Use-case catalogue, historical chat transcripts from Salesforce Service Cloud
l4_steps.output: NLU model with ≥50 utterances per intent, entity extraction rules for PNR, flight number, date, airport code
l4_steps.kpi: Intent recognition accuracy ≥88% in offline evaluation
l4_steps.pain_point: Airline-specific entities (IATA airport codes, fare basis codes, PNR formats) require custom entity extractors not available in generic NLU libraries; training data is sparse for low-frequency intents

l4_steps.name: Set containment thresholds & escalation routing rules
l4_steps.input: NLU confidence score ranges, queue capacity SLAs, skills-based routing matrix
l4_steps.output: Escalation policy: confidence <0.70 → clarification prompt; <0.55 → live agent; authenticated transaction failure → priority queue
l4_steps.kpi: Mis-escalation rate <5% (contacts escalated that chatbot could have resolved)
l4_steps.pain_point: Overly aggressive confidence thresholds during IRROP events flood live agent queues; Genesys routing rules require manual override during declared irregular operations

l4_steps.name: UAT regression test chatbot flows & approve release
l4_steps.input: Configured NLU model, test script covering all use-case catalogue scenarios including exception paths
l4_steps.output: UAT sign-off report; failed flows returned to step 1.2 for remediation
l4_steps.kpi: UAT pass rate ≥95% across all intent test cases before prod deployment
l4_steps.pain_point: Regression testing is manual and time-consuming; no automated test harness exists for end-to-end chatbot + PSS API integration paths, increasing release cycle to 3–4 weeks

l4_steps.name: Receive & parse inbound digital interaction
l4_steps.input: Customer message via web chat, mobile app, WhatsApp Business API, or Facebook Messenger
l4_steps.output: Normalised interaction record with channel source, session ID, timestamp, and raw utterance
l4_steps.kpi: Channel availability ≥99.9% uptime; median response latency <800 ms
l4_steps.pain_point: WhatsApp Business API throughput is capped by Meta rate limits during high-demand periods (e.g., weather events); fallback to web chat is not seamlessly communicated to passengers

l4_steps.name: Classify intent & extract booking / loyalty entities
l4_steps.input: Normalised customer utterance
l4_steps.output: Top intent label with confidence score, extracted entities (PNR, flight number, date, loyalty tier)
l4_steps.kpi: Live intent accuracy ≥85%; confidence score logged for every interaction
l4_steps.pain_point: Code-switching (multilingual passengers mixing English with Spanish or Portuguese) degrades CCAI intent accuracy by 10–15%; no per-language model version management currently in place

l4_steps.name: Authenticate customer for transactional self-service
l4_steps.input: Customer-supplied PNR + last name, or loyalty member ID + PIN via Salesforce Service Cloud identity service
l4_steps.output: Authenticated session token; customer profile (booking history, loyalty tier, contact preferences) retrieved
l4_steps.kpi: Authentication success rate ≥92% on first attempt; failed auth rate <3%
l4_steps.pain_point: Passengers frequently misquote 6-character PNR (alpha-numeric confusion); Altéa PSS timeout during peak load causes auth failures that appear as customer errors, inflating escalation rate

l4_steps.name: Execute self-service task via PSS & loyalty APIs
l4_steps.input: Authenticated session, validated intent (rebooking, refund request, seat selection, check-in, baggage add-on, flight status)
l4_steps.output: Transaction confirmation (new PNR, refund reference, boarding pass, baggage receipt) or structured error response
l4_steps.kpi: Self-service transaction completion rate ≥80% for eligible intents; API error rate <1%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS fare recalculation during voluntary rebooking via API does not always honour same-day change waiver rules, causing incorrect fare difference charges that require manual agent correction

l4_steps.name: Detect escalation trigger & package conversation context
l4_steps.input: CCAI confidence score below threshold, customer explicit escalation request ("speak to agent"), or transaction API failure flag
l4_steps.output: Escalation event with full conversation transcript, intent history, authentication status, and customer tier
l4_steps.kpi: Context transfer completeness ≥98% (no dropped transcripts); escalation routing latency <5 s
l4_steps.pain_point: During IRROP events, simultaneous escalation spikes overwhelm Genesys routing capacity; lack of dynamic queue prioritisation means high-value (elite tier) passengers wait alongside general queue

l4_steps.name: Route escalation to live agent by skill & priority
l4_steps.input: Escalation event, agent skill matrix (language, fare complexity, loyalty tier authorisation), real-time queue depth
l4_steps.output: Agent assignment with conversation context pre-loaded in Salesforce Service Cloud agent console
