l4_steps.kpi: Average speed to answer (ASA) for escalated contacts <90 s; first-contact resolution ≥75%
l4_steps.pain_point: Skills-based routing matrix requires manual update when agents are cross-trained; stale routing tables during shift changes cause mis-routing and repeat transfers

l4_steps.name: Agent reviews transcript & resumes resolution
l4_steps.input: Full chatbot transcript, customer profile (PNR, loyalty tier, prior cases), CCAI-suggested resolution from agent assist
l4_steps.output: Case updated in Salesforce; resolution actioned in Amadeus Altéa PSS (rebooking, waiver, compensation)
l4_steps.kpi: Agent handle time for escalated digital contacts <8 min; re-open rate <5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Agents frequently restart from scratch when CCAI transcript is truncated or context payload exceeds Salesforce Service Cloud screen-pop character limit, negating chatbot deflection savings

l4_steps.name: Ingest low-confidence & failed interaction logs
l4_steps.input: Daily CCAI interaction logs exported via Genesys Data Actions; confidence scores, unmatched utterances, fallback counts
l4_steps.output: Curated dataset of misclassified and unresolved intents ranked by volume and customer impact
l4_steps.kpi: Log ingestion SLA <24 h post-interaction; coverage 100% of chatbot sessions
l4_steps.pain_point: CCAI logs are stored in raw JSON requiring ETL transformation before analysis; no real-time intent failure alerting exists, meaning new failure patterns go undetected for 24–48 h

l4_steps.name: Update training utterances & FAQ knowledge content
l4_steps.input: Prioritised intent gap list, agent feedback on frequently asked questions, product/policy change notifications
l4_steps.output: Updated intent training dataset uploaded to CCAI; revised FAQ articles published in Salesforce Knowledge
l4_steps.kpi: Knowledge article freshness: 100% reviewed within 30 days of policy change; new utterances ≥20 per reclassified intent
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated trigger connects policy change management (e.g., baggage fee updates, new fare rules) to knowledge base update workflow; stale FAQ content causes chatbot to quote superseded policies

l4_steps.name: Retrain, validate & promote NLU model to production
l4_steps.input: Updated training dataset, baseline model accuracy benchmarks from last release
l4_steps.output: Validated NLU model version; A/B test report comparing new vs. current model on held-out test set
l4_steps.kpi: New model accuracy ≥baseline +2%; no regression on existing intents; staging validation pass rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: CCAI model versioning is not integrated with airline CI/CD pipeline; manual promotion steps increase risk of deploying untested models to production, with no instant rollback capability

l4_steps.name: Monitor containment rate, CSAT & escalation KPIs
l4_steps.input: Genesys Cloud CX interaction data, Medallia post-interaction CSAT survey results, AWS Redshift chatbot analytics
l4_steps.output: Weekly digital channel performance dashboard: containment rate, CSAT, escalation rate, top unresolved intents
l4_steps.kpi: Chatbot containment rate ≥65%; digital CSAT ≥4.0/5.0; escalation rate <35%
l4_steps.pain_point: Containment rate calculation methodology varies between Genesys and CCAI reporting, creating discrepancies of 5–8 percentage points that obscure true self-service performance

l4_steps.name: Identify intent gaps & journey abandonment patterns
l4_steps.input: Tableau dashboard KPI alerts, session path analysis, drop-off rates by intent and step
l4_steps.output: Root-cause analysis report identifying top 5 intent gaps and highest-abandonment journey points
l4_steps.kpi: Journey abandonment rate <15% per intent flow; report produced within 5 business days of KPI breach
l4_steps.pain_point: Session-level journey analytics require joining Genesys session IDs with CCAI interaction IDs and Salesforce case IDs — three separate identity namespaces with no unified customer journey ID

l4_steps.name: Prioritise & schedule chatbot enhancement backlog
l4_steps.input: Root-cause analysis report, capacity estimates from Conversational AI Engineering team, commercial priority from Revenue Management
l4_steps.output: Prioritised enhancement backlog in Confluence; sprint plan for next NLU model training cycle (step 1.2)
l4_steps.kpi: Backlog groomed and sprint-planned within 10 business days of KPI breach; enhancement cycle ≤6 weeks end-to-end
l4_steps.pain_point: Enhancement prioritisation is often driven by loudest stakeholder rather than quantified passenger impact; lack of a shared ROI model (cost-per-contact avoided) means high-value deflection improvements are deprioritised

l4_steps.name: Retrieve active flight plan from flight planning system
l4_steps.input: Scheduled departure, route database, aircraft tail assignment
l4_steps.output: Draft Operational Flight Plan (OFP) with route, altitude, and estimated fuel
l4_steps.kpi: Flight plan available ≥60 min before STD; plan accuracy within ±2% of actual fuel burn
l4_steps.pain_point: NAVBLUE integration latency with ATC slot data can delay plan finalization for constrained airspace; manual re-route required for TFR-affected corridors

l4_steps.name: Pull METAR, TAF, SIGMET and PIREP weather data
l4_steps.input: Departure, destination, and alternate ICAO codes; planned departure time
l4_steps.output: Consolidated weather package including en-route SIGMET and PIREP overlays
l4_steps.kpi: Weather package delivered ≤45 min before STD; SIGMET currency ≤6 hrs
l4_steps.pain_point: SIGMETs for en-route convection update every 4–6 hrs; late-breaking convective SIGMETs may not be captured before release window, requiring mid-dispatch reassessment

l4_steps.name: Assess weather at origin, destination and alternate
l4_steps.input: Weather package, airline published operating minima, alternate requirements
l4_steps.output: Weather go/no-go recommendation with alternate aerodrome confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Destination forecast visibility and ceiling at or above published CAT I/II/III minima at ETA
l4_steps.pain_point: Rapid deterioration below CAT II minima at destination with simultaneous weather impact on primary alternate forces late alternate change, disrupting fuel calculation and ATC filing

l4_steps.name: Calculate fuel uplift including contingency and alternate
l4_steps.input: Route fuel burn, wind data, alternate distance, company fuel policy, EDCT delay estimate
l4_steps.output: Minimum regulatory fuel figure plus discretionary uplift recommendation
l4_steps.kpi: Planned fuel ≥ FAR 121.645 / ICAO Annex 6 minimum (trip + 5% contingency + alternate + 30 min final reserve); fuel overage ≤3% of trip fuel
l4_steps.pain_point: EDCT ground delay burn estimates from FAA TFMS are systematically optimistic; dispatcher must manually add 10–15% buffer for GDP-affected departures, yet excess uplift increases fuel cost by ~$8/kg

l4_steps.name: File IFR flight plan with ATC via AFTN/SITA
l4_steps.input: Finalized OFP route, departure time, aircraft type and registration, SELCAL
l4_steps.output: Filed FPL message (ICAO format) acknowledged by ATC; filing receipt stored
l4_steps.kpi: Flight plan filed ≥30 min before EOBT; filing acknowledgment received ≤5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: EUROCONTROL NM slot allocation (CTOT) can force departure time change ≤2 hrs before departure, requiring immediate re-file and downstream fuel/crew duty recalculation

l4_steps.name: Confirm ATC slot/EDCT and assess crew duty impact
l4_steps.input: Filed FPL, GDP/AFP program data, crew duty time records from Jeppesen Crew Management
l4_steps.output: Confirmed CTOT/EDCT, updated STD, crew duty compliance confirmation
l4_steps.kpi: EDCT compliance rate ≥98%; crew duty limit breach rate <0.5% of dispatched flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Ground Delay Programs (GDPs) can shift EDCT by 60–180 min, pushing ATD past crew rest trigger thresholds under FAR Part 117; late crew swap triggers cascading downstream cancellations

l4_steps.name: Select and file alternate aerodrome with fuel coverage
l4_steps.input: Destination TAF, alternate airport ops and NOTAM status, fuel range envelope
l4_steps.output: Filed alternate ICAO code with calculated alternate fuel and regulatory compliance confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Alternate meets FAR 121.619 one-hour TAF forecast above alternate minima at ETA ±1 hr
l4_steps.pain_point: Popular alternates (e.g. ORD when MDW is destination) can become simultaneously weather-affected; dispatcher must identify second-order alternates increasing fuel requirement and potentially triggering MTOW constraint

l4_steps.name: Check aircraft airworthiness status in MRO system
l4_steps.input: Tail number, scheduled departure, inbound tech log entries
l4_steps.output: Airworthiness confirmation or open deferred defect list with MEL references
l4_steps.kpi: Aircraft status confirmed ≥90 min before STD; zero open airworthiness directives beyond MEL tolerance
l4_steps.pain_point: Late squawks logged by inbound crew within 45 min of departure may not propagate to AMOS before the dispatch review window closes, creating undocumented MEL exposure

l4_steps.name: Review MEL and CDL items for dispatch acceptability
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware + Boeing Toolbox
l4_steps.input: Open deferred defects, current MEL/CDL revision, route and operating conditions
l4_steps.output: MEL dispatch determination (go/no-go) with any operational restrictions documented
l4_steps.kpi: MEL review completed ≤60 min before STD; zero dispatches with expired MEL interval items
l4_steps.pain_point: Cat B/C MEL items may impose altitude, fuel, or route restrictions that are not automatically propagated to NAVBLUE OFP, requiring manual dispatcher override and re-calculation

l4_steps.name: Verify V-speeds and performance for current configuration
l4_steps.input: Aircraft weight, MEL-driven configuration restrictions, runway condition report (SNOWTAM/RCR)
l4_steps.output: Confirmed V1/VR/V2, flap setting, derate selection, and balanced field length
l4_steps.kpi: Performance calculations completed ≤45 min before STD; all V-speeds within aircraft flight manual limits
l4_steps.pain_point: Contaminated runway friction coefficients (SNOWTAM data) may be up to 2 hrs old; dispatcher must verify runway treatment status with station ops before confirming RTOW, as stale data can overstate runway performance by 8–12%

l4_steps.name: Receive preliminary load figures from load control
l4_steps.input: Booked passenger count, checked baggage manifest, cargo booking, crew count
l4_steps.output: Preliminary Zero Fuel Weight (ZFW) and estimated Takeoff Weight (TOW)
l4_steps.kpi: Preliminary load sheet received ≥60 min before STD; ZFW variance from final ≤500 lbs
l4_steps.pain_point: Late connecting passengers and ad-hoc cargo add-ons can shift ZFW by 500–2,000 lbs after the initial fuel calculation, invalidating the filed fuel figure and requiring dispatch release amendment

l4_steps.name: Calculate final takeoff weight and CG envelope
l4_steps.input: Final passenger count, actual baggage weights by zone, hold cargo manifest, ballast
l4_steps.output: Final load sheet with confirmed TOW, ZFW, CG position as percentage of MAC
l4_steps.kpi: CG within ±2% MAC of certified envelope limits; TOW ≤ MTOW; load sheet issued ≤40 min before STD
l4_steps.pain_point: Bulk cargo density variances and last-minute bag pulls can cause CG exceedance not detected until ramp loading check, requiring hold reload that delays departure by 20–45 min

l4_steps.name: Perform runway-limited weight and obstacle clearance check
l4_steps.input: Final TOW, runway conditions, OAT, pressure altitude, obstacle departure procedure
l4_steps.output: Confirmed Regulated Takeoff Weight (RTOW), required field length, net takeoff flight path
l4_steps.kpi: Net takeoff flight path clears obstacles by ≥35 ft per FAR 121.189; RTOW ≥ actual TOW
l4_steps.pain_point: High-elevation airports (DEN 5,431 ft, SLC 4,227 ft) combined with high OAT frequently trigger weight restrictions that were not anticipated in the original schedule, forcing payload offload decisions at gate

l4_steps.name: Generate Operational Flight Plan and dispatch release
l4_steps.input: Final fuel uplift, confirmed load sheet, MEL notes, weather package, NOTAM summary
l4_steps.output: Completed Operational Flight Plan (OFP) and unsigned Dispatch Release document
l4_steps.kpi: OFP issued ≥30 min before EOBT; NOTAM safety-critical items highlighted in release
l4_steps.pain_point: NOTAM volumes at major hubs can exceed 150 active NOTAMs per airport; dispatcher must manually filter safety-critical items, creating fatigue-driven oversight risk without automated NOTAM triage tooling

l4_steps.name: Brief Captain on route, weather, NOTAMs and MEL status
l4_steps.system: SITA ACARS / Telex (or face-to-face at hub)
l4_steps.input: OFP, weather package, NOTAM summary, MEL items, EDCT/CTOT, fuel figure
l4_steps.output: Completed crew briefing record with dispatcher and captain acknowledgement
l4_steps.kpi: Crew briefing completed ≥20 min before EOBT; briefing acknowledgment logged in dispatch system
l4_steps.pain_point: At remote outstations, dispatcher-captain contact via ACARS can be disrupted by ground power failures; fallback to VHF voice briefing must be documented under FAR 121.663 joint responsibility

l4_steps.name: Captain reviews and co-signs Dispatch Release (FAR 121.663)
l4_steps.system: SITA ACARS (electronic signature) or paper release
l4_steps.input: Dispatch Release document, OFP, fuel order, weather and NOTAM briefing package
l4_steps.output: Dual-signed Dispatch Release (dispatcher + captain) confirming joint airworthiness decision
l4_steps.kpi: Release co-signed ≤15 min before EOBT; 100% of departures have dual-signed release on file
l4_steps.pain_point: Under FAR 121, dispatch is a joint captain-dispatcher decision; captain fuel uplift amendments after signing trigger full release re-issue, consuming 10–20 min and risking EDCT miss

l4_steps.name: Issue final dispatch release and transmit to crew
l4_steps.input: Co-signed Dispatch Release, confirmed fuel order, updated departure time
l4_steps.output: Transmitted final release; flight authorized to depart; release archived in dispatch system
l4_steps.kpi: Release transmitted ≥10 min before EOBT; 100% compliance; ACARS delivery confirmation within 2 min
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS datalink failures at remote outstations require fallback to voice release per FAR 121.663; voice releases must be manually transcribed and archived, creating audit trail gaps if not logged within 1 hr

l4_steps.name: Monitor departure, pushback and initial climb confirmation
l4_steps.input: ATC off-blocks clearance, pushback notification from ramp, ACARS OUT message
l4_steps.output: Confirmed actual off-blocks time (AOBT); flight tracker status updated to airborne
l4_steps.kpi: AOBT recorded within 2 min of actual event; D0 (on-time departure) target ≥78%
l4_steps.pain_point: AMS/Altéa PSS timestamp synchronization errors can misreport AOBT by 3–8 min, causing downstream crew duty time calculations to use incorrect start-of-duty reference under FAR Part 117

l4_steps.name: Track flight en-route via ACARS position reports
l4_steps.input: Automatic ACARS position reports (15-min intervals), ATC radar handoff confirmations
l4_steps.output: Updated ETA, fuel-remaining trend, en-route deviation log, revised destination weather check
l4_steps.kpi: Position report gap ≤15 min; fuel remaining vs. plan within ±500 lbs at each waypoint
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS blackout over oceanic tracks (no VHF/SATCOM backup) leaves dispatcher without real-time fuel data for up to 60 min; oceanic fuel emergencies cannot be detected until HF radio contact is re-established

l4_steps.name: Initiate diversion or emergency response if required
l4_steps.input: In-flight emergency notification, medical diversion request, fuel emergency, weather deterioration below minima
l4_steps.output: Diversion airport selected with fuel coverage confirmed; ATC coordination initiated; ground support activated at diversion airport
l4_steps.kpi: Diversion decision communicated to crew ≤5 min from trigger event; ground support activated ≤15 min before ETA at diversion
l4_steps.pain_point: Diversion airports at unplanned stations may lack MEL-required spare parts or certified line maintenance capability, extending AOG time by 4–24 hrs and triggering cascading schedule disruption across the network

l4_steps.name: Receive OFP computation trigger from schedule
l4_steps.input: Confirmed flight schedule event (STD, flight number, aircraft registration) published by network scheduling system
l4_steps.output: OFP computation job queued in flight planning system with flight parameters loaded
l4_steps.kpi: OFP computation initiated ≥3 hrs before STD; 100% of flights have confirmed OFP before T-90 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Late aircraft swaps or gate changes in Altéa trigger cascading OFP recomputations; absence of real-time webhook integration between Altéa and NAVBLUE forces manual re-triggers, creating a 10–20 min dispatcher workload spike per swap event

l4_steps.name: Extract aircraft type, reg, and ZFW estimate
l4_steps.input: Flight number, STD, aircraft registration, confirmed bookings, preliminary cargo manifest
l4_steps.output: Aircraft type/registration confirmed, preliminary PAX count, planned Zero Fuel Weight (ZFW) estimate
l4_steps.kpi: Preliminary ZFW within ±2% of final ZFW to ensure accurate early fuel computation
l4_steps.pain_point: Early-trigger OFPs (T-12 hr) carry highly uncertain load estimates; late check-in surges force ZFW and fuel recomputation within the T-1 hr window, causing ramp delays and re-fuelling events that average 18 min delay per occurrence

l4_steps.name: Pull upper-wind, weather, and SIGMET data
l4_steps.input: Route waypoints, planned flight levels, estimated departure time
l4_steps.output: Upper-wind grid data (GRIB2), active SIGMETs/AIRMETs, convective forecast and icing outlook along planned route
l4_steps.kpi: Weather data refresh cycle ≤1 hr before STD; SIGMET coverage 100% of planned route corridor
l4_steps.pain_point: GoDirect data ingestion latency vs. real-time MWO (Meteorological Watch Office) SIGMET issuance can leave a 30–45 min gap for fast-moving convective systems; legacy dispatch integrations without automated SIGMET push alerts rely on dispatcher manual polling

l4_steps.name: Compute CI-optimised route — NAVBLUE
l4_steps.input: O&D city pair, aircraft performance model, upper-wind GRIB2 data, airline cost index (CI) policy
l4_steps.output: Optimised ICAO route string, estimated time en route (ETE), planned FL step-climb profile, preliminary trip fuel
l4_steps.kpi: Fuel saving vs. fixed routing ≥1.2% per flight; cost index adherence to fleet policy (CI 20–35 narrow-body); computation time ≤90 sec
l4_steps.pain_point: Aircraft performance model currency is a persistent risk — NAVBLUE performance database must be synced with aircraft modification records from AMOS; unrecorded winglet upgrades or engine modifications cause model accuracy drift of up to 0.8% fuel burn, skewing fleet-wide efficiency analytics

l4_steps.name: Calculate trip, contingency, alternate, and reserve fuel
l4_steps.input: NAVBLUE trip fuel output, alternate aerodrome distance and forecast, contingency policy (5% or fixed-minute rule), company extra fuel policy
l4_steps.output: Full fuel breakdown: trip fuel, contingency fuel, alternate fuel, final reserve (30-min FAR 121 / ICAO Annex 6), additional company fuel, total fuel order (kg)
l4_steps.kpi: Actual vs. planned fuel burn variance ≤±3%; zero-fuel-on-arrival (ZFOA) rate <0.1% of flights
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 91/121 domestic alternate fuel rules differ from ICAO Annex 6 international rules; carriers operating trans-border routes must maintain dual rule-sets in NAVBLUE configuration — version drift during software updates causes compliance risk and has triggered FAA Letter of Investigation (LOI) actions at US carriers

l4_steps.name: Validate fuel order within MTOW and structural limits
l4_steps.input: Total fuel order (kg), ZFW estimate from Altéa, aircraft MTOW for registration and airport elevation/temperature
l4_steps.output: Go/no-go decision for current routing; if MTOW exceeded, payload reduction request issued to Load Control or route adjusted to reduce trip fuel
l4_steps.kpi: MTOW exceedance rate 0% (hard regulatory limit); fuel reduction iteration cycles ≤2 per flight before escalation
l4_steps.pain_point: High summer temperatures (ISA+15°C or above) at hot/high airports (PHX, DEN, LAS) significantly reduce MTOW-limited payload; NAVBLUE does not provide automated MTOW-constrained route re-optimisation — dispatchers perform manual iteration, averaging 4 additional minutes per constrained flight

l4_steps.name: Filter and review NOTAMs for route and aerodromes
l4_steps.input: Route waypoints, departure/destination/alternate ICAO codes, ETD
l4_steps.output: Filtered NOTAM briefing package with operationally significant NOTAMs highlighted; ILS/approach procedure NOTAMs and runway closure NOTAMs flagged for captain attention
l4_steps.kpi: Dispatcher NOTAM review time ≤8 min per flight; Type I/II NOTAM inclusion rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: NOTAM data quality is a persistent industry problem — free-text, unstructured NOTAMs from certain states require manual parsing; Jeppesen Smart NOTAM keyword filtering reduces volume but has suppressed safety-critical items when taxonomy files are not updated after ICAO format revisions (ICAO Doc 8126 Annex 15 transition 2023)

l4_steps.name: Check ATFM flow programmes and special use airspace
l4_steps.system: FAA TFMS (Traffic Flow Management System) / EUROCONTROL CFMU NM
l4_steps.input: Filed route string, ETD, altitude profile, departure airport capacity programme status
l4_steps.output: Active Ground Delay Programmes (GDPs), Ground Stops (GS), Airspace Flow Programmes (AFP) applicable to flight identified; special use airspace (SUA/TFR) conflicts on route assessed
l4_steps.kpi: ATFM programme impact assessment completed ≥2 hr before STD; SUA conflict detection rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA TFMS GDP data is refreshed every 15–30 min; dispatchers using static NAVBLUE routing miss late-issued GDPs and incur unplanned EDCT delays at departure; military SUA activation in the Gulf of Mexico MOA complex is issued with <1 hr notice, invalidating already-filed ATC FPLs

l4_steps.name: Validate route is clear of restrictions and ATFM conflicts
l4_steps.input: NOTAM flags, SUA/TFR overlap results, applicable GDP/AFP programme constraints
l4_steps.output: Route approved or rerouted alternative generated; if rerouted, OFP recomputed from step 2.1
l4_steps.kpi: Reroute rate due to late SUA/flow conflicts <2% of flights; reroute cycle time (detection to new FPL) ≤12 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Military SUA activation notices (NOTAMs for ranges like W-151, W-168 Gulf ops) can arrive within 45 min of ETD, requiring an emergency reroute that bypasses normal NAVBLUE optimisation and may add 80–150 kg fuel burn on affected sectors

l4_steps.name: File ICAO FPL with ATC via SITA AFTN datalink
l4_steps.input: Completed OFP route string, ETD, ICAO equipment suffix, SELCAL code, aircraft registration, crew identifiers
l4_steps.output: ICAO FPL (format per ICAO Doc 4444 PANS-ATM) transmitted to ATC; ACK or CHG response received and logged
l4_steps.kpi: FPL filed ≥60 min before STD (FAR 91.169 / ICAO Annex 2 requirement); FPL acceptance rate (ACK without CHG) ≥94%
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AFTN message queuing during peak traffic windows (0600–0900 hub banks) adds 5–12 min filing latency; rejected FPLs (CHG messages) require manual field correction and re-filing, consuming 8–15 min of dispatcher time and compressing the pre-departure preparation window

l4_steps.name: Assess EDCT/CTOT slot assignment from ATFM authority
l4_steps.system: FAA TFMS / EUROCONTROL CFMU NM Portal
l4_steps.input: Filed FPL, active GDP/AFP programme data, departure airport acceptance rate
l4_steps.output: EDCT (Expect Departure Clearance Time) or CTOT issued and recorded; or no-restriction confirmation logged
l4_steps.kpi: EDCT compliance rate ≥98%; average ATFM delay per affected flight <8 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Multiple overlapping GDPs (destination GDP + en-route AFP simultaneously) create conflicting EDCT windows that TFMS cannot always auto-resolve; dispatchers must manually arbitrate priority — a process with no formal FAA guidance, leading to inconsistent outcomes across carriers

l4_steps.name: Negotiate slot relief or reroute via AOC coordination
l4_steps.system: FAA TFMS Flight Schedule Monitor (FSM) + EUROCONTROL CFMU NM Portal
l4_steps.input: Assigned EDCT/CTOT, crew duty time remaining, downstream connection passenger count, slot swap availability
l4_steps.output: Slot swap approval or alternate routing clearance granted; updated ETD recorded on OFP; crew notified via ACARS
l4_steps.kpi: Slot relief request success rate ≥30% of attempts; crew duty limit infringement due to ATFM delay <0.5% of flights
l4_steps.pain_point: FSM slot-swap portal requires AOC login and a dedicated coordinator — carriers without 24/7 AOC staffing (regional partners, red-eye operations) accept EDCT passively and absorb avoidable delays averaging 22 min per event

l4_steps.name: Generate and transmit OFP package to crew EFB
l4_steps.input: Finalised OFP, fuel order, NOTAM briefing package, weather package, current ATIS
l4_steps.output: Complete OFP briefing packet transmitted to crew EFB via ACARS datalink; delivery acknowledgement logged
l4_steps.kpi: OFP delivery to EFB ≥T-60 min before STD; datalink transmission success rate ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: NAVBLUE and Jeppesen FliteDeck EFB require matching document schema versions; version mismatches between aircraft EFB software (often on a slower certification update cycle) and NAVBLUE OFP output format cause rendering failures — crews revert to printed paper fallback, adding 10–15 min to pre-departure preparation

l4_steps.name: Captain reviews OFP fuel, route, and alternates on EFB
l4_steps.input: OFP package including fuel breakdown, route, alternates, NOTAM briefing, weather charts
l4_steps.output: Captain review complete; fuel acceptance confirmed or additional fuel request raised with dispatcher
l4_steps.kpi: Captain OFP review time ≤15 min; OFP acceptance without fuel change ≥82% of flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Captains on specific high-variability route segments (mountain wave, oceanic NAT) routinely add conservative discretionary fuel above company minima due to low confidence in NAVBLUE model accuracy on those segments — creates 0.3–0.8% fuel burn inefficiency per sector and can push TOW toward MTOW limits on weight-critical flights

l4_steps.name: Resolve captain commander's discretion fuel request
l4_steps.input: Captain's discretionary fuel request (kg), current planned fuel breakdown, MTOW headroom, ramp fuel availability
l4_steps.output: Agreed final fuel quantity; revised fuel order transmitted to ramp fuelling team; updated TOW confirmed within MTOW
l4_steps.kpi: Commander's discretion fuel (CDF) additions >200 kg rate <18% of flights; MTOW exceedance from CDF uplift 0%
l4_steps.pain_point: No structured data capture of CDF rationale in NAVBLUE or FliteDeck — inability to retrospectively analyse CDF patterns by route, captain, or weather condition prevents fuel policy refinement and limits regulatory evidence-gathering under ICAO Annex 6 / EU-OPS ORO.MLR.101 fuel documentation requirements

l4_steps.name: Monitor en-route fuel burn via ACARS position reports
l4_steps.input: ACARS ADS-C/ADS-B position reports with fuel on board (FOB) transmission, OFP fuel plan profile
l4_steps.output: Real-time fuel burn comparison vs. OFP plan; trend line for fuel state at destination and alternate
l4_steps.kpi: Fuel monitoring update interval ≤15 min oceanic / ≤5 min domestic; fuel deviation alert threshold ±5% of plan
l4_steps.pain_point: ADS-C oceanic position reports over HF/SATCOM on North Atlantic and Pacific tracks have 10–30 min latency; dispatchers cannot confirm fuel state in real time for ETOPS critical fuel scenarios and rely on crew self-reporting — a single-point-of-failure monitoring model that increases diversion initiation latency when fuel deviation occurs

l4_steps.name: Assess fuel deviation and issue diversion recommendation
l4_steps.input: ACARS FOB report, computed fuel remaining from OFP, alternate fuel requirement, destination weather update
l4_steps.output: Continue-as-planned confirmation or fuel advisory message to crew; diversion recommendation issued if destination fuel falls below alternate + final reserve requirement
l4_steps.kpi: Fuel emergency declaration rate (MAYDAY FUEL / PAN PAN FUEL) <0.01% of flights; diversion for fuel exhaustion <0.05% of flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Dispatcher authority to recommend diversion is legally advisory-only under FAR 121.533; PIC has final authority, but late-stage diversions after dispatcher flags critical fuel state incur $40K–$120K IROPS cost per event — absence of a shared decision-making protocol between crew and dispatcher increases initiation latency by an average of 8 min

l4_steps.name: Close flight plan and record actuals in data lake
l4_steps.system: NAVBLUE + Amadeus Altéa PSS + AWS Redshift
l4_steps.input: ACARS actual time of arrival (ATA), final fuel on board at blocks-on, en-route amendment log, uplift confirmation
l4_steps.output: Flight plan closed with ATC; actual fuel burn, block time, and route deviations recorded in airline data lake for performance analytics
l4_steps.kpi: Flight plan closure within 30 min of ATA (ICAO Doc 4444 requirement); fuel burn data capture rate 100% for post-flight analytics
l4_steps.pain_point: NAVBLUE actuals data is not natively streamed to the airline data lake; a manual export or scheduled ETL pipeline introduces 4–12 hr latency before actuals reach AWS Redshift — preventing same-day fuel efficiency feedback loops and delaying monthly CORSIA fuel reporting submissions

l4_steps.name: Ingest flight plan, route & forecast winds
l4_steps.input: Active OFP, SIGMET/AIRMET, upper-wind forecast (NWP model)
l4_steps.output: Route profile with fuel-burn model loaded; wind data timestamp recorded
l4_steps.kpi: Wind data currency ≤ 6 hours before STD; 100% OFP retrieval success rate
l4_steps.pain_point: NWP upper-wind refresh is 6-hourly; stale data can inflate or underestimate trip fuel by 2–4%, with no automatic dispatcher alert when forecast age exceeds threshold

l4_steps.name: Calculate trip fuel, alternate & final reserve
l4_steps.input: Route profile, aircraft type/registration, payload estimate, alternate airport selection
l4_steps.output: Trip fuel, alternate fuel, and final reserve fuel (FRF) values in USG/kg
l4_steps.kpi: Fuel calculation accuracy ±1% vs. actual block burn; alternate fuel covers closest suitable alternate per ops spec
l4_steps.pain_point: Aircraft performance deck must be updated after each engine shop visit or EFW change; stale performance model causes systematic over/under-fuelling accumulating to 0.5–1% fuel cost variance fleet-wide

l4_steps.name: Apply regulatory minimum fuel policy
l4_steps.input: Trip fuel, alternate fuel, FRF; ETOPS/EDTO authorisation if applicable; company fuel policy
l4_steps.output: Regulatory minimum block fuel (FAR 121.639 / ICAO Annex 6 compliant); ETOPS ERA fuel added where required
l4_steps.kpi: 100% regulatory compliance; zero dispatches with sub-minimum fuel on record
l4_steps.pain_point: ETOPS 180-min routes require En-Route Alternate (ERA) fuel that must be recalculated if the ERA changes post-OFP publication due to NOTAM or weather; no automated re-trigger in Lido when ERA status changes after release

l4_steps.name: Validate fuel load against MTOW & payload limits
l4_steps.system: Lido/Flight by Lufthansa Systems + Weight & Balance System
l4_steps.input: Planned fuel load, estimated payload (pax + cargo + mail), aircraft MTOW/MLW/MZFW limits
l4_steps.output: Approved fuel quantum; or payload-fuel trade decision with affected bookings flagged
l4_steps.kpi: Revenue payload protection ≥ 95% of booked payload on MTOW-limited sectors
l4_steps.pain_point: MTOW-limited flights at hot/high airports (e.g. LAS in summer, BOG year-round) force late payload offload; no automated interface between Lido and PSS to surface the constraint earlier in the booking cycle

l4_steps.name: Query into-plane fuel prices at origin & destination
l4_steps.system: Aviator Fuel Intelligence (AvFuel) / SAP S/4HANA Finance (FI/CO)
l4_steps.input: Flight date, origin/destination ICAO codes, fuel supplier contract references
l4_steps.output: Into-plane fuel price per USG/kg at origin and destination; contract vs. spot price flagged
l4_steps.kpi: Price data latency ≤ 24 hours; contract uplift preference achieved ≥ 95% of uplifts
l4_steps.pain_point: Fuel price APIs from major suppliers (BP, Shell, World Fuel Services) vary in latency and data format; feed outages require manual extraction from supplier portals, creating price data gaps that default the model to stale contract rates

l4_steps.name: Model tankering NPV versus weight penalty cost
l4_steps.system: Aviator Fuel Intelligence (AvFuel) / Lido/Flight by Lufthansa Systems
l4_steps.input: Price differential (origin vs. destination), extra fuel weight, aircraft fuel-burn profile at gross weight
l4_steps.output: Net tankering value in USD per flight; break-even uplift quantity identified
l4_steps.kpi: Tankering model accuracy: positive NPV realised ≥ 90% of cases where model predicted benefit > $150
l4_steps.pain_point: Weight-penalty calculation in simplified models assumes linear burn increase, but penalty is non-linear at high gross weights; simplified model can overstate tankering benefit by 5–10% on heavy flights, leading to sub-optimal decisions

l4_steps.name: Approve or reject tankering uplift quantity
l4_steps.input: Tankering NPV, aircraft structural maximum fuel load, available turnaround time, payload outlook
l4_steps.output: Approved tankering quantity (USG) or 'No tankering' decision recorded with rationale
l4_steps.kpi: Tankering uplift decision issued ≥ 90 minutes before STD; decisions documented 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Late payload additions (ULD cargo, late-checked bags) post-tankering approval can invalidate the approved quantity; no automated re-trigger of the tankering model when payload changes after OFP release, requiring manual analyst intervention

l4_steps.name: Finalise planned uplift quantity on OFP
l4_steps.input: Regulatory minimum fuel, tankering decision, captain's discretionary fuel allowance (if pre-authorised)
l4_steps.output: Final planned uplift quantity on signed OFP; fuel release document generated
l4_steps.kpi: Planned vs. actual uplift variance ≤ 2%; OFP fuel release issued ≥ 60 minutes before STD
l4_steps.pain_point: Dispatcher discretionary fuel additions above plan are not consistently documented with a rationale code; absence of structured data makes post-flight fuel efficiency analysis unreliable and prevents feedback into planning model to reduce systematic under-planning

l4_steps.name: Transmit fuel release order to into-plane supplier
l4_steps.input: Fuel release document: planned uplift quantity, aircraft registration, parking stand, STD
l4_steps.output: Fuel order transmitted; supplier acknowledgement received with ETA
l4_steps.kpi: Order transmitted ≥ 60 minutes before fuelling start; supplier ACK received ≤ 15 minutes of transmission
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA FuelsManager integration is absent at smaller outstations, requiring manual phone or fax orders; gaps in electronic audit trail complicate post-flight fuel reconciliation and contract compliance reporting

l4_steps.name: Confirm truck dispatch and stand assignment
l4_steps.input: Fuel order, aircraft stand/gate assignment, turnaround schedule
l4_steps.output: Fuel truck dispatched; confirmed ETA to aircraft stand
l4_steps.kpi: Truck on-stand ≤ 20 minutes before scheduled fuelling start; zero missed fuelling windows due to late truck
l4_steps.pain_point: Late stand changes communicated via AMS cause fuel truck repositioning delays, particularly at congested hub airports; AMS–fuel truck coordination relies on VHF radio and phone at many stations rather than automated system-to-system dispatch

l4_steps.name: Validate fuelling window against turnaround schedule
l4_steps.input: Truck ETA, aircraft block-in time, turnaround milestones, STD
l4_steps.output: Fuelling window confirmed; or expedite request issued to handler with revised fuelling start
l4_steps.kpi: Fuelling completed ≥ 20 minutes before STD; fuelling-related departure delays < 0.5% of turns
l4_steps.pain_point: Short-haul turn times (45–60 min) leave minimal buffer; a single fuelling delay cascades directly into a departure delay when there is no concurrent-task optimisation — fuelling, catering, and cleaning compete for the same ramp corridor

l4_steps.name: Perform pre-fuelling fuel quality sample check
l4_steps.system: Fuel Quality Management log (AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware at MRO bases; paper logbook at outstations)
l4_steps.input: Fuel sample drawn from tanker drain or hydrant pit; density meter; water-detection paste
l4_steps.output: Pass/fail quality certificate; density (kg/L) and temperature recorded; release-to-aircraft signed
l4_steps.kpi: 100% pre-fuelling sample compliance; zero aircraft fuelled without a logged pass certificate
l4_steps.pain_point: At outstations with hydrant systems, sample accountability is paper-based and not linked to AMOS; contamination events (water ingress, incorrect fuel grade) have historically been missed — Avianca 052 (1990, fuel exhaustion) and multiple near-misses underscore the cost of manual-only controls at remote stations

l4_steps.name: Execute fuel uplift to planned quantity
l4_steps.system: Fuel truck flow meter / Aircraft fuel gauging system (ACARS uplink)
l4_steps.input: Approved uplift quantity, current fuel-on-board from aircraft gauges, truck flow meter
l4_steps.output: Actual uplift quantity delivered; aircraft fuel gauges confirmed at target level
l4_steps.kpi: Uplift accuracy ±1% of planned quantity; zero over/under-fuelling events per month
l4_steps.pain_point: Aircraft fuel gauge tolerance is ±2% on narrow-body types (737/A320); systematic gauge bias, if uncorrected in planning assumptions, causes repeated uplift variance; most fuel planning systems do not ingest gauge correction factors from avionics maintenance records

l4_steps.name: Record actual uplift in tech log and transmit via ACARS
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware + Telex / SITA ACARS
l4_steps.input: Flow meter final reading, aircraft gauge reading, fueller's delivery receipt
l4_steps.output: Actual uplift entered in aircraft tech log; ACARS fuel completion message sent to OCC and dispatcher
l4_steps.kpi: ACARS fuel message transmitted ≤ 5 minutes after fuelling complete; tech log discrepancy rate < 1%
l4_steps.pain_point: Discrepancy between flow meter and aircraft gauge requires licensed engineer sign-off, adding 5–10 minutes at outstations with limited engineering cover; paper tech logs at regional stations delay OCC visibility into actual fuel state until ACARS message is manually triggered

l4_steps.name: Dispatcher briefs captain on OFP fuel plan & alternates
l4_steps.system: Lido/Flight by Lufthansa Systems (OFP) + SITA ACARS Datalink
l4_steps.input: Finalised OFP, actual fuel onboard, latest weather update, active NOTAMs, alternate aerodrome status
l4_steps.output: Captain briefed; OFP reviewed and queried or ready for signature
l4_steps.kpi: Dispatcher briefing completed ≥ 30 minutes before STD; zero departures without dispatcher-signed OFP
l4_steps.pain_point: Late weather or NOTAM changes after OFP release require a re-issue; re-issue process in Lido is manual and time-consuming under short turns, creating pressure on dispatchers to release without capturing the latest data

l4_steps.name: Captain accepts or requests additional discretionary fuel
l4_steps.system: Aircraft fuel management panel / Jeppesen FliteDeck Pro (EFB)
l4_steps.input: OFP fuel plan, personal weather/routing assessment, alternate viability, ATC restriction outlook
l4_steps.output: Captain's fuel decision; discretionary addition quantity and rationale (if fuel added)
l4_steps.kpi: Average captain discretionary addition ≤ 5% of trip fuel; additions above 10% flagged for safety review
l4_steps.pain_point: Captain discretionary fuel additions are unstructured — no system captures the stated rationale; without structured data, flight ops cannot distinguish legitimate tactical additions from systematic under-planning, preventing feedback loop improvement in Lido fuel models

l4_steps.name: Finalise load sheet with captain-approved fuel figures
l4_steps.system: Lido/Flight by Lufthansa Systems + Amadeus Altéa PSS (load control module)
l4_steps.input: Captain-approved fuel quantity, actual payload (pax + baggage + cargo), aircraft zero-fuel weight
l4_steps.output: Finalised load sheet signed; OFP fuel figures locked; departure clearance issued to captain
l4_steps.kpi: Load sheet issued ≤ 15 minutes before STD; 100% OFP/load-sheet fuel figure consistency
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual reconciliation between Lido fuel figures and Altéa load control introduces transcription error risk; most carriers lack a direct system interface between flight planning and PSS load control, requiring copy-paste of fuel figures and creating an auditable gap in the data chain

l4_steps.name: Transmit departure fuel state to Operations Control Centre
l4_steps.system: SITA ACARS Datalink + OCC Operations Dashboard (AWS-hosted)
l4_steps.input: Final block fuel figures, actual departure time, gate/stand number
l4_steps.output: OCC fuel state record updated; block-off fuel confirmed and archived for post-flight analysis
l4_steps.kpi: OCC fuel state updated ≤ 5 minutes of block-off; 100% ACARS message delivery rate
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS VHF channel congestion at major hubs (LHR, JFK, LAX) causes message delivery failures during peak pushback windows; manual phone fallback to OCC creates audit gaps in the fuel tracking data stream used for end-of-day fuel efficiency reporting

l4_steps.name: Pull aircraft DOW/DOI from maintenance system
l4_steps.input: Tail number assignment from OCC
l4_steps.output: Dry Operating Weight, Dry Operating Index, seating config, hold bay limits
l4_steps.kpi: Configuration accuracy 100%; zero dispatches with incorrect DOW
l4_steps.pain_point: Last-minute aircraft swaps (e.g., 737-800 replaced by 737-700) cause DOW discrepancy if AMOS weight record not updated within 30 min of tail reassignment

l4_steps.name: Retrieve fuel uplift from flight planning system
l4_steps.input: Signed flight plan released by dispatcher
l4_steps.output: Fuel figure (trip, contingency, alternate, final reserve) in kg for load calculation
l4_steps.kpi: Fuel data transfer latency < 5 min from dispatch plan release
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual re-entry required when API link between Lido/Flight and SITA LoadManager is unavailable; transcription errors produce erroneous TOW calculations

l4_steps.name: Calculate structural limits and underload allowance
l4_steps.input: DOW, fuel load, aircraft type structural limits (MTOW, MZFW, MLW, MAC envelope)
l4_steps.output: Maximum payload, underload figure, allowed traffic load by cabin and hold
l4_steps.kpi: Underload figure accuracy ±50 kg versus final actuals
l4_steps.pain_point: MZFW and MTOW vary by 737 sub-variant (e.g., 737-800 vs 737-8 MAX); incorrect variant code in LoadManager causes structural limit overrun risk without automated alert

l4_steps.name: Extract PAX counts from check-in at cutoff
l4_steps.input: Departure control check-in data at standard cutoff (T-35 min)
l4_steps.output: Final passenger counts by cabin class; PAX weight totals using standard weights
l4_steps.kpi: Cutoff-to-load-sheet cycle time < 15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Late check-in waivers granted after cutoff add PAX to Altéa without auto-alerting load controller; controller may issue load sheet based on stale PAX count

l4_steps.name: Apply IATA standard or actual PAX weights
l4_steps.input: PAX count, season flag, route type (domestic/international), cabin class mix
l4_steps.output: Total PAX weight per IATA Resolution 788 (84 kg male / 76 kg female with carry-on)
l4_steps.kpi: Weight deviation vs actuals < 2% for domestic routes
l4_steps.pain_point: Incorrect season flag (summer/winter) in SITA LoadManager causes systematic 4 kg/PAX under-estimate on narrow-body routes with no automated audit trail for season changes

l4_steps.name: Capture checked baggage weights at bag room
l4_steps.input: Baggage tag scans at make-up area belt
l4_steps.output: Per-flight total hold baggage weight by zone and ULD
l4_steps.kpi: Baggage weight reconciliation ≥ 99% of tagged bags per flight
l4_steps.pain_point: Individual baggage weighting not performed on narrow-body short-haul; weight estimated from PAX count × standard bag weight, resulting in actual vs plan variance exceeding 200 kg on full flights

l4_steps.name: Process special PAX categories from SSR codes
l4_steps.input: SSR codes (UMNR, WCHC, EXST, BSCT, MEDA) from reservation record
l4_steps.output: Special category weights and seating constraints applied to load plan
l4_steps.kpi: SSR compliance rate 100%; zero unmanaged special PAX categories at load sheet issue
l4_steps.pain_point: EXST (extra seat) PAX body weight not consistently captured in Altéa SSR; load controller must query gate agent manually, adding 5–10 min and creating CG error risk

l4_steps.name: Receive cargo manifest and ULD build data
l4_steps.input: Air waybill manifest, ULD build sheets from cargo acceptance
l4_steps.output: Cargo weight, volume, and loading sequence by hold bay
l4_steps.kpi: Cargo manifest received ≥ T-60 min before departure; late manifest rate < 5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Belly cargo manifest routinely received < T-30 min for connection flights; load controller must estimate cargo weight, creating CG shift risk if actuals differ by more than 150 kg

l4_steps.name: Validate and approve DG load — issue NOTOC
l4_steps.input: DG declaration, ICAO packing group, quantity and UN number
l4_steps.output: Approved DG stowage position; NOTOC transmitted to captain via ACARS
l4_steps.kpi: DG NOTOC issued to captain ≥ T-30 min before departure; 100% ICAO Annex 18 compliance
l4_steps.pain_point: Late DG declarations from freight forwarders cause NOTOC amendments after load sheet issue; each amendment requires captain re-signature, adding 10–20 min average delay

l4_steps.name: Allocate hold bay loading positions for CG target
l4_steps.input: Cargo weight and volume by ULD, DG stowage rules, ZFW CG target
l4_steps.output: Bay loading plan (fwd/aft hold, bulk), tie-down instructions for ramp crew
l4_steps.kpi: CG within ±1% MAC of target after initial bay allocation
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual bay allocation for 737 holds (bays 41F/42G/43H) is error-prone; no automated CG feedback loop in LoadManager until all weights are confirmed, delaying detection of CG exceedance

l4_steps.name: Generate preliminary e-LoadSheet with ZFW/TOW/LDW
l4_steps.input: PAX weights, baggage weights, cargo bay plan, fuel load, DOW
l4_steps.output: Preliminary ZFW, TOW, LDW, CG %MAC on electronic Load Sheet
l4_steps.kpi: Preliminary load sheet ready ≥ T-30 min before scheduled departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Tankering fuel decisions made by dispatch after preliminary load sheet generation require full recalculation; re-issue cycle adds 5 min and risks version mismatch between load controller and captain

l4_steps.name: Validate CG within certified flight envelope
l4_steps.input: TOW and CG %MAC from preliminary load sheet
l4_steps.output: CG validation result — pass or fail against fwd and aft certified limits
l4_steps.kpi: CG out-of-envelope rate < 0.01% of departures (IATA industry benchmark)
l4_steps.pain_point: Aft CG limit exceedance on 737-800 with full cabin and light belly cargo is a known risk scenario; redistribution or trim ballast adds 15–25 min to turnaround time

l4_steps.name: Calculate stabiliser trim setting and confirm CG index
l4_steps.input: Final TOW, CG %MAC, selected flap setting
l4_steps.output: Stab trim setting transmitted to captain; load sheet CG index confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Stab trim setting issued to flight deck ≥ T-20 min before departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Discrepancy between load controller stab trim (SITA) and EFB-computed value (Jeppesen FliteDeck) when aircraft config tables are not synchronised; manual cross-check adds 3–5 min per occurrence

l4_steps.name: Transmit final load sheet to flight deck via ACARS
l4_steps.input: Finalised and signed e-LoadSheet
l4_steps.output: Load sheet delivered to flight deck; ACARS receipt confirmation captured
l4_steps.kpi: Load sheet delivery ≥ T-20 min before departure; ACARS receipt confirmation within 2 min
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS transmission failure at remote stands without ground-to-aircraft data link requires manual paper load sheet handoff, breaking the e-signature audit trail required under ICAO Annex 6

l4_steps.name: Captain reviews and signs load sheet on EFB
l4_steps.input: e-LoadSheet, stab trim, NOTOC, and fuel plan
l4_steps.output: Captain's electronic signature on load sheet; acceptance transmitted to load control
l4_steps.kpi: Captain acceptance cycle time < 5 min; load sheet rejection rate < 0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Captain queries on ZFW discrepancy require callback to load controller; FliteDeck has no in-app messaging, forcing VHF or phone communication and adding average 4 min delay per query

l4_steps.name: Issue final loading instruction and close holds
l4_steps.input: Accepted load sheet, finalised bay loading plan
l4_steps.output: Final loading instruction transmitted to ramp; hold door closure authorised
l4_steps.kpi: Hold closure notification ≥ T-10 min before departure; D0 on-time departure impact attributable to W&B < 0.3%
l4_steps.pain_point: Late passenger offloads (IROPS, no-show reconciliation) after hold closure require baggage pull, repeat CG validation, and captain re-acceptance — average additional delay 20 min per occurrence

l4_steps.name: Archive load sheet and transmit LDM to destination
l4_steps.input: Signed load sheet; final PAX, cargo, and fuel actuals
l4_steps.output: Load Distribution Message (LDM) transmitted to destination station and OCC; load sheet archived per ICAO Annex 6 (24-month retention)
l4_steps.kpi: LDM transmitted within 5 min of actual departure; 100% archival compliance rate
l4_steps.pain_point: LDM is not auto-transmitted when SITA LoadManager is in failover mode; manual Telex composition is error-prone and causes destination station misinterpretation of hold contents

l4_steps.name: Retrieve NOTAMs from FAA/ICAO AFTN network
l4_steps.input: Continuous AFTN/CIDIN feed from FAA NOTAM System (FNS) and ICAO NOF
l4_steps.output: Raw NOTAM messages ingested into NOTAM processing queue
l4_steps.kpi: NOTAM ingestion latency ≤5 min from issuance to system receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA NOTAM System outages (e.g., Jan 2023 FAA NOTAM system failure grounding 10,000 flights) can break AFTN feed with no automatic failover to backup source

l4_steps.name: Parse and classify NOTAMs by type and location
l4_steps.input: Raw NOTAM text strings from AFTN queue
l4_steps.output: Classified NOTAM records: type (N, C, R, Q-code), ICAO location, validity window
l4_steps.kpi: NOTAM parse accuracy ≥99.5%; misclassification rate <0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Legacy free-text NOTAM format (pre-ICAO Digital NOTAM standard) leads to high parse error rates, especially for non-standard national formats from international destinations

l4_steps.name: Validate NOTAM format completeness and decode Q-line
l4_steps.input: Parsed NOTAM record with Q-line fields (FIR, code, purpose, scope, coordinates)
l4_steps.output: Validated NOTAM record or rejection flag with error description
l4_steps.kpi: Validation cycle time ≤30 sec per NOTAM batch
l4_steps.pain_point: Incomplete Q-lines from some national NOTAM offices require manual correction, creating dispatcher workload spikes during high-NOTAM-volume periods (e.g., airshow TFRs, VIP TFRs)

l4_steps.name: Filter NOTAMs against active airline route network
l4_steps.input: Validated NOTAM records; active city-pair route list from Amadeus SkyWORKS
l4_steps.output: Route-relevant NOTAM subset filtered by departure, destination, alternate, and enroute FIRs
l4_steps.kpi: False-positive NOTAM rate ≤10% (irrelevant NOTAMs passed to dispatchers)
l4_steps.pain_point: Overly broad geographic filters result in NOTAM overload — dispatchers report reviewing 200–400 NOTAMs per long-haul release; filter tuning is manual and not route-aware

l4_steps.name: Assign operational severity level to filtered NOTAMs
l4_steps.input: Route-relevant NOTAM subset with Q-code purpose/scope fields
l4_steps.output: Severity-ranked NOTAM list: Critical (runway/navaid closed), Significant (degraded service), Advisory (FYI)
l4_steps.kpi: Critical NOTAM identification accuracy ≥99.9%; missed critical NOTAM rate = 0
l4_steps.pain_point: Automated severity scoring relies on Q-code purpose field, which is inconsistently applied by international NOTAM offices — human review remains mandatory for all Critical-category items

l4_steps.name: Determine if NOTAM affects operational route or airport
l4_steps.input: Severity-ranked NOTAM list; scheduled flight manifest for next 24 hours
l4_steps.output: Action decision: Escalate for impact assessment (Critical/Significant) or Archive (Advisory only)
l4_steps.kpi: Escalation decision cycle time ≤10 min per NOTAM batch review
l4_steps.pain_point: Dispatchers managing 30–50 concurrent flights face decision fatigue during high-tempo NOTAM periods; no AI-assisted triage available in current Jeppesen version

l4_steps.name: Analyse runway and navaid availability constraints
l4_steps.input: Critical/Significant NOTAMs for departure, destination, and alternate airports
l4_steps.output: Runway availability matrix; navaid serviceability status per airport
l4_steps.kpi: Constraint analysis completion ≥2 hours before STD for all affected flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Runway NOTAM status may conflict with airport ATIS/D-ATIS if NOTAM is issued but not yet reflected in automated terminal information — dispatchers must cross-check both sources manually

l4_steps.name: Review AIP amendments and SUPs for permanent changes
l4_steps.input: Current AIP amendments (AIRACs) and AIP Supplements for affected airports
l4_steps.output: List of permanent procedural changes affecting approach minima, SIDs/STARs, or obstacle clearance
l4_steps.kpi: AIRAC cycle review completion within 24 hours of effective date; 0 missed effective-date changes
l4_steps.pain_point: AIRAC cycle updates (every 28 days) require coordinated updates across FliteDeck, NAVBLUE, and FMS navigation databases — misaligned update windows create temporary procedure inconsistencies

l4_steps.name: Assess alternate airport availability under active NOTAMs
l4_steps.input: Alternate airport candidates from flight plan; NOTAMs affecting alternate runways and navaids
l4_steps.output: Approved alternate airport list with NOTAM-qualified minima adjustments
l4_steps.kpi: Alternate qualification cycle time ≤20 min per flight; 0 releases with non-qualified alternates
l4_steps.pain_point: Destination alternate requirements under FAR 91.169 / ICAO Annex 2 require dispatcher to verify alternate ILS/RNAV availability — NOTAM-driven navaid outages at alternates frequently require last-minute alternate substitution

l4_steps.name: Determine if flight plan modification is required
l4_steps.input: Runway/navaid constraints; AIP changes; alternate qualification results
l4_steps.output: Modification flag: re-route, alternate change, fuel uplift revision, or no change required
l4_steps.kpi: Flight plan modification decision issued ≥90 min before STD
l4_steps.pain_point: Late-issued TFRs and runway NOTAMs within 90 minutes of departure compress decision windows and may force gate-hold or airborne re-route, increasing ATC workload and crew duty time

l4_steps.name: Compile route-specific NOTAM briefing package
l4_steps.input: Filtered, severity-ranked NOTAMs for departure, enroute FIRs, destination, and alternates
l4_steps.output: Structured NOTAM briefing document: categorised, sorted by phase of flight, valid times highlighted
l4_steps.kpi: Briefing package generation time ≤15 min; package length ≤ 10 pages for domestic, ≤25 pages for international
l4_steps.pain_point: Unfiltered NOTAM packages can exceed 80 pages on busy international routes — crews report difficulty identifying safety-critical items; no regulatory standard mandates package length limits

l4_steps.name: Push NOTAM package to crew EFB pre-departure folder
l4_steps.input: Compiled NOTAM briefing package; flight number and tail assignment from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: NOTAM package loaded on crew EFB with push notification to assigned Captain and First Officer
l4_steps.kpi: EFB delivery confirmation ≥60 min before STD; push failure rate <1%
l4_steps.pain_point: EFB connectivity at gates with poor Wi-Fi infrastructure can delay package delivery; crews boarding late international flights may not receive updates if EFB sync occurs only at logon

l4_steps.name: Confirm critical NOTAM acknowledgement by flight crew
l4_steps.input: NOTAM briefing package with Critical items flagged; crew electronic signature workflow
l4_steps.output: Signed acknowledgement record with timestamp; unacknowledged items escalated to dispatcher
l4_steps.kpi: Crew acknowledgement completion ≥30 min before STD for all Critical NOTAMs; 0 departures without acknowledgement
l4_steps.pain_point: Electronic acknowledgement workflow is checkbox-based — does not confirm comprehension; NTSB has cited NOTAM awareness failures in several runway incursion incidents where crews signed off on packages without reviewing Critical items

l4_steps.name: Validate flight plan route against active airspace NOTAMs
l4_steps.input: Filed flight plan route (ICAO format); active airspace restriction NOTAMs (TFRs, restricted areas, ADIZs)
l4_steps.output: Route compliance report: conflicts flagged with NOTAM reference and lateral/vertical extent
l4_steps.kpi: Route validation cycle time ≤5 min; 0 flight plans released with unresolved airspace conflicts
l4_steps.pain_point: Dynamic TFR activations (security, VIP movements, wildfire operations) may occur after initial flight plan filing — NAVBLUE automated airspace conflict check must be re-run within 30 min of departure

l4_steps.name: Update alternate airport selections per NOTAM constraints
l4_steps.input: NOTAM-qualified alternate list from Step 3.3; current fuel load plan
l4_steps.output: Revised alternate airports filed in ICAO flight plan; fuel adjustment order if additional alternate required
l4_steps.kpi: Alternate update reflected in ATC-filed flight plan ≥45 min before STD
l4_steps.pain_point: Adding a more distant alternate due to NOTAM-driven disqualification increases fuel burn — late alternate changes may require fuel truck return to gate, impacting on-time departure (D0) performance

l4_steps.name: Confirm flight plan is fully NOTAM-compliant before release
l4_steps.input: Final flight plan with route, alternates, and fuel load; complete active NOTAM set
l4_steps.output: Dispatcher release signature and Aircraft Dispatcher's Release (ADR) document compliant with FAR 121.593
l4_steps.kpi: 0 dispatcher releases with open unresolved Critical NOTAMs; release issued ≥30 min before STD
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR 121.593 requires joint Captain/Dispatcher release — if Captain refuses to sign due to NOTAM concern, operational control dispute escalation process is time-consuming and not well-documented in most airline SOPs

l4_steps.name: Monitor NOTAM updates for airborne flights via ACARS
l4_steps.input: Real-time NOTAM feed from Honeywell GoDirect; active airborne flight list
l4_steps.output: ACARS uplink messages to affected crews with new or amended NOTAM details
l4_steps.kpi: In-flight NOTAM update transmission latency ≤10 min from issuance; crew acknowledgement receipt ≥95%
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS coverage gaps over oceanic tracks and remote domestic segments (e.g., Alaska corridors) can delay critical NOTAM uplinks; satellite ACARS costs constrain message frequency on some routes

l4_steps.name: Archive expired NOTAMs and update operational log
l4_steps.input: Expired and cancelled NOTAM records; flight completion confirmations from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Archived NOTAM audit trail; updated operational log with NOTAM-driven delay and re-route codes
l4_steps.kpi: NOTAM archive completeness 100%; delay attribution accuracy ≥98% for NOTAM-caused events
l4_steps.pain_point: NOTAM-driven delays are frequently miscoded in delay tracking systems (e.g., coded as 'weather' rather than 'NOTAM/airspace') — corrupting operational performance data used for ATC slot planning and DOT reporting

l4_steps.name: Ingest METAR/TAF feeds from NWS/NOAA
l4_steps.input: Automated weather station transmissions from NWS ASOS/AWOS network
l4_steps.output: Normalised METAR/TAF data loaded into weather workstation
l4_steps.kpi: Data refresh latency ≤5 min for all airports in route network
l4_steps.pain_point: NWS ASOS outages at smaller spoke airports create data gaps; GoDirect fallback to model-derived obs introduces ±3°C temperature error affecting performance calculations

l4_steps.name: Ingest SIGMET, AIRMET & convective outlook
l4_steps.input: NWS Aviation Weather Center SIGMET/AIRMET issuances; convective outlooks (Day 1–3)
l4_steps.output: Active SIGMET/AIRMET polygons overlaid on route map
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of active domestic SIGMETs captured within 10 min of NWS issuance
l4_steps.pain_point: International SIGMET ingestion via SADIS requires separate subscription; coverage gaps over oceanic tracks (OTS) require manual cross-check against NAT SIGMET bulletins

l4_steps.name: Validate data currency and completeness
l4_steps.input: All ingested weather feeds from steps 1.1 and 1.2
l4_steps.output: Data quality flag (Pass/Fail) per station; stale-data alerts for gaps >30 min
l4_steps.kpi: ≥98% of route-relevant stations reporting within 30-min window at pre-departure check
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated alerting when upstream NWS feed drops; dispatcher must manually notice missing station data during busy multi-departure windows

l4_steps.name: Analyse route-specific weather hazards
l4_steps.input: Active SIGMETs, radar composites, turbulence prog charts, icing PIREPs
l4_steps.output: Route weather hazard summary per flight: turbulence, icing, CB/convective activity, low-level wind shear flags
l4_steps.kpi: Hazard assessment completed ≥45 min before scheduled departure (D-45)
l4_steps.pain_point: Rapidly developing convection (pop-up cells) outpaces 1-hourly radar update cycle; AviationSentry nowcast accuracy degrades beyond +3 hr for mesoscale convective systems

l4_steps.name: Assess departure, destination & alternate wx
l4_steps.input: Current METAR/TAF for departure, destination, and minimum two alternates
l4_steps.output: Ceiling/visibility/wind report per airport; go/no-go flag against FAR Part 121.619 alternate minima
l4_steps.kpi: Alternate airport identification completed for 100% of IFR releases within D-60
l4_steps.pain_point: TAF validity windows (±1 hr) create ambiguity at scheduled arrival time; low-frequency alternates may lack TAF service, requiring meteorological judgement unsupported by system data

l4_steps.name: Classify weather threat level against ops specs
l4_steps.input: Route hazard summary from 2.1; airport assessments from 2.2; airline ops specs (OpSpec A002/A025)
l4_steps.output: Threat classification: Green / Amber / Red per flight; Amber/Red triggers reroute or hold evaluation
l4_steps.kpi: Zero flights released into Red-classified weather corridor without Duty Manager override sign-off
l4_steps.pain_point: OpSpec thresholds for convective avoidance (20 nm lateral separation from CBs) not programmatically enforced in AviationSentry; relies on dispatcher visual judgement of radar returns

l4_steps.name: Cross-reference weather threats with flight plans
l4_steps.input: Red/Amber threat polygons from 2.3; active flight plan waypoints and airways
l4_steps.output: Conflict list: flights whose planned route intersects active hazard polygon within ±30 NM buffer
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of active flight plans checked against current SIGMET polygons pre-departure
l4_steps.pain_point: NAVBLUE polygon overlay requires manual SIGMET boundary entry when NWS feed XML schema changes; integration SLA between NWS and NAVBLUE API is 15 min, creating a window of stale data

l4_steps.name: Calculate fuel burn impact of weather deviations
l4_steps.input: Proposed deviation routing around hazard polygons; aircraft performance model (B737-800/MAX 8)
l4_steps.output: Revised fuel burn delta vs. filed plan; go/no-go flag against minimum fuel uplift threshold
l4_steps.kpi: Fuel recalculation turnaround ≤8 min per rerouted flight to preserve D-45 release window
l4_steps.pain_point: NAVBLUE performance model uses scheduled aircraft type; last-minute tail swaps (B737-700 for -800) require re-entry of performance data manually — no automated tail-type pull from Altéa OCC

l4_steps.name: Verify alternate airport weather acceptability
l4_steps.input: Revised alternate candidates after route deviation; current METAR/TAF at alternate(s)
l4_steps.output: Confirmed alternate airport(s) meeting FAR 121.619 ceiling/visibility minima at ETA ±1 hr
l4_steps.kpi: Alternate confirmation completed for 100% of IFR dispatch releases before crew briefing
l4_steps.pain_point: Peak-demand periods force simultaneous alternate re-evaluation for multiple flights; limited dispatcher bandwidth increases risk of using stale TAF data beyond 6-hour validity window

l4_steps.name: Issue or withhold dispatch weather release
l4_steps.input: Approved routing, fuel plan, and alternate from Phase 3; threat classification from 2.3
l4_steps.output: Signed dispatch release (FAR 121.663) with weather addendum; or hold notification to crew scheduling
l4_steps.kpi: ≤2% of departures held >30 min beyond SOBT for weather-related dispatch rework
l4_steps.pain_point: Dispatcher joint release authority requires co-sign from PIC; when crew is in-bound the electronic co-sign workflow in NAVBLUE times out after 15 min, forcing a manual paper release process

l4_steps.name: Brief flight crew on significant weather via EFB
l4_steps.input: Dispatch release with weather addendum; radar snapshots; SIGMET polygons; turbulence PIREPs
l4_steps.output: Weather briefing package pushed to crew EFB ≥30 min before departure; crew acknowledgment record
l4_steps.kpi: Crew acknowledgment of weather briefing received for 100% of Amber/Red-classified departures
l4_steps.pain_point: EFB push notification delivery confirmation is not real-time; dispatcher cannot distinguish between un-delivered and unread briefings, risking undocumented crew awareness gaps before FAR 121.601 compliance check

l4_steps.name: Confirm crew acceptance of dispatch release
l4_steps.input: Dispatch release and weather briefing from 4.2
l4_steps.output: Crew acceptance message (ACARS uplink) or crew request for amended release
l4_steps.kpi: Crew acceptance ACARS message received ≥20 min before SOBT for 95% of departures
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS acceptance workflow is non-standardised across gate types; at congested gates crews sometimes provide verbal acceptance to ground ops without ACARS confirmation, leaving no auditable record for FAR 121.663

l4_steps.name: Monitor en-route convective activity in real time
l4_steps.input: Airborne flight position data (ADS-B via FlightAware); updated radar mosaics refreshed every 5 min
l4_steps.output: Live flight track overlaid on convective radar; proximity alert if cell within 30 NM of track
l4_steps.kpi: Dispatcher workstation refresh ≤5 min; proximity alert generated within 2 min of threshold breach
l4_steps.pain_point: Single dispatcher managing 15–20 simultaneous en-route flights cannot sustain continuous radar monitoring; AviationSentry automated proximity alerting requires manual polygon configuration per flight and resets on sector boundary crossings

l4_steps.name: Evaluate PIREP and crew weather deviation reports
l4_steps.input: In-flight PIREP uplinks (turbulence severity, icing level, CB observations); crew position reports
l4_steps.output: Updated route hazard picture; PIREP filed with ATC for distribution to following aircraft
l4_steps.kpi: PIREP relay to NWS/ATC within 15 min of crew report for 90% of severe turbulence encounters
l4_steps.pain_point: PIREP data entry format inconsistency between crews (free-text vs. structured ACARS form) reduces automated parsing accuracy in AviationSentry; significant events may be missed in multi-flight monitoring queue

l4_steps.name: Assess need for divert, reroute or amended release
l4_steps.input: Updated weather picture from 5.1 and 5.2; remaining fuel on board (ACARS fuel telemetry); nearest alternate airports
l4_steps.output: Amended dispatch release with revised routing or divert authorisation; ACARS uplink to crew
l4_steps.kpi: Amended release issued within 10 min of divert-trigger threshold being met; zero diversions without prior dispatcher-crew coordination
l4_steps.pain_point: Amended release workflow in NAVBLUE requires re-opening a filed plan and triggers full recalculation; under time pressure dispatchers sometimes relay route changes verbally without formal amended release, creating FAR 121.663 compliance exposure

l4_steps.name: Obtain ATIS & meteorological briefing
l4_steps.input: Scheduled departure time, origin/destination airport pair
l4_steps.output: Current ATIS information code, wx briefing package
l4_steps.kpi: Briefing completed ≥45 min before STD; 100% crew acknowledgement rate
l4_steps.pain_point: GoDirect ATIS latency can lag live tower broadcasts by 3–5 min during high-volume periods, risking crew departure on stale altimeter settings

l4_steps.name: File IFR flight plan with ANSP
l4_steps.input: Optimised route, fuel load, aircraft type, SELCAL code
l4_steps.output: Filed ICAO flight plan (FPL message) accepted by ANSP
l4_steps.kpi: Flight plan filed ≥60 min before STD per ICAO Doc 4444; acceptance rate ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: NAVBLUE route optimisation does not automatically incorporate FAA Coded Departure Routes (CDRs) during Ground Delay Programs, requiring manual dispatcher override

l4_steps.name: Request CTOT/EDCT slot from ATFM system
l4_steps.input: Filed flight plan, GDP/GS advisory for destination or en-route ARTCC
l4_steps.output: EDCT (Expect Departure Clearance Time) slot assignment
l4_steps.kpi: EDCT compliance rate ≥95%; slot deviation window ±5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: TFMS EDCT updates can arrive with <15 min notice, making ground crew coordination nearly impossible during high-frequency departure banks at focus cities

l4_steps.name: Negotiate revised slot if CTOT unacceptable
l4_steps.input: Initial EDCT that conflicts with operational constraints or crew duty limits
l4_steps.output: Revised EDCT or cancellation/delay decision logged in NAVBLUE
l4_steps.kpi: Slot substitution request processed within 10 min of receipt; substitution approval rate ~60% per FAA ATCSCC data
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA does not guarantee slot substitution approval; carriers without dedicated ATC coordination desk (like low-cost carriers) suffer higher rejection rates

l4_steps.name: Request IFR departure clearance from ATC
l4_steps.input: Filed route, EDCT window, current ATIS code
l4_steps.output: ATC clearance (SID, squawk code, initial altitude, departure frequency)
l4_steps.kpi: Clearance received ≥15 min before EDCT; clearance readback accuracy 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Voice clearance delivery congestion at Class B airports (ORD, ATL, LAX) causes average 8–12 min clearance delays during push banks; PDC via ACARS not universally available

l4_steps.name: Verify clearance against filed route & amend if needed
l4_steps.input: Received ATC clearance text, original filed IFR route
l4_steps.output: Amended flight plan accepted by ATC or confirmation of route match
l4_steps.kpi: Route amendment turnaround <5 min; zero departures on unapproved route
l4_steps.pain_point: ATC short-notice route amendments (e.g. miles-in-trail restrictions) require rapid NAVBLUE recalculation that may invalidate pre-filed fuel load, triggering re-release

l4_steps.name: Coordinate pushback & engine start with ground ATC
l4_steps.input: Approved clearance, gate status from AMS, ramp clearance
l4_steps.output: Pushback approval, engine start time logged in AMS
l4_steps.kpi: Pushback-to-wheels-up compliance with EDCT ±5 min; gate conflict rate <2%
l4_steps.pain_point: AMS gate conflict data and ATC ground movement frequency are separate systems with no real-time integration, causing dispatcher blind spots during congested apron operations

l4_steps.name: Obtain taxi clearance & confirm runway assignment
l4_steps.input: Engine start confirmation, active runways, NOTAMs from FliteDeck
l4_steps.output: Taxi route confirmed on EFB moving map; runway assignment accepted
l4_steps.kpi: Taxi time within airline benchmark (e.g. ≤12 min at focus cities); runway incursion events = 0
l4_steps.pain_point: FliteDeck moving-map airport diagrams rely on Jeppesen chart update cycle (28-day AIRAC); temporary construction NOTAMs between cycles create taxiway routing errors if crew relies solely on EFB

l4_steps.name: Monitor ATC sector handoffs & frequency changes
l4_steps.input: Departure from origin TRACON, en-route ARTCC sector list from NAVBLUE
l4_steps.output: ACARS position reports at waypoints; sector contact log
l4_steps.kpi: ACARS position report every 30 min or at each waypoint; missed report alert <2 min
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS coverage gaps over oceanic/remote segments require HF radio fallback (SELCAL), which many newer pilots have limited proficiency with due to shift away from HF in domestic ops

l4_steps.name: Receive & assess TFMS en-route flow advisories
l4_steps.input: En-route Miles-in-Trail (MIT) restrictions, Airspace Flow Program (AFP) advisories
l4_steps.output: Compliance assessment; amended release or hold action if needed
l4_steps.kpi: AFP compliance rate ≥97%; dispatcher response to advisory <10 min
l4_steps.pain_point: TFMS AFP advisories can affect multiple concurrent flights simultaneously; single dispatcher managing 15+ flights during an AFP event is a documented overload risk with no automated prioritisation tool

l4_steps.name: Coordinate weather deviation or reroute with ATC
l4_steps.input: Onboard weather radar data, GoDirect TurbCast/convective sigmets
l4_steps.output: ATC-approved route deviation or altitude change; updated NAVBLUE flight plan
l4_steps.kpi: Deviation request approval by ATC <3 min after pilot request; fuel impact assessed 100% of deviations
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew-initiated deviation requests during congested sector workload may receive delayed ATC responses; no automated conflict-free re-route suggestion pushed from ground to cockpit in real time

l4_steps.name: Obtain destination ATIS & update approach briefing
l4_steps.input: Current destination ATIS (D-ATIS), TAF, PIREP data from GoDirect
l4_steps.output: Updated approach briefing; alternate airport confirmed if wx below minima
l4_steps.kpi: ATIS update obtained ≥30 min before TOD; alternate fuel carried 100% when wx within 3h of approach minima
l4_steps.pain_point: D-ATIS refresh intervals (30 min at many airports) can lag rapidly deteriorating convective conditions, creating a wx state mismatch between briefing and actual approach environment

l4_steps.name: Sequence into STAR & configure for arrival flow
l4_steps.input: ATC-assigned STAR, speed/altitude restrictions, runway in use
l4_steps.output: FMS programmed with STAR; compliance with ATC sequence instructions confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: STAR compliance rate ≥99%; speed restriction deviation events <0.5% of arrivals
l4_steps.pain_point: Late STAR reassignments by TRACON (within 50 NM) require rapid FMS re-programming under high workload; FliteDeck chart page and FMS are not electronically linked, requiring dual cross-check

l4_steps.name: Execute holding pattern if ATC flow delay required
l4_steps.input: ATC holding instruction, current fuel state vs NAVBLUE holding fuel reserves
l4_steps.output: Holding entry flown or divert decision made; dispatcher notified of fuel state
l4_steps.kpi: Holding fuel contingency ≥30 min per FAR 121.639; divert decision made before minimum divert fuel threshold
l4_steps.pain_point: NAVBLUE fuel models do not auto-recalculate holding burn in real time from cockpit; dispatcher relies on crew verbal reports, introducing latency risk in marginal fuel scenarios

l4_steps.name: Coordinate gate & stand assignment with airport ops
l4_steps.input: ETA update from ACARS, gate availability from AMS, inbound connection data
l4_steps.output: Confirmed gate assignment published in AMS; ground handling notified
l4_steps.kpi: Gate assignment confirmed ≥20 min before ETA; gate conflict rate <1%
l4_steps.pain_point: ATC arrival sequencing changes (e.g. runway change) can shift ETA by 10–20 min, invalidating pre-assigned gate in AMS; no automated ATC-to-AMS ETA feed at most regional airports

l4_steps.name: Close flight plan & confirm arrival report
l4_steps.input: Block-in time from AMS, ATC arrival message
l4_steps.output: Flight plan closed in NAVBLUE; OOOI times recorded (Out/Off/On/In)
l4_steps.kpi: Flight plan closure within 5 min of block-in; OOOI data accuracy 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual flight plan closure is required when ATC arrival message (ARR) is not auto-forwarded to NAVBLUE; missed closures generate ATC search-and-rescue alerts after 30 min per ICAO Annex 2

l4_steps.name: Review ATC communications log for deviations
l4_steps.input: ACARS message archive, crew debrief notes
l4_steps.output: Deviation log entry; flag for ASAP review if applicable
l4_steps.kpi: Post-flight review completed within 2 hours of block-in for all flagged flights
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS stores text messages but does not archive voice ATC transmissions; voice deviations are entirely reliant on crew self-report, creating an underreporting risk for FAR Part 91/121 deviations

l4_steps.name: File ASAP/MOR report for ATC deviation or incident
l4_steps.input: Deviation flag from step 5.2, crew narrative, ATC incident reference number
l4_steps.output: ASAP report submitted to airline safety program; MOR filed with ANSP if required
l4_steps.kpi: ASAP report filed within 24 hours of incident per FAA AC 120-66B; 100% of flagged deviations reported
l4_steps.pain_point: No direct integration between NAVBLUE deviation logs and the airline ASAP reporting portal; dispatcher must re-enter data manually, creating transcription errors and reporting delays

l4_steps.name: Monitor real-time flight progress network-wide
l4_steps.input: Live ACARS position reports, gate departure/arrival feeds
l4_steps.output: Real-time operational picture displayed on NOC wall board
l4_steps.kpi: Flight tracking refresh rate ≤60 sec; network visibility ≥99.5% uptime
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS datalink gaps over oceanic/remote sectors create blind spots; controller must cross-reference multiple screens to build situational awareness
