l4_steps.input: Finalised NOTOC, captain ACARS uplink address, departure gate
l4_steps.output: NOTOC delivered to flight deck with ACARS delivery confirmation timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: NOTOC ACARS delivery confirmation rate ≥99%; delivery completed ≥D-30 min
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS uplink to an aircraft on the ground can fail when avionics are in pre-power state during early turnaround; backup paper NOTOC delivery via physical runner to the gate adds 15–20 min and relies on ramp coordination that frequently breaks down at congested hubs

l4_steps.name: Captain Reviews and Accepts NOTOC
l4_steps.input: NOTOC received via ACARS or EFB datalink; DG policy briefing from dispatcher
l4_steps.output: Captain acceptance acknowledgement or rejection with stated reason
l4_steps.kpi: Captain NOTOC rejection rate <1% of DG flights; acceptance completed ≥D-20 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Under ICAO Annex 18 and FAR 121.285 the captain has absolute authority to offload DG; rejections after DG is physically loaded require ramp return and cause an average 35-min departure delay — root cause is often insufficient pre-departure DG briefing to the cockpit crew

l4_steps.name: Ramp Agent Loads DG per NOTOC Stowage Instructions
l4_steps.input: Finalised NOTOC, ULD build sheets, Loading Instruction Report (LIR)
l4_steps.output: DG ULDs or bulk items loaded at designated hold positions as per NOTOC
l4_steps.kpi: DG loading position accuracy 100%; loading completion ≥D-25 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Ramp teams handle DG orientation labels and class placards under intense time pressure; IATA DGR Sec 9.3 requires 'This Way Up' orientation labels on liquid DG — compliance miss rates spike during peak turn operations when the same ramp team handles multiple aircraft simultaneously

l4_steps.name: Verify DG Load Position and Condition Post-Loading
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS — loading confirmation module)
l4_steps.input: NOTOC stowage locations, physical hold inspection, DG condition checklist
l4_steps.output: DG load verification sign-off; discrepancy or damage report if applicable
l4_steps.kpi: DG load verification completion rate 100% ≥D-20 min; discrepancy rate <0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Hold access for DG load verification requires DG-certified personnel per IATA DGR Sec 9.4; at out-stations with thin staffing the verification is sometimes conducted by non-certified ramp agents, constituting a regulatory non-compliance that is rarely detected until a line audit

l4_steps.name: Update Final Loadsheet with Confirmed DG Positions
l4_steps.input: Verified DG hold positions, ULD manifest, passenger and cargo weights
l4_steps.output: Final signed loadsheet with DG positions confirmed; takeoff weight and CG transmitted to cockpit
l4_steps.kpi: Loadsheet finalisation ≥D-15 min; weight discrepancy vs actual ≤0 kg
l4_steps.pain_point: Late DG offloads — triggered by captain rejection or discovered package damage — require full loadsheet reissue; Altéa DCS reissue and re-signature cycle averages 8–12 min, severely compressing the pre-departure critical path and contributing to D0 departure misses

l4_steps.name: Transmit DG Manifest to Destination & En Route Stations
l4_steps.system: SITA ACARS / Amadeus Altéa DCS (inter-station messaging)
l4_steps.input: Final NOTOC, DG manifest with UN numbers, classes, quantities and positions
l4_steps.output: DG advance notification transmitted to destination and en route handling agents
l4_steps.kpi: Destination DG advance notification lead time ≥2 hours before scheduled arrival (IATA RP 1654); transmission success rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA RP 1654 requires advance DG notification to the destination station; system-to-system messaging reliability degrades at stations running legacy DCS versions incompatible with modern SITA XML message formats, requiring manual telephone or email follow-up that is frequently missed

l4_steps.name: File DG Occurrence Report if Incident Detected
l4_steps.system: Safety Management System (SMS) integrated with ECCAIRS (EU) or FAA ASRS (US)
l4_steps.input: DG handling incident, package damage, leakage, or undeclared DG discovery during loading
l4_steps.output: DG occurrence report filed per ICAO Annex 18 Chapter 14 and applicable national CAA requirements
l4_steps.kpi: DG incident reporting compliance 100%; report filed ≤72 hours of incident per ICAO Annex 18
l4_steps.pain_point: DG incident under-reporting is a recognised industry-wide issue; ramp and cargo staff are reluctant to self-report fearing personal liability — airlines that have not established non-punitive SMS reporting cultures consistently show under-reporting rates estimated at 60–80% of actual DG incidents

l4_steps.name: Archive DG Documentation per Regulatory Retention Policy
l4_steps.system: CargoWise (document archive and retention management module)
l4_steps.input: NOTOC, shipper DG declarations, acceptance checklist, captain sign-off, loading verification
l4_steps.output: DG documentation set archived with jurisdiction-appropriate retention flag applied
l4_steps.kpi: Documentation archival rate 100% within 4 hours of flight departure; retrieval time for audit requests ≤2 min
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA DGR mandates minimum 3-month retention while FAA 49 CFR Part 175 requires 2 years and some EASA states require longer; carriers operating across jurisdictions must apply the longest applicable period globally, but CargoWise retention defaults are often configured to the shortest period, creating audit exposure

l4_steps.name: Extract published flight schedule for pairing input
l4_steps.input: Published SSIM flight schedule file for planning period
l4_steps.output: Validated flight activity file loaded into crew system
l4_steps.kpi: Schedule completeness ≥99.5% of planned departures loaded
l4_steps.pain_point: Schedule changes from network planning arriving <72 hrs before month close disrupt pairing optimization cycles and require costly re-runs

l4_steps.name: Load FAR Part 117 and CBA constraint parameters
l4_steps.input: FAR Part 117 regulation set, current Collective Bargaining Agreement
l4_steps.output: Legal constraint rule set activated in optimization engine
l4_steps.kpi: 100% rule compliance across all published pairings
l4_steps.pain_point: CBA rule amendments negotiated mid-planning cycle require manual rule re-entry into Jeppesen and full re-optimization, adding 8–12 hrs to the planning cycle

l4_steps.name: Validate fleet type and crew qualification matrix
l4_steps.input: Fleet assignment file, crew qualification and currency database
l4_steps.output: Qualified crew pool confirmed per aircraft type and domicile
l4_steps.kpi: Zero unqualified crew assignments at publish; qualification data currency ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: Mixed-fleet type-rating transitions (e.g., 737-800 to MAX) create temporary qualification bottlenecks that reduce eligible crew pools by up to 15% during conversion windows

l4_steps.name: Generate candidate duty periods from flight activity
l4_steps.input: Validated flight activity file, crew base and domicile data
l4_steps.output: Candidate duty period library (50,000+ pairings)
l4_steps.kpi: Generate ≥50,000 candidate pairings per iteration; generation run time <30 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Combinatorial explosion in dense network segments (e.g., 200+ daily departures from hub bases) causes candidate generation times exceeding 4 hrs, compressing the optimization window

l4_steps.name: Filter candidate pairings against FAR Part 117 limits
l4_steps.input: Candidate duty period library, FAR Part 117 duty and rest limits
l4_steps.output: Legally filtered duty period library
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of retained pairings FAR Part 117 compliant; filter pass rate logged
l4_steps.pain_point: Augmented crew rules for ultra-long-haul operations add rule complexity that standard Jeppesen rule builds handle inconsistently without custom coding, requiring manual legal audit

l4_steps.name: Enforce crew base and domicile deadhead constraints
l4_steps.input: FAR-filtered duty periods, crew base capacity allocations
l4_steps.output: Domicile-constrained pairing set with deadhead cost estimates
l4_steps.kpi: Deadhead ratio ≤3.5% of total pairing block hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Unbalanced base staffing at thin-market domiciles forces excessive deadheading; Jeppesen does not dynamically rebalance base headcount, requiring manual planner intervention

l4_steps.name: Execute integer programming pairing optimization
l4_steps.input: Filtered pairing library, cost objective (minimize hotel, deadhead, duty cost)
l4_steps.output: Optimized pairing solution with full flight coverage
l4_steps.kpi: Pairing cost per block hour ≤$22 benchmark; solver convergence within 2 hrs
l4_steps.pain_point: Column-generation solver can converge to local optima on irregular or charter-heavy schedules, requiring manual seed pairing injection and re-run, which add 3–5 hrs to cycle time

l4_steps.name: Validate 100% flight coverage in optimized solution
l4_steps.input: Optimized pairing solution
l4_steps.output: Coverage validation report; list of uncovered flights if any
l4_steps.kpi: 100% flight coverage — zero uncovered departures at validation
l4_steps.pain_point: Last-minute schedule insertions post-optimization leave uncovered flights requiring manual pairing construction; no automated re-trigger exists in current Jeppesen deployment

l4_steps.name: Assess hotel and per-diem cost against budget targets
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management + SAP S/4HANA Finance (FI/CO)
l4_steps.input: Optimized pairing plan, hotel contract rate file, CBA per-diem schedule
l4_steps.output: Crew cost estimate vs. budget variance report
l4_steps.kpi: Layover hotel cost ≤$85/night average; total pairing cost within 5% of budget
l4_steps.pain_point: Hotel contract gaps at thin-market outstations force use of non-preferred vendors exceeding CBA per-diem caps; contract database in SAP not always current with Jeppesen cost model

l4_steps.name: Run CBA work rule validation on all pairings
l4_steps.input: Optimized pairing set, CBA rules library (versioned)
l4_steps.output: CBA compliance report with pass/fail per pairing
l4_steps.kpi: CBA violation rate <0.5% at initial validation run
l4_steps.pain_point: CBA rules for minimum rest, trip rig provisions, and max monthly hours are version-controlled; mismatches between Jeppesen rule builds and actual contract language cause violations that trigger formal grievances

l4_steps.name: Resolve CBA violations via manual pairing edit
l4_steps.input: CBA violation report, flagged pairings
l4_steps.output: Corrected pairings with no CBA violations
l4_steps.kpi: All violations resolved within 4 hrs; zero violations at final publish
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual edits to resolve CBA violations frequently create secondary coverage gaps or cost overruns, requiring iterative re-optimization loops that compress downstream rostering windows

l4_steps.name: Build crew roster lines from approved pairing set
l4_steps.input: Approved pairing set, roster period calendar, CBA day-off requirements
l4_steps.output: Draft roster lines with guaranteed time, days off, and pairing assignments
l4_steps.kpi: Average monthly guaranteed-time utilization ≥82% of CBA contractual maximum
l4_steps.pain_point: Constructing balanced roster lines that satisfy min/max flying-time guarantees across all domiciles while meeting productivity targets is highly constrained during holiday and off-peak schedule reductions

l4_steps.name: Allocate reserve crew coverage by domicile
l4_steps.input: Draft roster lines, 12-month historical disruption and sick-call rates
l4_steps.output: Reserve crew allocation plan per domicile and day type
l4_steps.kpi: Reserve coverage ratio ≥110% of projected daily sick/IRROP requirement
l4_steps.pain_point: Reserve sizing driven by IRROP scenarios requires holding excess reserves above minimum-legal levels, increasing direct crew costs by ~8%; Jeppesen reserve modelling does not natively simulate multi-day disruption cascades

l4_steps.name: Publish bid package to crew self-service portal
l4_steps.input: Finalized roster lines, reserve allocation, CBA bid lead-time requirement
l4_steps.output: Bid package published for crew seniority-based self-bidding
l4_steps.kpi: Bid package published ≥21 days before period start per CBA; 100% of lines posted
l4_steps.pain_point: Delays in schedule finalization from network planning compress bid publication windows; missing the 21-day CBA requirement triggers grievance procedures and potential arbitration costs

l4_steps.name: Process crew bids and award by seniority
l4_steps.input: Submitted crew bids, current seniority list
l4_steps.output: Awarded roster assignments per crew member
l4_steps.kpi: Bid award accuracy ≥99.9%; zero seniority inversion errors
l4_steps.pain_point: Seniority list discrepancies from SAP SuccessFactors HR integration can cause bid inversions; manual corrections require re-award runs and generate formal grievances under the CBA

l4_steps.name: Publish final rosters and sync to PSS
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management + Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Awarded bid assignments, PSS crew manifest interface
l4_steps.output: Published crew rosters; crew manifest updated in Altéa PSS
l4_steps.kpi: Roster publication ≥14 days before period start; PSS sync completed within 1 hr
l4_steps.pain_point: Roster-to-PSS sync failures cause crew check-in discrepancies at airports; bidirectional reconciliation between Jeppesen and Altéa is not fully automated, requiring manual exception clearing

l4_steps.name: Import approved pairings into rostering module
l4_steps.input: Approved crew pairing solution exported from CM-01 pairing optimisation
l4_steps.output: Pairing library loaded into rostering module for the bid period
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of approved pairings imported with zero data loss; import completed ≤2 hours after CM-01 sign-off
l4_steps.pain_point: Pairing handoff format mismatches between Jeppesen pairing and rostering modules cause silent truncation of augmented-crew flags — manual audit required for long-haul pairings

l4_steps.name: Configure bid period parameters and CBA rules
l4_steps.input: Flight schedule, collective bargaining agreement (CBA), bidding calendar, vacation approval list
l4_steps.output: Bid period configuration: dates, block-hour limits, vacation slots, trip-trade eligibility rules
l4_steps.kpi: Bid package published ≥21 days before period start per CBA; 0 rule-configuration errors at bid launch
l4_steps.pain_point: CBA rule amendments require manual reconfiguration of Jeppesen constraint tables — no automated ingestion from contract management system; misconfigurations discovered only when crew protests are filed

l4_steps.name: Validate crew qualification and fleet eligibility
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management + Boeing Toolbox / CAMP
l4_steps.input: Crew qualification records, recurrent training schedule, expiry dates from training tracking system
l4_steps.output: Eligible crew list segmented by fleet type and seat position for bid period
l4_steps.kpi: 0 unqualified crew included in bid package; eligibility validation completed ≥25 days before period start
l4_steps.pain_point: Qualification expiry records in Boeing Toolbox / CAMP sync to Jeppesen with a 24–48-hour lag — risk of including crew whose type-rating or medical lapses within the bid window

l4_steps.name: Publish bid package to crew self-service portal
l4_steps.input: Finalized pairing library, bid period configuration, eligible crew list
l4_steps.output: Published bid package accessible to all eligible crew via CrewPortal and mobile app
l4_steps.kpi: Bid package live ≥21 days before bid close; 0 incorrect or duplicate pairings in published package
l4_steps.pain_point: Late schedule changes after bid publication require reissuing the full package, compressing crew bid time below the CBA-mandated minimum — triggers grievance filings and OCC planning disruption

l4_steps.name: Capture ranked bid preferences from crew members
l4_steps.input: Published bid package, personal scheduling preferences, personal rest requirements
l4_steps.output: Ranked preference list submitted per crew member; system timestamp of each submission
l4_steps.kpi: Bid submission rate ≥95% by deadline; average ranking depth ≥15 preferences per crew member
l4_steps.pain_point: Mobile app version fragmentation causes intermittent bid submission failures for crew on older devices — preference loss occurs without error confirmation, leading to unintended default-assignment triggers

l4_steps.name: Validate bid completeness and close bidding window
l4_steps.input: Submitted crew bids, bid deadline, CBA late-bid rules
l4_steps.output: Validated bid dataset; list of non-bidders flagged for reserve-rule default assignment
l4_steps.kpi: 100% bid validation completed within 2 hours of bid close; non-bidder list issued to planning team within 1 hour
l4_steps.pain_point: Non-bidders assigned by reserve default rules increase reserve utilisation pressure during high-absence periods (holidays, training blocks), reducing buffer for day-of-operations coverage

l4_steps.name: Run automated seniority-based bid award algorithm
l4_steps.input: Validated crew bids, seniority list, pairing library, block-hour limits per crew
l4_steps.output: Draft roster with bid awards allocated by seniority order; uncovered-pairing exception list
l4_steps.kpi: Automated award covers ≥85% of pairings without manual intervention; optimisation run completes <3 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Seniority-driven award algorithm creates systematic clustering — junior crew receive chronically undesirable pairings, driving grievance filings and attrition at base cities with high seniority concentration

l4_steps.name: Apply FRMS fatigue constraints to draft roster
l4_steps.input: Draft roster, crew duty history for prior 90 days, rest period records
l4_steps.output: FRMS-validated roster with per-crew fatigue index scores; list of crew flagged above threshold
l4_steps.kpi: 0 crew assigned duties with predicted fatigue index >70 (Jeppesen FRMS 0–100 scale); FRMS validation completed <2 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: FRMS scoring relies on self-reported rest periods logged in CrewPortal — inaccurate entries produce false-compliant rosters that trigger FRMS alerts only on the day of operation when it is too late to rebalance

l4_steps.name: Check FAR Part 117 duty and rest compliance
l4_steps.input: FRMS-validated draft roster, FAR Part 117 / EASA FTL rule set, augmented-crew designation flags
l4_steps.output: Compliance report per crew member; list of FAR Part 117 violations with step-number reference
l4_steps.kpi: 0 FAR Part 117 violations in roster at publication; compliance check completed <4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Augmented-crew provisions under FAR Part 117 §117.21 are not fully parameterised in Jeppesen — ultra-long-range pairings require manual override and legal review, adding 24–48 hours to the rostering cycle

l4_steps.name: Resolve uncovered pairings via reserve assignment
l4_steps.input: Uncovered pairing list, qualified reserve crew availability, CBA reserve-call rules
l4_steps.output: Fully covered draft roster with reserve assignments documented; updated reserve utilisation report
l4_steps.kpi: 0 uncovered pairings at draft finalisation; reserve utilisation ≤30% of available reserve pool
l4_steps.pain_point: Reserve pool insufficiency during peak holiday bid periods forces voluntary overtime — CBA premium-pay triggers create budget variance of up to 15% above planned crew cost in Q4

l4_steps.name: Review and adjudicate crew bid award protests
l4_steps.input: Crew grievance and protest submissions, draft roster, CBA seniority and award rules
l4_steps.output: Adjudicated roster with documented award rationale per disputed assignment
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of bid protests resolved within 5 business days per CBA; protest rate <2% of total crew bids
l4_steps.pain_point: Seniority disputes requiring CBA interpretation escalate to labor relations, extending resolution timelines and delaying roster finalisation — unresolved protests at publication date force provisional assignments

l4_steps.name: Incorporate pre-approved trip trades and swaps
l4_steps.input: Pre-approved trip trade requests, adjudicated roster, qualification matrix
l4_steps.output: Updated roster with pre-period swaps incorporated; qualification validation report for all traded duties
l4_steps.kpi: Trip trade approval cycle ≤48 hours; 0 qualification violations resulting from approved trades
l4_steps.pain_point: Trip trades approved outside Jeppesen via email bypass the system's built-in qualification check — latent safety risk discovered only at crew sign-in when crew tracking flags the mismatch

l4_steps.name: Obtain final compliance sign-off and lock roster
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management + AWS S3 / Redshift (compliance audit log)
l4_steps.input: Final roster, FAR Part 117 compliance report, FRMS validation summary
l4_steps.output: Signed compliance certificate; roster record locked against further edits; audit log entry written to AWS data lake
l4_steps.kpi: Compliance sign-off completed ≥5 days before period start; 0 open violations at sign-off
l4_steps.pain_point: Compliance audit trail stored in a separate AWS S3/Redshift data lake has no direct linkage to the Jeppesen roster record — reconstructing evidence for FAA audit queries requires manual correlation across two systems

l4_steps.name: Publish final roster and notify crew via portal
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management (CrewPortal) + airline push-notification service
l4_steps.input: Locked compliant roster, crew contact preferences
l4_steps.output: Published roster visible in CrewPortal; push notifications sent to crew mobile devices; acknowledgment tracking open
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of crew notified within 1 hour of publication; crew acknowledgment rate ≥90% within 48 hours of release
l4_steps.pain_point: Push-notification delivery rates drop to ~70% for crew on international layovers with low cellular connectivity — crew risk missing roster start dates, forcing manual telephone outreach by crew scheduling

l4_steps.name: Distribute final roster data feed to OCC
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management + SITA Airport Management System (AMS)
l4_steps.input: Published final roster
l4_steps.output: Crew roster data feed ingested by OCC systems; gate and stand planning inputs updated with crew assignments
l4_steps.kpi: Roster data available in OCC within 30 minutes of publication; 0 data-sync errors in first 24 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Roster-to-OCC data feed uses legacy SFTP batch transfer rather than a real-time API — the resulting 30-minute lag means OCC operates on stale crew assignments during the handoff window, creating conflict risk for back-to-back duty pairings

l4_steps.name: Pull daily crew duty roster from CMS
l4_steps.input: Published monthly roster, intraday amendments, real-time crew updates
l4_steps.output: Day-of-operations crew duty list with flight assignments and report times
l4_steps.kpi: Roster accuracy ≥99% match to published pairings; list generated ≥3 hrs before first departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Late roster amendments from crew bidding workflow can cause data sync lag between Jeppesen and Altéa PSS, risking crew data mismatches at check-in during hub-complex rotations

l4_steps.name: Send automated duty-start notifications to crew
l4_steps.input: Day-of-operations crew duty list, crew contact and mobile app registration database
l4_steps.output: SMS and app push notifications with report time, flight number, aircraft registration, and gate
l4_steps.kpi: Notification delivery rate ≥99.5% within 30 min of duty window opening; read-receipt confirmed for ≥90% of app-registered crew
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew mobile app adoption varies across base seniority groups; SMS fallback provides no read-receipt confirmation, creating unverified notification risk for critical duty changes during irregular operations

l4_steps.name: Verify crew check-in at required report time
l4_steps.input: Crew self-reported check-in entries, kiosk or app check-in timestamps, scheduled report times
l4_steps.output: Confirmed check-in log; no-show flag with timestamp for absent crew members
l4_steps.kpi: On-time check-in rate ≥98%; no-show detection and standby activation trigger within 15 min of missed report time
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual check-in verification at outstations with no dedicated crew desk compresses the standby activation window; regional airport staffing gaps mean no-shows may not be detected until gate agents escalate, often inside 60 min to departure

l4_steps.name: Validate crew qualifications, recency & type currency
l4_steps.input: Crew training records from LMS integration, qualification and recency database, aircraft type assignment
l4_steps.output: Qualification check pass/fail decision; restriction flags forwarded to pairing optimizer
l4_steps.kpi: Zero qualified-crew-on-illegal-assignment incidents; automated compliance check runtime ≤2 min per crew member
l4_steps.pain_point: Training record sync delays between the airline LMS and Jeppesen can allow stale qualification data to persist, creating regulatory exposure under FAR Part 61 if a crew member's type rating lapse is not reflected in the CMS before duty commencement

l4_steps.name: Initialize duty period clock & FRMS baseline
l4_steps.input: Confirmed check-in timestamp, crew fatigue risk profile, prior-duty rest duration
l4_steps.output: Active duty record with ACTT (Applicable Cumulative Trip Time) counter initialized; FRMS alerting thresholds set
l4_steps.kpi: Duty record initialization within 5 min of check-in confirmation; FRMS baseline computed for 100% of active crew
l4_steps.pain_point: FRMS models calibrated on aggregate fleet data may underestimate fatigue for crew transitioning from high-density transcontinental rotations into back-to-back short-haul turns, particularly where rest was taken across multiple time zones

l4_steps.name: Monitor real-time duty time against FAR Part 117 limits
l4_steps.input: ACARS flight departure and arrival timestamps, active duty records, FAR Part 117 FDP and rest parameters
l4_steps.output: Running duty time totals per crew member; automated alerts triggered at 90% of applicable limit thresholds
l4_steps.kpi: Zero FAR Part 117 FDP exceedances; alert triggered ≥60 min before any limit breach; alert-to-action response time ≤10 min
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS timestamp delays at congested hub airports (e.g., ORD, ATL) can cause duty time calculations to lag actual operations by 5–12 min, compressing the crew controller's response window before a legally binding FDP limit is reached

l4_steps.name: Calculate projected rest requirement & next availability
l4_steps.input: Projected duty end time, FAR Part 117 minimum rest table, hotel inventory data from accommodation vendor API
l4_steps.output: Minimum rest end timestamp; crew availability window for next assignment; hotel block release notification
l4_steps.kpi: Rest calculation accuracy ±0 min (regulatory requirement); hotel release notification issued within 30 min of projected rest start; ≥95% of rest-period hotel blocks confirmed before duty release
l4_steps.pain_point: Hotel inventory management for irregular operations is handled outside the CMS via a separate vendor portal, requiring manual coordination that increases the risk of accommodation errors and delays crew rest commencement, eroding the legally mandated minimum rest period

l4_steps.name: Track crew-to-aircraft assignment via ACARS OOOI data
l4_steps.input: Aircraft OOOI (Out/Off/On/In) movement messages, crew assignment records from Jeppesen CMS
l4_steps.output: Real-time crew-aircraft match or mismatch status per flight sector
l4_steps.kpi: Crew position update latency ≤5 min after OOOI event; position mistrack rate <0.5% of daily operated sectors
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS message dropouts in remote or oceanic airspace create position gaps; fallback to manual satellite phone verification adds 15–20 min lag, which is operationally critical for connecting crew or minimum-rest rotations at outstation overnight bases

l4_steps.name: Confirm crew on-board status against PSS manifest
l4_steps.input: Boarding pass scan data, crew manifest from CMS-to-PSS integration feed
l4_steps.output: Confirmed crew on-board record per flight; late-boarding or missing-crew flag escalated to crew desk
l4_steps.kpi: Crew boarding confirmation ≥15 min before STD; zero departures with unresolved unconfirmed crew status
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa crew manifest data refresh depends on the Jeppesen–Altéa integration batch cycle; if the interface runs on a 10-min cadence, last-minute crew swaps may not be reflected in the PSS boarding system, triggering false missing-crew alerts and unnecessary departure holds

l4_steps.name: Update crew position records after each completed sector
l4_steps.input: OOOI timestamps from ACARS, gate arrival confirmation, crew pairing sequence
l4_steps.output: Updated crew position records with current station; next-sector readiness status flag
l4_steps.kpi: Position record updated within 10 min of IN event; data accuracy ≥99.8% match to ACARS source timestamps
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-leg rotations with short turn times under 45 min risk position record overwrites if the prior segment's IN event message arrives after the subsequent segment's OUT event has already been logged, creating a phantom dual-assignment state in the CMS

l4_steps.name: Receive & triage crew-impacting disruption alerts from NOC
l4_steps.input: Flight delay and cancellation alerts from NOC disruption board, ATC ground stop and GDP notifications
l4_steps.output: Crew impact assessment listing affected pairings, downstream connections, and estimated delay propagation
l4_steps.kpi: Initial crew impact assessment within 10 min of disruption notification; zero unacknowledged disruption alerts aged >15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: NOC disruption data feeds into the CMS via a polling API; 5-min polling intervals can delay crew controller awareness of fast-moving ATC programs or ground stops at high-traffic hubs, shortening the window available to proactively cover downstream crew illegalities

l4_steps.name: Assess revised schedule legality for impacted crew
l4_steps.input: Revised flight schedule from operations control, active crew duty records, FAR Part 117 FDP and rest parameters
l4_steps.output: Legal or illegal status for each impacted crew member under revised schedule; extension waiver eligibility flags
l4_steps.kpi: Legality check completed within 15 min of disruption triage; waiver utilization rate <5% of disrupted operations; zero post-event FAR Part 117 violations
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen's automated solver engine may time out on complex network disruptions affecting 20 or more crew simultaneously, requiring manual controller override and extending resolution time beyond the OTP recovery window, particularly during hub-wide weather events

l4_steps.name: Source and assign replacement or standby crew
l4_steps.input: Standby crew availability list, deadhead crew pool, hotel and accommodation records, airport reserve pool by base
l4_steps.output: Confirmed crew reassignment with pairing details; standby activation record; deadhead authorization if applicable
l4_steps.kpi: Standby crew activated within 30 min of need identification; deadhead crew positioned within 2 hrs; crew coverage rate ≥97% of disrupted flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Standby pool sizing is optimized for statistically expected disruption levels; severe weather events causing hub ground stops exceeding 4 hrs exhaust local standby pools, forcing cross-base deadhead that itself consumes FAR Part 117 FDP, further compressing available duty time for replacement crews

l4_steps.name: Issue crew reassignment notifications & sync downstream systems
l4_steps.input: Confirmed reassignment records from Jeppesen CMS
l4_steps.output: Push notifications delivered to affected crew; updated pairings in CMS; Altéa PSS crew manifest refreshed; payroll audit trail updated
l4_steps.kpi: Crew notification sent within 5 min of reassignment confirmation; CMS-to-PSS sync completed before gate opens (≥30 min before STD); notification delivery confirmation rate ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Cascading reassignments in multi-hub disruptions generate notification storms; crew mobile app rate limits and carrier network congestion at hub airports cause delivery delays precisely during peak disruption windows when accurate crew information is most critical

l4_steps.name: Confirm crew sign-off & record actual duty-out time
l4_steps.input: Crew self-reported duty-out via mobile app or kiosk, gate departure records, hotel check-in confirmation where applicable
l4_steps.output: Closed duty record with actual block-out to duty-release timestamps; open duty record flag for anomalies
l4_steps.kpi: Duty record closed within 1 hr of crew release; sign-off discrepancy rate <1% of operated duties; open duty record resolution within 4 hrs
l4_steps.pain_point: Overnight outstations with no crew desk rely entirely on self-reported sign-off via mobile app; connectivity issues at regional airports cause delayed uploads, creating open duty records that block the next crew scheduling build cycle and may delay payroll processing

l4_steps.name: Recalculate 28-day cumulative flight & duty hours
l4_steps.input: Closed duty records, FAR Part 117 cumulative limits (100 hrs per 672-hr window, 1,000 hrs per calendar year), crew fatigue history
l4_steps.output: Updated 28-day and 365-day flight and duty time totals per crew member; scheduling availability flags for next build cycle
l4_steps.kpi: Fatigue record updated within 2 hrs of duty close; zero crew members scheduled before 28-day rolling total validated; cumulative total accuracy ±0 min
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 117 rolling window calculations across international timezone boundaries introduce date-ambiguity edge cases in legacy CMS implementations, historically requiring manual audit for transmeridian crew rotations and generating compliance review backlog during peak international operation periods

l4_steps.name: Archive duty records & sync actuals to scheduling and payroll
l4_steps.input: Validated duty records with actual block times, fatigue recalculation output
l4_steps.output: Archived duty data package; payroll hours feed to SAP S/4HANA Finance (FI/CO); scheduling feedback to crew pairing optimizer for next build cycle
l4_steps.kpi: Payroll data handoff to SAP within 24 hrs of duty close; scheduling feedback loop complete before next crew build cycle (T+48 hrs); archive integrity check ≥99.99%
l4_steps.pain_point: Discrepancies between Jeppesen actual block hours and SAP payroll-recognized hours require manual reconciliation by crew admin; during irregular operations months, reconciliation volume can exceed crew administration capacity, delaying accurate payroll for 2–5% of crew members and generating grievance risk under collective bargaining agreements

l4_steps.name: Pull crew schedule and rest window data
l4_steps.input: Published crew roster and pairing assignments
l4_steps.output: Rest window dataset per crew member for next 72 hours
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of crew records extracted ≤15 min before duty window opens
l4_steps.pain_point: Roster amendments late in the day can invalidate pre-computed rest windows; Jeppesen batch refresh cycles may lag real-time pairing changes by up to 30 minutes

l4_steps.name: Validate minimum rest vs FAR 117.25 requirement
l4_steps.input: Rest window dataset from step 1.1
l4_steps.output: Rest compliance flag (Pass/Fail) per crew member
l4_steps.kpi: Zero crew members assigned with <10-hr rest or <8-hr sleep opportunity; compliance check completed ≥4 hrs before scheduled report time
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR 117.25 requires rest free from all restraint including deadhead travel; mis-classification of deadhead as rest is a common audit finding and can trigger FAA enforcement action

l4_steps.name: Escalate non-compliant rest to Crew Scheduling
l4_steps.input: Fail-flagged crew records from step 1.2
l4_steps.output: Replacement or re-routing request logged in crew scheduling queue
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of rest violations resolved ≥2 hrs before report time; zero crew members reporting for duty with open violation
l4_steps.pain_point: Replacement pool exhaustion during irregular operations forces cascading re-assignments; lack of real-time hotel check-in data makes actual sleep opportunity difficult to verify

l4_steps.name: Calculate maximum FDP from Table B/C values
l4_steps.input: Report time (local), number of scheduled flight segments, acclimation status
l4_steps.output: Maximum FDP in hours per FAR 117.13 Table B (unaugmented) or Table C (augmented)
l4_steps.kpi: FDP calculation completed ≤5 min per crew pairing; 100% of FDPs within published table limits before sign-out
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR 117 Table B/C values vary by report time window; scheduling systems may default to most permissive bracket if report time is ambiguous, creating compliance risk on early-morning or red-eye pairings

l4_steps.name: Determine if augmented crew operations apply
l4_steps.input: Crew complement (2 vs 3+ pilots), planned in-flight rest facility class
l4_steps.output: Augmented operations flag and applicable FDP extension allowance
l4_steps.kpi: Augmented classification accuracy ≥99.9%; mis-classification rate <1 per quarter
l4_steps.pain_point: Rest facility class (Class 1/2/3) on the aircraft must match the assumption in the FDP extension; discrepancies between charter configuration and published aircraft spec cause mid-trip compliance gaps

l4_steps.name: Apply FDP extension if operationally justified
l4_steps.input: Operational need justification, augmented crew flag, crew consent
l4_steps.output: Approved FDP extension record (max 1-hr, once per calendar day per FAR 117.19)
l4_steps.kpi: FDP extensions ≤5% of total monthly pairings; no extension applied without documented crew consent
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR 117.19 limits extension to once per calendar day and requires crew concurrence; pressure from operations control to extend without concurrence is a recurring safety culture risk

l4_steps.name: Authorize FDP and issue pre-departure brief
l4_steps.input: Validated FDP, rest compliance records, pairing details
l4_steps.output: Signed FDP authorization record; crew brief packet distributed
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of crew departures with FDP authorization on file; brief packet delivered ≥60 min before report time
l4_steps.pain_point: Digital brief distribution depends on crew mobile app connectivity; offline crews at remote outstations may not receive updates, requiring phone confirmation fallback

l4_steps.name: Monitor real-time duty time against FDP limits
l4_steps.input: Live ACARS/ADS-B block times, ATC delay feeds, gate departure confirmations
l4_steps.output: Running FDP counter per crew member updated every 15 minutes
l4_steps.kpi: Real-time duty counter latency ≤15 min; alert triggered ≥30 min before projected FDP breach
l4_steps.pain_point: ATC ground delays extend FDP without triggering automatic alerts if block-out time is used as the FDP clock start; ambiguity between pushback and engine-start as FDP trigger creates audit exposure

l4_steps.name: Receive and log crew fatigue self-declaration
l4_steps.input: Crew member fatigue declaration via crew portal or ACARS datalink
l4_steps.output: Fatigue event record with timestamp, flight number, and crew ID
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of fatigue declarations acknowledged by Crew Tracking within 10 min; zero declarations closed without resolution note
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR 117.9 gives crew unlimited authority to declare fatigue; ground pressure to continue operations despite declaration is a safety culture issue tracked in ASAP/SMS; anonymous reporting gap remains if crew fear punitive response

l4_steps.name: Coordinate AOC for substitution or flight delay
l4_steps.input: Fatigue declaration or projected FDP breach from steps 3.1–3.2
l4_steps.output: Replacement crew assignment or delay/cancellation decision logged in AOC system
l4_steps.kpi: Replacement crew sourced ≤90 min from declaration for flights with >2 hrs to departure; cancellation rate due to fatigue <0.1% of monthly operations
l4_steps.pain_point: Reserve pools at outstations are thin; during IROPS a single fatigue declaration can cascade into multi-flight cancellations if no qualified crew is within legal deadhead range

l4_steps.name: Calculate 60-hr limit in 168 consecutive hours
l4_steps.input: Historical flight duty records for prior 168 hours per crew member
l4_steps.output: Rolling 60-hr utilisation figure per crew member; alert if ≥85% (51 hrs)
l4_steps.kpi: Zero crew members exceeding 60-hr limit; alert threshold triggered at 51 hrs to allow scheduling intervention
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen rolling-window calculation relies on accurate block-in times; late ACARS updates during IROPS create data gaps that cause the 168-hr window to be computed from estimated rather than actual times

l4_steps.name: Calculate 190-hr limit in 672 consecutive hours
l4_steps.input: Historical flight duty records for prior 672 hours per crew member
l4_steps.output: Rolling 190-hr utilisation figure; alert if ≥85% (162 hrs)
l4_steps.kpi: Zero crew members exceeding 190-hr limit in any 28-day window; alert generated ≥10 days before projected breach
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew pick-up flying during high-demand periods (holiday banks, peak summer) can push cumulative limits faster than monthly bidding models project; late additions to open-time are the primary cause of 190-hr violations

l4_steps.name: Track annual 1,000-hr flight time limit
l4_steps.input: Year-to-date flight time log per crew member (block hours)
l4_steps.output: Annual flight time projection and alert if ≥900 hrs (90% of limit)
l4_steps.kpi: Zero crew members exceeding 1,000 flight hours in any calendar year; 90% threshold alert issued ≥45 days before year-end for projected breaches
l4_steps.pain_point: Annual limit interacts with contract maximums and PBS bid awards; crew members approaching the limit late in Q4 reduce reserve coverage exactly when holiday operations demand peaks

l4_steps.name: Remove near-limit crew and notify Crew Planning
l4_steps.input: Alert flags from steps 4.1–4.3
l4_steps.output: Crew member status updated to limit-protected; open pairings returned to scheduling pool
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of limit-alert crew removed from active schedule within 2 hrs of alert; zero limit violations in FAA audit sample
l4_steps.pain_point: Removing crew mid-rotation at an outstation forces last-minute positioning of replacements; hotel and transportation costs associated with early release are not always captured in scheduling cost models

l4_steps.name: Aggregate fatigue events in FRMS database
l4_steps.input: Fatigue declarations, FDP breaches, near-limit alerts from phases 3–4
l4_steps.output: Consolidated FRMS event dataset with route, crew base, pairing-type dimensions
l4_steps.kpi: FRMS dataset refreshed within 24 hrs of event; 100% of fatigue events linked to pairing and route data
l4_steps.pain_point: FRMS data lives in a separate analytics store from Jeppesen operational data; ETL latency and schema mismatches between crew scheduling and safety systems delay monthly trend analysis by 3–5 days

l4_steps.name: Analyse fatigue patterns by route, base, pairing type
l4_steps.input: FRMS event dataset from step 5.1
l4_steps.output: Monthly FRMS trend report with heat-map by route and crew base
l4_steps.kpi: FRMS report issued within 5 business days of month-end; ≥3 pairing types or routes reviewed per cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: Small event counts per route make statistical significance difficult to establish; safety analysts lack crew scheduling write-back access to act directly on findings without a manual change-request workflow

l4_steps.name: Revise pairings and notify Safety Review Board
l4_steps.input: FRMS trend report identifying systemic fatigue risk in specific pairings
l4_steps.output: Revised pairing set submitted for next bid period; Safety Review Board notification issued
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of systemic-risk pairings revised within 2 bid periods of identification; recurrence rate of flagged pairing type <20% after revision
l4_steps.pain_point: Pairing revisions that improve fatigue compliance may reduce utilisation efficiency and increase crew costs; trade-off approval requires VP-level sign-off which extends lead time by 2–4 weeks

l4_steps.name: Generate FAR 117 compliance report for FAA
l4_steps.input: Duty records, rest logs, FDP authorizations, fatigue event records for reporting period
l4_steps.output: FAR Part 117 compliance report (quarterly); violation summary if applicable
l4_steps.kpi: Report submitted ≥5 business days before FAA due date; zero data gaps in duty record coverage
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA may request ad hoc audits beyond scheduled reporting; retrieving complete duty records for specific crew members across legacy and current systems takes 3–5 days if data spans a system migration boundary

l4_steps.name: File voluntary disclosure or corrective action plan
l4_steps.input: Identified FAR 117 violations from compliance report
l4_steps.output: FAA voluntary disclosure (ASAP) submission or corrective action plan on file
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of identified violations disclosed within 10 business days; corrective action plan implemented within 60 days of disclosure
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA ASAP program requires an established MOU with the local FSDO; airlines without an active ASAP agreement lose the enforcement mitigation benefit and face higher civil penalty exposure for self-disclosed violations

l4_steps.name: Identify expiring crew certifications
l4_steps.input: Crew qualification records, certificate expiry calendar
l4_steps.output: List of crew members with certifications expiring within 90 days
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of expiring certs identified ≥60 days before expiry
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen qualification module requires manual reconciliation with FAA IACRA records; mismatches cause last-minute groundings when discrepancies surface during pre-flight checks

l4_steps.name: Map requirements against FAR/AQP framework
l4_steps.input: Expiry list, FAR Part 61/63/65 requirements, airline AQP approval document
l4_steps.output: Per-crew training requirement matrix (type rating, recurrent, PC, OE, SEP)
l4_steps.kpi: Requirement matrix accuracy ≥99% vs. FAA-approved AQP schedule
l4_steps.pain_point: Airlines with FAA-approved AQP have different recurrency intervals than standard FAR Part 135/121 defaults; Jeppesen must be manually configured per AQP module or will generate false compliance gaps

l4_steps.name: Validate requirements against fleet qualification matrix
l4_steps.input: Training requirement matrix, aircraft type endorsements per crew member
l4_steps.output: Validated training plan with fleet-specific simulator variant assignments
l4_steps.kpi: Zero invalid simulator variant assignments at time of booking
l4_steps.pain_point: Fleet commonality assumptions (e.g. 737-700 vs. 737 MAX 8 differences) can result in incorrect simulator type bookings; reconfigured MAX simulators require separate certification after Boeing grounding

l4_steps.name: Generate training schedule and crew assignments
l4_steps.input: Validated training plan, simulator availability calendar, crew contract bid periods
l4_steps.output: Draft training schedule with crew-to-session assignments
l4_steps.kpi: Training schedule published ≥45 days before earliest session date
l4_steps.pain_point: CAE SimFinity scheduling does not natively integrate with Jeppesen rostering; double-bookings arise when crew are simultaneously assigned to flying duties and simulator sessions during the same duty period

l4_steps.name: Check crew scheduling conflicts and FAR legality
l4_steps.input: Draft training schedule, current crew pairing and rostering data
l4_steps.output: Conflict-free training assignments with FAR Part 117 rest compliance confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Zero training assignments that violate FAR Part 117 rest or duty limits
l4_steps.pain_point: Simulator sessions count as duty time under FAR Part 117 but are often omitted from crew duty calculators; non-compliance discovered late in scheduling cycle forces expensive last-minute crew swaps

l4_steps.name: Reserve simulator slots and instructor resources
l4_steps.input: Conflict-free training assignments, simulator capacity at CAE/FlightSafety facilities
l4_steps.output: Confirmed simulator reservations and instructor assignments
l4_steps.kpi: Simulator utilisation rate ≥85%; booking cancellation rate ≤5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Industry-wide simulator capacity constraints (limited Level D 737 MAX simulators globally) cause lead times of 6–12 weeks; last-minute certificate expirations cannot be accommodated without costly wet-lease of third-party simulator time

l4_steps.name: Notify crew of training assignments and prerequisites
l4_steps.input: Confirmed simulator reservations, eLearning pre-requisite course list
l4_steps.output: Training notification delivered to crew via crew portal; pre-study materials assigned in LMS
l4_steps.kpi: Crew acknowledgement of training assignment ≥95% within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew portal notification fatigue leads to missed acknowledgements; no escalation workflow in SAP SuccessFactors Learning to flag non-response to crew base managers automatically

l4_steps.name: Deliver CBT and ground school modules
l4_steps.input: Crew training assignment, eLearning modules (systems, procedures, emergency)
l4_steps.output: Completed CBT records with pass/fail scores per module
l4_steps.kpi: CBT completion rate ≥98% before simulator session; average CBT pass rate ≥90% on first attempt
l4_steps.pain_point: CBT content refresh lags behind Boeing and Airbus service bulletin cycles; crews may train on outdated emergency procedure content if LMS version control is not tightly managed with OEM curriculum releases

l4_steps.name: Execute simulator training session (PC/OE/LOFT)
l4_steps.input: Simulator briefing pack, AQP Maneuvers Requirements Table (MRT), crew pairing for session
l4_steps.output: Completed simulator session log with performance ratings per MRT maneuver
l4_steps.kpi: Session completion rate ≥97%; average maneuver proficiency score ≥3.0/4.0 on CAST/AQP rubric
l4_steps.pain_point: CAE SimFinity session logs are stored locally at training centre; real-time sync to Jeppesen qualification records requires manual file export and upload, creating a 24–48h data latency window during which crew show as non-current in scheduling systems

l4_steps.name: Verify attendance and training hours compliance
l4_steps.input: Simulator session logs, ground school attendance records
l4_steps.output: Verified training completion certificate with total contact hours
l4_steps.kpi: Attendance verification completed within 24h of session end; zero incomplete records forwarded to assessment phase
l4_steps.pain_point: Partial session completions (e.g. simulator hardware fault mid-session) require FAA Operations Specification deviation approval before credit can be granted; no automated workflow in SAP SuccessFactors to flag partial completions for regulatory review

l4_steps.name: Administer written and oral knowledge exam
l4_steps.input: Completed ground school record, FAA-approved question bank
l4_steps.output: Exam result with pass/fail determination and topic-level breakdown
l4_steps.kpi: Exam pass rate ≥92% on first attempt; remedial re-exam scheduled within 7 days of failure
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA-approved question banks must be updated within 30 days of regulatory change (e.g. new NOTAM format, amended AOM chapter); SAP SuccessFactors Learning has no automated content update trigger linked to ATPCO or FAA rulemaking RSS feeds

l4_steps.name: Evaluate simulator checkride performance
l4_steps.input: AQP Maneuvers Requirements Table, simulator session video/data replay
l4_steps.output: Proficiency Check (PC) evaluation form; pass/fail recommendation per AQP standards
l4_steps.kpi: Checkride pass rate ≥95% on first attempt; debrief delivered within 1h of session end
l4_steps.pain_point: Under AQP, unsatisfactory grades must be correlated across crew cohorts to identify systemic training gaps vs. individual performance issues; CAE SimFinity does not natively produce cohort-level analytics — requires separate export to AWS Redshift for trend analysis

l4_steps.name: Process pass/fail outcome and assign remedial path
l4_steps.input: PC evaluation form, exam results, crew training history
l4_steps.output: Pass: qualification advancement triggered. Fail: remedial training plan with timeline and restricted flying status applied
l4_steps.kpi: Remedial plan issued within 24h of failure; restricted flying status applied in Jeppesen within 2h of fail determination
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen does not automatically restrict crew from scheduled flights upon a failed checkride — manual status update required; delay in status change creates legal exposure if a non-current crew member departs before the block is applied

l4_steps.name: Issue or renew certificate and update qualification record
l4_steps.system: FAA IACRA (Integrated Airman Certification and Rating Application)
l4_steps.input: Passed PC evaluation form, current pilot certificate data, airline training records
l4_steps.output: Updated FAA airman record; renewed type rating or recurrent certification on file
l4_steps.kpi: Certificate updated in FAA IACRA within 5 business days of checkride pass; zero expired certificates active in Jeppesen qualification module
l4_steps.pain_point: IACRA processing delays (common during peak season or after mass recurrent training cycles) can leave pilots in a limbo state — passed checkride but no updated certificate — requiring Temporary Authorisation letters that must be manually tracked outside automated systems

l4_steps.name: Sync updated qualifications to crew scheduling system
l4_steps.input: Updated FAA IACRA record, CAE SimFinity training completion data
l4_steps.output: Crew qualification profile updated in Jeppesen; crew cleared for line flying on qualified fleet type
l4_steps.kpi: Qualification sync completed within 4h of IACRA update; scheduling legality check auto-passed in Jeppesen within same window
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen qualification record sync relies on manual CSV import from FAA IACRA; no API integration exists, creating a reconciliation bottleneck during high-volume recurrent training months (typically January and July for most carriers)

l4_steps.name: Monitor upcoming recurrency expiry dates
l4_steps.input: Crew qualification profiles, recurrency interval rules (FAR 121.433, AQP cycle)
l4_steps.output: Rolling 90-day expiry dashboard updated daily; crew at-risk list generated
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of expiring qualifications flagged ≥60 days before expiry; dashboard refresh latency ≤1h
l4_steps.pain_point: AQP recurrency windows are qualification-event-based (not calendar-based), making rolling expiry calculation complex; Jeppesen's standard recurrency alert module applies calendar logic and generates false alarms for AQP-credentialed crew, reducing alert credibility

l4_steps.name: Trigger automated recurrency alert to crew and base manager
l4_steps.input: At-risk crew list, crew contact directory, base manager hierarchy
l4_steps.output: Automated alert sent to crew member (60-day) and base manager (30-day); training scheduling re-triggered
l4_steps.kpi: Alert delivery confirmation rate ≥99%; training re-scheduling initiated within 3 business days of 60-day alert
l4_steps.pain_point: Alert fatigue from Jeppesen's notification volume causes base managers to filter or ignore automated messages; no read-receipt or escalation logic exists in standard Jeppesen notification module — critical alerts are indistinguishable from routine operational messages

l4_steps.name: Escalate non-compliant crew to Crew Compliance team
l4_steps.input: Unresolved expiry alerts, crew scheduling status, FAA compliance reporting requirements
l4_steps.output: Non-compliant crew grounded in Jeppesen; compliance incident logged; corrective action plan issued to Director of Operations
l4_steps.kpi: Zero crew operating with lapsed certifications; escalation-to-grounding action completed within 2h of SLA breach
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA Certificate Management Office requires airlines to self-report systemic training programme non-compliance within 10 days; failure to ground and report non-compliant crew can trigger enforcement action under 14 CFR Part 13, including civil penalties up to $25,000 per violation per day

l4_steps.name: Ingest airman certificate data from FAA IACRA
l4_steps.system: FAA IACRA (Integrated Airman Certification and Rating Application)
l4_steps.input: Scheduled nightly sync trigger from FAA IACRA API
l4_steps.output: Refreshed airman certificate dataset with ATP, type rating, and medical records
l4_steps.kpi: Data sync completion rate ≥99.5%; sync latency <4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA IACRA API throttling during peak batch windows causes stale cert data; no real-time push — polling-only model creates up to 24-hour lag for urgent status changes

l4_steps.name: Risk-rank crew by certification expiry proximity
l4_steps.input: Refreshed IACRA certificate dataset; crew scheduling horizon (90-day window)
l4_steps.output: Risk-ranked crew list: Red (expiry <30 days), Amber (30–60 days), Green (>60 days)
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of crew with expiry <30 days flagged Red; zero missed flags
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen CM risk-ranking logic does not account for Special Issuance (SI) medical conditions with shorter validity windows, causing under-flagging of affected crew

l4_steps.name: Issue automated crew renewal notification
l4_steps.input: Risk-ranked crew list with Red/Amber flags
l4_steps.output: Automated email and in-app notification to crew member and Chief Pilot with renewal deadlines and action links
l4_steps.kpi: Notification delivery rate ≥99%; crew acknowledgement within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew members on extended international layovers or LOA may miss email alerts; no SMS or push notification fallback in current Jeppesen CM configuration

l4_steps.name: Submit MedXpress application for AME examination
l4_steps.input: Crew renewal notification; upcoming medical certificate expiry date
l4_steps.output: Completed FAA Form 8500-8 application submitted to designated AME; confirmation number issued
l4_steps.kpi: MedXpress submission completed ≥21 days before certificate expiry
l4_steps.pain_point: MedXpress portal outages during FAA system maintenance windows block submission; crew booking AME appointments within <14 days of expiry creates duty-coverage gaps

l4_steps.name: Conduct Class 1 AME physical examination
l4_steps.input: FAA Form 8500-8; crew member presenting at AME office
l4_steps.output: Completed physical examination; AME determination recorded in MedXpress
l4_steps.kpi: First-attempt Class 1 pass rate ≥92%; examination cycle time <2 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Age-40 rule requires captains over 40 to hold Class 1 medical renewed every 6 months (vs. 12 months under 40), doubling administrative burden for senior captain cohort; resource-intensive for AME network

l4_steps.name: Validate medical certificate against FAR Part 67
l4_steps.input: AME examination result and MedXpress determination
l4_steps.output: Medical certificate issued (valid) or Special Issuance referral / denial issued
l4_steps.kpi: Validation processing time <24 hours post-examination; Special Issuance cases escalated within 4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 67 Special Issuance (SI) for conditions such as hypertension or AASM-treated OSA requires FAA Regional Flight Surgeon review averaging 30–90 days, creating extended grounding risk for borderline cases

l4_steps.name: Upload validated medical certificate to crew record
l4_steps.input: Issued FAA First-Class medical certificate PDF; validation confirmation from MedXpress
l4_steps.output: Updated crew qualification record in Jeppesen CM with new medical expiry date; scheduling constraints lifted
l4_steps.kpi: Record update latency <2 hours post-certificate issue; zero scheduling errors attributable to stale medical data
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual PDF upload to Jeppesen CM creates transcription error risk; no automated IACRA-to-Jeppesen integration for medical records means dual-entry is required

l4_steps.name: Query aircraft type rating currency in Jeppesen CM
l4_steps.input: Updated crew record; assigned aircraft type (B737-700 / B737-800 / B737 MAX 8)
l4_steps.output: Type rating currency report showing rating issue date, expiry, and recency event log
l4_steps.kpi: Query response time <30 seconds; currency data accuracy ≥99.9% vs. FAA IACRA record
l4_steps.pain_point: B737 MAX 8 return-to-service post-2020 grounding introduced new FCTM differences training requirement tracked outside standard type rating schema in Jeppesen CM, causing manual gap-check overhead

l4_steps.name: Verify FAR 61.57 recency requirements for flight ops
l4_steps.input: Type rating currency report; recent flight log data from crew tracking module
l4_steps.output: Recency compliance determination: compliant or lapsed for each currency category (takeoff/landing, IFR, PIC)
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of crew checked for recency currency before schedule publication; zero recency violations detected post-assignment
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR 61.57(d) instrument currency requires 6 approaches in 6 months; crew returning from extended medical leave frequently have lapsed IFR currency not flagged until check-in, requiring last-minute schedule swaps

l4_steps.name: Schedule simulator proficiency check for lapsed recency
l4_steps.input: Recency lapse determination; simulator availability calendar
l4_steps.output: Simulator proficiency check event booked in Jeppesen CM; crew notified with date, location, and evaluator
l4_steps.kpi: Simulator slot secured within 10 business days of recency lapse identified; no-show rate <3%
l4_steps.pain_point: Simulator capacity at airline training centres is shared with initial qualification training; short-notice recency check bookings are frequently bumped, extending grounding duration and creating crew shortage risk on high-frequency routes

l4_steps.name: Cross-reference certificates with FAA IACRA Airmen Inquiry
l4_steps.system: FAA IACRA (Integrated Airman Certification and Rating Application)
l4_steps.input: Crew qualification records from Jeppesen CM; FAA certificate numbers
l4_steps.output: IACRA cross-reference report confirming or flagging discrepancies in ATP, type rating, and medical certificate status
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of active crew cross-referenced monthly; discrepancy detection rate >95% vs. manual audit
l4_steps.pain_point: IACRA Airmen Inquiry public API does not expose enforcement action flags or certificate surrender status in real time; airlines must rely on PRIA (Pilot Records Improvement Act) database for hiring but have no automated ongoing pull for current employees

l4_steps.name: Verify Special Issuance conditions and SODA exemptions
l4_steps.input: IACRA cross-reference report; crew medical history flags; FAA SI letter on file
l4_steps.output: SI compliance verification: conditions met, or deviation requiring FAA Regional Flight Surgeon follow-up identified
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of crew with active SI conditions reviewed quarterly; zero SI deadline breaches
l4_steps.pain_point: Special Issuance conditions (e.g., post-cardiac event, CPAP therapy compliance) carry individual FAA-imposed timelines and monitoring requirements; tracking these in a generic crew management system without structured SI workflow fields leads to missed review deadlines

l4_steps.name: Update crew qualification matrix with verified certifications
l4_steps.input: IACRA cross-reference report; SI compliance verification; proficiency check results
l4_steps.output: Fully updated crew qualification matrix; scheduling system reflects current authorised aircraft types and positions
l4_steps.kpi: Qualification matrix updated within 4 hours of verification completion; scheduling system sync lag <1 hour
l4_steps.pain_point: Qualification matrix updates in Jeppesen CM do not automatically propagate to codeshare partner crew systems, requiring manual data exchange for any interline or wet-lease arrangements

l4_steps.name: Flag non-compliant crew and initiate grounding hold
l4_steps.input: Compliance failure flag from certification validation or IACRA cross-reference
l4_steps.output: Grounding hold applied in Jeppesen CM; crew member status set to NOT QUALIFIED; Chief Pilot and Crew Scheduling notified
l4_steps.kpi: Grounding hold applied within 2 hours of compliance failure detection; zero non-compliant crew departing on scheduled flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Grounding holds in Jeppesen CM do not automatically trigger crew pay adjustment workflow in SAP SuccessFactors; manual payroll correction required for grounded crew on paid leave status, creating HR disputes

l4_steps.name: Remove crew from active schedule and source replacement
l4_steps.input: Grounding hold notification; affected flight assignments; available reserve crew list
l4_steps.output: Affected flights reassigned or covered by reserve crew; operational disruption minimised
l4_steps.kpi: Replacement crew sourced within 3 hours of grounding notification; schedule disruption rate <1% attributable to certification grounding
l4_steps.pain_point: Reserve crew pools sized for weather/irregular operations events — simultaneous grounding of multiple crew for certification non-compliance (e.g., post-audit sweep) can exhaust reserve capacity on thin-coverage focus city stations

l4_steps.name: Track remediation progress and certification renewal
l4_steps.input: Grounding hold record; crew member self-reported remediation milestones; AME/simulator confirmations
l4_steps.output: Remediation tracking log with milestone dates; estimated return-to-duty date communicated to Crew Scheduling
l4_steps.kpi: Average grounding duration <14 days for medical renewal cases; <7 days for recency cases
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen CM has no structured remediation workflow module; compliance analysts track grounding cases in spreadsheets outside the system, creating audit trail gaps and no automated escalation if remediation stalls beyond SLA

l4_steps.name: Restore crew to active status and release scheduling block
l4_steps.input: Confirmed certification compliance from remediation tracking; updated qualification matrix
l4_steps.output: Grounding hold lifted; crew status restored to QUALIFIED; crew available for scheduling from next bid period or immediate standby
l4_steps.kpi: Reinstatement processing time <2 hours after compliance confirmed; zero scheduling errors on reinstatement day
l4_steps.pain_point: Reinstatement requires manual dual-approval (Crew Compliance Manager + Chief Pilot) with no digital workflow; paper sign-off process creates delays when approvers are on-duty in different time zones

l4_steps.name: Generate certification compliance dashboard in Tableau
l4_steps.input: Qualification matrix export from Jeppesen CM; grounding event log; remediation tracking data
l4_steps.output: Live certification compliance dashboard showing fleet-wide expiry profile, grounding incidents, and trend lines by certificate type
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard refresh latency <4 hours; fleet-wide certification compliance rate KPI target ≥99.0%
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau dashboard relies on manual Jeppesen CM data exports rather than live API feed; stale data during audits or regulatory inspections undermines credibility with FAA Principal Operations Inspector (POI)

l4_steps.name: Export FAA regulatory audit package and file deviations
l4_steps.input: Certification compliance dashboard; grounding and reinstatement event log; corrective action records
l4_steps.output: Regulatory audit package (PDF + CSV) ready for FAA POI review; deviation reports filed via ASAP program if compliance threshold breached
l4_steps.kpi: Audit package prepared within 24 hours of FAA request; zero open compliance findings older than 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Aviation Safety Action Program (ASAP) event reporting for certification deviations is voluntary and narrative-based; without structured data capture in Jeppesen CM, root cause trending across deviation events requires labour-intensive manual analysis

l4_steps.name: Compute reserve coverage requirements by base
l4_steps.input: Historical sick-call rates, IROPS frequency data, scheduled pairing volume
l4_steps.output: Reserve pool size targets by base, fleet type, and crew position
l4_steps.kpi: Reserve callout success rate ≥95% within 60 min; reserve buffer ≥110% of forecast open duties
l4_steps.pain_point: Historical sick-call rates underestimate demand during seasonal IROPS surges; model recalibration requires manual analyst intervention — no auto-refresh in Jeppesen planning module

l4_steps.name: Allocate reserve positions per CBA obligations
l4_steps.input: Reserve coverage targets, collective bargaining agreement (CBA) reserve-day ratios
l4_steps.output: Reserve allocation roster by base, fleet, and crew position (Captain / FO / FA)
l4_steps.kpi: CBA compliance rate 100%; reserve allocation published ≥72 hours before period start
l4_steps.pain_point: CBA restrictions on reserve obligation days limit scheduling flexibility; union grievances filed when allocation violates contractual reserve windows or exceeds maximum days-on-call

l4_steps.name: Validate reserve pool adequacy vs. coverage model
l4_steps.input: Reserve allocation roster, demand forecast, known vacation/training commitments
l4_steps.output: Approved reserve pool plan or escalation to Director of Crew Scheduling
l4_steps.kpi: Reserve pool adequacy score ≥90% across all bases; gap closure within 48 hours of identification
l4_steps.pain_point: Coverage model accuracy degrades during network-wide weather events; no predictive depletion forecast natively in Jeppesen — requires manual scenario modelling in spreadsheets

l4_steps.name: Detect open crew position from absence or IROPS
l4_steps.input: Real-time crew absence notification (sick call, no-show), flight disruption alert from NOC
l4_steps.output: Open duty record with flight ID, departure time, required crew position, and base
l4_steps.kpi: Open duty detection latency ≤10 min from absence notification; 100% of open duties logged before T-90 min departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Sick-call surges during IROPS overwhelm scheduler capacity; legacy Jeppesen alert queues do not auto-triage by urgency, forcing manual prioritisation under time pressure

l4_steps.name: Query available reserve crew by qualification match
l4_steps.input: Open duty requirements (base, fleet type, position), current reserve availability roster
l4_steps.output: Ranked shortlist of available reserves sorted by CBA callout obligation (earliest callout first)
l4_steps.kpi: Query response time ≤2 min; shortlist generated for 100% of open duties before callout initiation
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen does not automatically apply all CBA tie-breaker rules in the sort order; schedulers manually override, introducing errors and exposing airline to union grievances

l4_steps.name: Initiate automated reserve callout sequence
l4_steps.input: Ranked reserve shortlist, open duty details (flight, departure, report time)
l4_steps.output: Callout attempt log; crew acceptance or declination response captured
l4_steps.kpi: Reserve answer rate ≥85% within 30 min of first callout; callout-to-assignment cycle ≤45 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew unreachable on personal phones during off-duty sleep periods; no regulatory mandate requiring reserve crew to answer within a defined window in all jurisdictions, creating unpredictable response latency

l4_steps.name: Escalate to secondary reserve or open-time board
l4_steps.input: Failed callout log, remaining eligible reserve list, CBA open-time posting rules
l4_steps.output: Secondary callout initiated or duty posted to open-time voluntary pickup board
l4_steps.kpi: Secondary escalation resolution ≤45 min; open-time fill rate ≥70% within 60 min of posting
l4_steps.pain_point: Reserve pool exhaustion during cascading IROPS requires manager authorisation to use voluntary overtime; CBA overtime budgets frequently exhausted mid-event, forcing flight cancellations

l4_steps.name: Validate FAR Part 117 rest requirements
l4_steps.input: Reserve crew duty history, callout date/time, proposed report time, cumulative flight duty period
l4_steps.output: Legality check result (legal / illegal); disqualification flag with violation code if illegal
l4_steps.kpi: Legality check completion ≤1 min per crew member; 0 illegal pairings assigned per month
l4_steps.pain_point: Rest period calculations for reserve crews differ from lineholder rules under FAR 117; system may not correctly flag cumulative fatigue across split reserve periods (FAR 117.25), requiring manual secondary checks

l4_steps.name: Verify aircraft type currency and recency
l4_steps.input: Reserve crew qualification record, assigned aircraft type, last operating date, training records feed from LMS
l4_steps.output: Currency and recency confirmation or disqualification flag with expiry date
l4_steps.kpi: Zero misassignment events due to lapsed currency; qualification check latency ≤1 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Currency lapses during extended reserve periods not proactively surfaced; recency tracking in Jeppesen relies on accurate and timely training record feeds from the LMS — data latency causes stale qualification status

l4_steps.name: Confirm route-specific qualifications (ETOPS/special airports)
l4_steps.input: Assigned flight route, special qualification requirements (ETOPS, high-altitude, noise-sensitive airports), crew qualification record
l4_steps.output: Route qualification confirmed or reassignment required with reason code
l4_steps.kpi: Zero ETOPS qualification violations; 100% route compliance rate
l4_steps.pain_point: ETOPS qualification status not always current in crew tracking system due to training record feed delays; manual cross-check with training department adds 10–15 min to assignment cycle

l4_steps.name: Assign reserve crew to open duty in system
l4_steps.input: Validated crew record, open duty ID, legality and qualification confirmation
l4_steps.output: Confirmed crew assignment; updated roster visible to crew, airport ops, and dispatch
l4_steps.kpi: Assignment completion ≤5 min from legality confirmation; roster visibility propagated to all systems ≤2 min post-assignment
l4_steps.pain_point: Simultaneous assignment attempts by multiple schedulers during IROPS cause optimistic locking conflicts in Jeppesen; failed writes require manual retry, adding delay during time-critical coverage windows

l4_steps.name: Notify reserve crew via mobile push notification
l4_steps.input: Confirmed assignment record (flight, report time, gate, hotel/transport if applicable)
l4_steps.output: Push notification delivered to crew device; crew digital acknowledgment captured
l4_steps.kpi: Notification delivery ≤2 min of assignment; crew acknowledgment receipt rate ≥92% within 15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Notification failures when crew device is offline or app version is outdated; no guaranteed delivery SLA from mobile OS push services (APNs/FCM) — silent failures require fallback SMS or phone call

l4_steps.name: Brief crew on flight plan, NOTAMs, and special conditions
l4_steps.input: Flight plan package, NOTAM briefing pack, weather advisory, airport operational notices
l4_steps.output: Crew briefed and sign-off recorded; briefing record logged with timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: Briefing completion ≥30 min prior to departure for 100% of reserve activations; zero regulatory briefing compliance failures
l4_steps.pain_point: Reserve crew unfamiliar with last-minute route changes or unfamiliar destination airports; time pressure in IROPS degrades briefing thoroughness, increasing risk of operating with incomplete situational awareness

l4_steps.name: Monitor reserve pool utilization in real time
l4_steps.input: Live reserve assignment data, remaining available reserves by base and fleet type
l4_steps.output: Reserve utilization dashboard; automated alert triggered at depletion threshold breach
l4_steps.kpi: Alert triggered when available reserves ≤20% of pool; dashboard refresh interval ≤5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Dashboard refresh latency during high-volume IROPS masks true pool depletion until critically low; Jeppesen base module lacks predictive depletion forecast — operational awareness depends on manual monitoring

l4_steps.name: Post voluntary extension offer to open-time board
l4_steps.system: IBS Software iCrew (open-time posting) + Jeppesen Crew Management
l4_steps.input: Pool depletion alert, CBA voluntary overtime eligibility rules, remaining open duties
l4_steps.output: Voluntary extension offers posted and crew responses captured; coverage gap delta updated
l4_steps.kpi: Voluntary coverage fill rate ≥70% within 60 min of posting; overtime authorisation cycle ≤15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: CBA limits on forced extensions restrict scheduler options during IROPS; voluntary overtime budget frequently exhausted during prolonged disruptions, leaving residual open duties uncovered

l4_steps.name: Escalate unresolved open duties to NOC for cancellation decision
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) + NOC Operations Board
l4_steps.input: Unresolved open duty list, remaining reserve pool status, downstream flight impact assessment
l4_steps.output: NOC decision: cancel flight, sub-fleet, or continue with substitution plan; cancellation record logged
l4_steps.kpi: Escalation-to-decision cycle ≤30 min; cancellation decision communicated to all stakeholders ≤10 min post-decision
l4_steps.pain_point: NOC cancellation decisions during cascading IROPS require simultaneous crew, aircraft, and gate inputs — single-system views in SITA AMS delay decision quality; lack of integrated crew-aircraft-gate dashboard extends resolution time

l4_steps.name: Update FTL and fatigue counters post-reserve duty
l4_steps.input: Completed duty log, actual block hours, actual duty period start/end times
l4_steps.output: Updated crew flight time limitation (FTL) records, cumulative fatigue counters, rest period start
l4_steps.kpi: FTL record update SLA ≤4 hours post-duty completion; 100% record accuracy verified by audit
l4_steps.pain_point: Late inbound flight data delays FTL record updates; accumulated entry errors trigger false legality alerts in the next scheduling cycle, blocking legal crew assignments and requiring manual override

l4_steps.name: Analyse reserve utilisation metrics for planning feedback
l4_steps.input: Reserve duty assignment history, callout response logs, pool depletion events, IROPS correlation data
l4_steps.output: Monthly reserve utilisation report with callout success trends and pool size recommendations
l4_steps.kpi: Monthly report delivered within 5 business days of period close; callout success rate trend ≥95%; report consumed in next planning cycle within 30 days
